2. ENI operating margin expanded nearly 10 percentage points YoY to 40.3%, driven by a 44% increase in management fees and strong operating leverage.
3. ENI diluted EPS grew 108% YoY to $1.33, reflecting significant growth in recurring management fee profit.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. The blended fee rate has declined year-over-year due to the mix shift towards lower-fee Enhanced strategies, though management expects stabilization.
2. Operating expenses increased 19% YoY due to investments in technology and higher compensation, though revenue growth significantly outpaced this increase.
3. The company noted operating against a 'challenging geopolitical and macroeconomic backdrop,' which creates underlying market risk despite strong performance.
rows.key_quote: We realized $4.3 billion of positive net client cash flows... a 9% annualized organic growth rate, driven by Enhanced and Extension strategies.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Massive Aluminum Performance: Record revenue (INR 21,158 crores, +45% YoY) and EBITDA (INR 10,499 crores, +134% YoY) driven by record production (632 kt), higher prices, and EBITDA per ton expanding to $1,804.
2. Strong Demerged Vedanta Ltd. Results: EBITDA nearly doubled (+98% YoY) with margin expanding 985 bps to 57%, propelled by Zinc India achieving a record-low cost of production of $851/t.
3. Successful Deleveraging & Refinancing: Group deleveraged by $1.1 billion in Q1, Vedanta Ltd's net debt/EBITDA reached a low of 0.3x, and refinancing will save over INR 1,000 crores in annual interest costs.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Operational Issues in Specific Units: Vedanta Power's performance was impacted by an incident at the Sakti unit, while Aluminum's alumina production fell 6% QoQ due to stabilization issues.
2. Production Declines in Oil & Gas: The business saw revenue fall 3% QoQ due to natural reservoir decline, with gross production at 77,700 boepd, highlighting the need for decline management.
3. Geopolitical Impact on Copper International: Rod sales in the Copper International business fell 51% YoY due to supply chain disruptions in the Middle East.
rows.key_quote: EBITDA nearly doubled, rising by 98% Y-o-Y to highest level... with a margin of 57%, up 985 basis points Y-o-Y.

rows.positive_highlights: Record trailing 12-month results: Adjusted EPS of $6.96 and Adjusted EBITDA of $1.7B represent all-time highs. Strategic capital build: Trading capital increased from $2.0B to $3.4B YoY, enhanced by a $500M term loan, to fund growth. Robust profitability and execution: Generated $437M in adjusted EBITDA at a 61% margin, with management noting qualitative improvements that drove outperformance.
rows.negative_highlights: Rising compensation costs: Cash compensation ratio has risen to 23% YTD, guided as a near-term norm due to aggressive talent acquisition. Increased brokerage & transaction costs: The line item saw a 'bigger jump' driven by business mix, creating a potential drag on net revenue. Reliance on market environment: Management acknowledged that the favorable operating environment of high volumes and volatility is a 'primary determinant' of performance.
rows.key_quote: it's also notable... that we've improved qualitatively. If you repeated this environment two years ago... then we wouldn't have done as well.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Achieved the strongest quarterly organic growth in three years at 9%, driven by broad-based performance and a 15% rebound in the OEM business. 2. Non-GAAP EPS grew 18% YoY, and non-GAAP operating margin expanded 142 bps to 22.6%, exceeding the high end of guidance even after excluding a tariff refund benefit. 3. Recent acquisitions like Biolife are outperforming, with its full-year revenue forecast raised to ~$23 million from an original $18-20 million.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Renal Therapies sales declined 2% due to a product recall, though the issue has been resolved and sales would have grown ~10% otherwise. 2. Ongoing tariff uncertainty remains a headwind, with a projected $16 million impact for the full year, contributing to a wider-than-usual Q3 guidance range. 3. Procedural Solutions sales declined 12% on a reported basis, a headwind entirely attributable to the prior divestiture of the DualCap product line.
rows.key_quote: The beat was broad-based... when our index-style portfolio is all hitting, you get these types of growth rates.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong US Market: Higher activity, constrained imports, and rising OCTG pricing are driving strong asset utilization and bookings.
Robust Profitability and Cash Flow: Despite lower volumes, delivered a strong 21.4% group EBITDA margin and ended with a net cash position of $183 million.
Major Offshore Contract Wins: Secured the largest line pipe contract in company history for ExxonMobil Guyana, underpinning future growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
Middle East Disruptions: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz caused shipment delays, leading to sequentially lower volumes and revenue in Q2.
Increased Near-Term Costs: Incurring additional freight, insurance, and storage costs due to Middle East disruptions, which will negatively impact Q3 EBITDA/ton.
Lowered Mine Segment Guidance: Full-year guidance for the Mine & Forest segment was reduced to 5-5.5 million tonnes, reflecting softer demand due to higher freight costs.
rows.key_quote: Despite sequentially lower volumes in our international business, Tubes profitability remained highly robust at USD 722 per ton, similar to the level in Q1.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised full-year 2026 EPS guidance to $6.25-$6.55, an increase of $0.10 at the midpoint, citing strong business performance and confidence.
2. Contracted an additional 6 GW of large customer load, bringing the total pipeline to 69 GW through 2030, reinforcing a massive long-term growth runway.
3. Proactively secured 13 GW of gas turbine capacity for deployment through 2031 and has options for an additional 10 GW, de-risking generation needs for future load.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Q2 operating EPS of $1.36 declined from $1.43 in the prior year, primarily due to the 2025 transmission minority interest sale and timing of tax items.
2. The proposed authorized ROE in an Oklahoma rate case settlement decreased slightly from 9.5% to 9.375%.
3. Earnings were partially offset by increased O&M spending to enhance system reliability.
rows.key_quote: Just during the second quarter, AEP contracted an additional six gigawatts of load, primarily driven by fully executed LOAs in Texas.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Profitability: Achieved highest-ever quarterly net profit of PLN 1.1 billion and a Return on Tangible Equity of nearly 22%.
2. Strong Volume Growth: Loans grew 13% YoY and deposits grew 21% YoY, outpacing the market. Mortgage sales were particularly strong, up 74% YoY in H1.
3. Improved Full-Year Guidance: Raised 2026 revenue guidance to exceed 2025 levels and lowered cost of risk guidance to ~55 basis points due to strong credit quality.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Margin Compression: Net Interest Margin (NIM) declined to 3.47% in Q2, reflecting the lower interest rate environment, though it is expected to stabilize.
2. Corporate Lending Spreads: Management acknowledged that spreads in the corporate lending segment have compressed, though they see signs of bottoming out.
3. Increased Operating Costs: Underlying costs rose 8% quarter-on-quarter, driven by strategic investments in IT, marketing, and seasonal factors.
rows.key_quote: NII rose by around 3% quarter-on-quarter, supported by loan growth and disciplined deposit pricing.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Risk Management (Gallagher Bassett) organic growth of 12% and EBITAC margin expansion of 140 bps.
2. Strong progress on AssuredPartners integration with synergy targets reaffirmed ($160M by YE26, $325M by early 2028).
3. Continued underlying margin expansion in Brokerage (50 bps) driven by productivity and quality efforts.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant headwind from softening property insurance pricing, with renewal premiums down 10% in the quarter.
2. Slower pace of tuck-in M&A, running at about 80% of the historical average deal count.
3. U.S. P&C Benefits growth has been lagging other areas, though management believes its current 3-4% rate is solid.
rows.key_quote: Only about 1 point of our organic growth is tied to rates. The bigger drivers continue to be new business, strong retention, and exposure growth.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong top-line growth: Revenue grew 32% to $1.3B, driven by 31% membership growth.
Margin expansion: Adjusted MBR improved 40bps YoY to 86.3%, the lowest as a public company, leading to 60bps of adjusted EBITDA margin expansion.
Raised full-year guidance: Raised revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance due to strong first-half performance and increased confidence in full-year objectives.
rows.negative_highlights:
Planned Q3 investments to increase MBR and SG&A: Management is guiding for a seasonally higher MBR and SG&A in Q3 due to investments in clinical operations, AI, and new market preparations.
Unfavorable Prior Year Development (PYD): Recorded approximately $6.5M of unfavorable PYD in the quarter, which management framed as a prudent choice to bolster reserves.
Higher acuity new member mix: An intentional focus on C-SNP and D-SNP eligible members elevates the initial MBR for the new member cohort.
rows.key_quote: Our AVA AI model now accurately predicts the 10% of members accounting for nearly 70% of hospital admissions over the next 30 days.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record recruiting pipeline and strong recruited assets of $25 billion, the strongest quarter in nearly two years (ex-large institutional deals).
2. Achieved record adjusted EPS of $5.84 and lowered the full-year Core G&A outlook to $2.14B-$2.165B due to greater efficiency.
3. Commonwealth integration is on track for Q4, with an increased run-rate EBITDA estimate of ~$435 million.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Organic net new assets of $23B represented a 4% annualized growth rate, which is below the company's mid-to-high single-digit target range.
2. The payout rate is expected to increase by approximately 80 basis points in Q3 due to seasonality and advisory pricing reductions.
3. Transaction revenue is forecasted to decline by approximately $5 million in Q3 after reaching record levels in Q2.
rows.key_quote: recruited assets improved to $25 billion... this was our strongest quarter of recruiting in nearly 2 years.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record Refining Performance: Operating income surged to $4.5 billion (vs. $1.3B YoY) on a structural shift to a higher margin environment, with product cracks now set by less efficient European hydroskimming capacity. 2. Strong Renewables & Ethanol: Renewable Diesel operating income hit $717M (vs. -$79M loss YoY) as D4 RIN values outpaced feedstock costs, while Ethanol benefited from a new ~$0.17/gallon production tax credit. 3. Favorable Feedstock & Export Dynamics: Strong export demand to Latin America and a closed gasoline import arb from Europe boosted capture rates, with management seeing advantaged access to Venezuelan and Canadian heavy crude.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Port Arthur DHT Unit Outage: The Port Arthur DHT unit requires repairs estimated at $250 million, included in updated sustaining CapEx guidance, with the unit expected back online by year-end. 2. RIN Market Risk: Management voiced concern that the RFS system could become 'unfeasible' as the RIN bank is depleted, creating significant policy and price uncertainty, despite being well-positioned. 3. Conservative Cash Deployment: The company is holding cash at $7.9 billion, well above its $4-5 billion target, to manage volatility, thus deferring the potential for accelerated share buybacks.
rows.key_quote: As supply-and-demand balances have tightened, refinery crack spreads are now really being set by hydroskimming margins in Northwest Europe.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong IAS segment growth: Revenue grew 23% Y/Y, driven by a 40% increase in the business solutions unit. 2. Improved group profitability: Adjusted EBIT increased 18% to €224 million with the margin expanding to 7.7%, aided by efficiency savings. 3. Strategic automation progress: Acquired 70% of Smart Innovation NV to develop autonomous pallet trucks and successfully deployed AI in logistics.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Lowered full-year guidance: Midpoints for revenue and EBIT were reduced due to a weaker outlook for the large ITS segment, citing macro conditions. 2. Weak order intake: Group orders declined 20% Y/Y against a tough comparison, also impacted by Q1 pre-watch effects in the ITS segment. 3. ITS margin pressure: The Industrial Trucks segment's gross margin declined over 100 bps sequentially from Q1 and was also impacted by negative FX.
rows.key_quote: IAS revenue increased by 23% year-over-year due to higher order intake... and driven by a 40% growth in business solutions.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. U.S. Senior Housing Operating Portfolio (SHOP) delivered 18% NOI growth and 360 basis points of occupancy growth year-over-year. 
2. Full-year normalized FFO guidance was raised to $3.85-$3.90 per share (8-10% growth), driven by accretive investments. 
3. Full-year investment guidance was increased from $3.0 billion to $4.5 billion, focusing on high-return senior housing acquisitions.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. The research portfolio experienced occupancy loss from tenant non-renewals, creating a $900,000 negative year-over-year impact. 
2. The FFO guidance increase was partially offset by a $0.01 per share headwind from higher interest rates. 
3. New development is not currently viable, with management noting rents need to be 25-40% higher for projects to be economical.
rows.key_quote: The community is currently 90% or more occupied delivered 25% NOI growth.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong AMVUTTRA uptake: AMVUTTRA revenue exceeded $1 billion in the quarter, driving total product revenue growth of 74% YoY.
2. Favorable competitive landscape: A key competitor's (eplontersen) trial failed and the generic entry for tafamidis was delayed to 2031.
3. Robust first-line growth: First-line patient starts now account for ~80% of category growth, indicating a strong, durable demand base.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Lowered revenue guidance: Full-year product revenue guidance was reduced by $200M at the midpoint, signaling a near-term growth reset.
2. Normalization of second-line demand: The initial surge of patients switching to AMVUTTRA (pent-up demand) has moderated to a lower sustainable rate.
3. Deteriorated gross margin: Gross margin declined 4 percentage points YoY to 75% due to higher royalty payments to Sanofi.
rows.key_quote: early second-line demand growth in 2025 benefited significantly from pent-up demand for a new therapy that has since normalized.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Announced accretive acquisition of stoba Group, expected to add $80M in revenue and $25M in EBITDA, expanding into off-highway and aerospace markets.
2. Reported strong Q2 results with revenue up 5.6% to $940M and adjusted EPS up 20.5% to $1.53, benefiting from an unexpected $11M tariff refund contribution to earnings.
3. Increased full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance to $210M-$250M and returned $53M to shareholders in Q2 via buybacks and dividends.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Lowered full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 13.5%-14.1%, citing dilutive impacts from FX, tariff pass-throughs, and product mix.
2. Quarterly results were impacted by a $9M headwind from higher incentive compensation costs, partially offsetting operational gains.
3. Management noted regional weakness in the China light vehicle market, which was down in the mid-teens.
rows.key_quote: Net tariff expense and anticipated refunds were an $11 million contribution to earnings in the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Origination Activity: Advanced $154 million in Q2 and $315 million year-to-date, a meaningful increase over last year. 2. Progress on Stage Loan Resolution: Stage 3 loan balances declined by over 51% since year-end, signaling progress on resolving problem assets. 3. Stable Distributable Income: Generated $14.6 million ($0.18/share), which management believes is stable and supports the monthly dividend.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Significant Drop in Net Income: Net income fell to $7.8 million from $12.4 million in the prior period due to increased expected credit losses (ECLs). 2. Elevated Credit Loss Provisions: Took higher provisions on a Vancouver retail portfolio and Victoria assets, impacting current earnings as part of exit strategies. 3. High Payout Ratio: Distributable income payout ratio was high at 97.7%, leaving little room for redeployment or unforeseen issues.
rows.key_quote: Net income before expected credit losses remained stable at $14.5 million, providing a useful view of the underlying earnings capacity as stage loan resolutions progress.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong well outperformance continued, with NE BC Montney wells up 28% and Alberta Deep Basin wells up 14% over prior 5-year averages. 2. Q2 OpEx decreased 10% YoY to $4.59/BOE, demonstrating successful cost control. 3. Expanded market access with a long-term agreement to increase propane/butane exports by ~55% through the Altagas Reef terminal, improving realized margins.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Low Q2 natural gas prices forced the company to defer activity, shut in production, and inject more gas into storage. 2. Q2 production of 594,000 BOE/d was marginally below the guidance range of 595k-605k BOE/d. 3. A one-year pause was announced for the Phase 2 BC Montney infrastructure project, delaying a major component of long-term growth.
rows.key_quote: Production was below guidance... as we injected more nat gas into storage and deferred activity in response to low Q2 natural gas prices.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong High-Value Segment Performance: The high-value segment drove results, with volumes up 3.5% in H1 and its share of sales increasing to 82%.
2. Stable Profitability Amidst Headwinds: Adjusted EBIT margin was maintained at 16% as efficiency gains (EUR 81M) and positive price/mix (+2.5%) offset negative external impacts.
3. Robust Net Profit Growth: Net profit rose 13% year-on-year to EUR 299 million, benefiting from lower financial expenses and a one-off gain.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Worsening Macro Environment: Management confirmed a deteriorating scenario due to geopolitical tensions, leading to a downward revision of the 2026 car tire market demand outlook.
2. Raw Material Headwind in H2: A positive EUR 32M raw material impact in H1 is expected to reverse to a negative EUR 70M impact in H2.
3. Weakness in Standard Segment: Volumes in the standard segment declined by 11% in Q2 as the company strategically reduced exposure in a highly competitive market.
rows.key_quote: organic growth of 2.5% driven by stronger high-value, accounting now for 82% of group sales and price/mix improvement.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. AI-led innovation strategy is a "game changer," driving double-digit pipeline growth and attracting new customers previously hesitant to leave vendor support.
2. Adjusted revenue (ex-PeopleSoft) grew 10% YoY, and annualized recurring revenue (ex-PeopleSoft) grew 8.1%, indicating strong underlying business acceleration.
3. Confidently reiterated full-year 'Rule of 20' guidance, supported by strong demand signals including a 30% pipe close rate and double-digit new bookings growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Non-GAAP EPS declined to $0.06 from $0.08 in the prior year, reflecting higher investments in sales and marketing for new AI offerings.
2. Billings declined 8.8% year-over-year, attributed to renewal timing, creating noise around near-term growth momentum.
3. Sales and Marketing expense as a percentage of revenue increased to 37.6% (non-GAAP) from 35.5% YoY, pressuring operating margins in the near term.
rows.key_quote: The fact that we are now giving customers a path...has been a game changer...in terms of overall demand generation.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong revenue growth in non-RV markets: Marine revenue grew 22% and Powersports revenue grew 28%, validating the company's diversification strategy.
2. Significant organic growth and content gains: Achieved 7% organic revenue growth and increased Marine content per unit by 22%, indicating market share wins.
3. Proactive capital allocation and strategy: Repurchased $91 million of shares and is preparing for a strategic merger with LCI Industries.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Core RV market weakness: RV revenue fell 15% due to a 16% decline in industry wholesale shipments, which dragged down overall performance.
2. Lowered full-year guidance: Reduced its 2026 outlook for RV wholesale shipments and consequently lowered its operating cash flow forecast.
3. Margin pressure: Adjusted operating margin contracted by 80 basis points YoY, with guidance for a potential additional 20 bps headwind in the second half.
rows.key_quote: We estimate the year-over-year change in our revenue was comprised of 7% organic growth, 1% acquisition growth and negative 9% industry.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Exceptional Revenue Growth & Profitability: Revenue grew 61% YoY to $805M, marking the eighth straight quarter of over 60% growth. Adjusted EBITDA margin hit 43% and GAAP diluted EPS more than doubled to $1.25.
2. Strong Ad Business Momentum: Ad revenue grew 64%, driven by a 70% YoY increase in active advertisers and 100%+ growth in conversion volume. The automated 'Reddit Max' ad platform saw revenue grow over 150% from Q1.
3. Improving User Quality: Despite search headwinds, new app user retention improved 50% YoY on a relative basis, a key indicator that product improvements are successfully creating more valuable, direct users.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. User Growth Headwinds from Search: Overall DAU growth was hampered by volatile search referral traffic, leading to a slight sequential decline in U.S. DAUs and raising analyst concerns about external dependencies.
2. Inefficient Paid Marketing: Management stated that user acquisition spending "needs stronger attention to improve returns," acknowledging that better user retention is required to justify higher marketing investment.
3. Data Licensing Uncertainty: Management offered no clear visibility on the renewal of major data licensing deals, stating the "range of outcomes is wide," creating uncertainty around a key revenue stream.
rows.key_quote: We turned intent into outcomes with conversion volume growing over 100% and click volume growing over 30% year-over-year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1) Strong Preneed Sales Growth: Comparable preneed cemetery sales production grew 8% ($29.7M) and preneed funeral sales production grew 7% ($20M).
2) Robust Operating Cash Flow: Adjusted operating cash flow increased 42% YoY to $239M, leading to a $50M increase in full-year cash flow guidance.
3) Improving Funeral Volume Trend: Core funeral volume decline of 1.7% was better than expected, with the trend moderating through the quarter and showing slight growth in June.
rows.negative_highlights:
1) Funeral Gross Margin Decline: Funeral gross margin fell 130 basis points to 18.5% due to slow revenue growth and higher recognized watching compensation.
2) Funeral Volume Decline: Comparable core funeral volume declined 1.7% for the quarter, continuing to be a headwind.
3) GAAP Expense Recognition Headwinds: A shift to more insurance-funded preneed contracts resulted in higher upfront recognition of watching compensation, negatively impacting reported funeral margins.
rows.key_quote: Comparable preneed cemetery sales production grew by 8% and comparable preneed funeral sales production grew by 7% for the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Drilling Activity & Pricing: Rig activity recovered faster than expected, with new contract pricing up 10-15% vs Q1, driven by demand from private E&Ps.
2. Completions Market Tightening: The market for natural gas-powered frac equipment is "effectively fully utilized," leading to meaningful pricing improvements and a strong outlook for further recovery.
3. Drilling Products Record Revenue: Segment achieved its highest quarterly revenue since the Ulterra acquisition despite geopolitical disruptions in the Middle East.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Working Capital Use: Significant use of cash in Q2 due to the rapid ramp-up in activity and a one-time ERP system transition, impacting free cash flow.
2. Colombia Business Exit: Took a $21 million non-cash charge to exit the Contract Drilling business in Colombia due to aging assets and an unfavorable political environment.
3. Middle East Disruption: The Drilling Products segment faced conflict-related disruptions in logistics and activity levels in its largest international region.
rows.key_quote: Private E&Ps have responded more quickly to higher oil prices and are now driving a meaningful increase in drilling activity.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. P&C division delivered an exceptionally strong combined ratio of 79.5% for the quarter, driven by benign catastrophe activity and excellent underlying attritional performance. 2. Strong growth in targeted areas, with Alternative Solutions premiums up over 70% YTD and Specialty lines up 19.8% in recent renewals. 3. Balance sheet strengthened, with solvency ratio increasing to 220% and progress made on deleveraging, while also building prudential buffers.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Life & Health insurance service result was reduced to €49 million for the quarter due to a negative one-off arbitration impact of €64 million. 2. P&C reinsurance market is seeing increased competition, particularly in property cat where U.S. prices decreased around 20% in recent renewals. 3. P&C gross written premium was negatively impacted by revisions to prior year estimates from cedents and adverse foreign exchange effects.
rows.key_quote: P&C continued its strong performance...supported by a relatively benign cat activity and an excellent attritional loss ratio, demonstrating the quality of our portfolio.

rows.positive_highlights: Net profit attributable to shareholders increased 157% to EUR 78 million; The valuation of the concession portfolio grew 16% year-over-year to EUR 4.601 billion; Operating cash flow increased 18% on a comparable basis to EUR 631 million.
rows.negative_highlights: Consolidated net debt increased by EUR 429 million during the first half to EUR 6.788 billion; The Engineering and Infrastructure division's EBITDA grew 4% on 10% revenue growth, indicating margin compression; Working capital saw a cash outflow due to significant costs from bidding on large U.S. infrastructure projects.
rows.key_quote: Concessions continue to account for the vast majority of EBITDA, accounting for more than 91% of the total.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Exceptional Operational Performance: Achieved record refinery utilization of 102% in a high-margin period and record production in Brazil Upstream. The Pennsylvania Petrochemicals Complex also delivered its best performance to date.
2. Strong Integrated Gas & Trading Results: Successfully offset lost LNG volumes from Qatar with strong performance from its global portfolio (LNG Canada, Nigeria, Trinidad) and significant value capture from LNG trading and optimization activities.
3. Strategic Progress: Advanced its cost-cutting program ($700M delivered in 2026), progressed the value-accretive ARC Resources acquisition, and continued portfolio high-grading, strengthening long-term free cash flow generation.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Middle East Disruptions: Ongoing hostilities caused loss of LNG volumes from Qatar and physical damage to one train at the Pearl GTL facility, which is not expected back online until Q1 2027.
2. Anticipated Q3 Headwinds: Management flagged potential softening, including weakening chemical spreads, more planned refinery turnarounds, and the base oil supply for the lubricants business being challenged by the Pearl GTL outage.
3. Underperforming Low-Carbon Capital: A portion of capital in the low-carbon business is currently unproductive as assets like Holland Hydrogen I are under construction, with returns not expected until 2027 or later.
rows.key_quote: Our refineries achieved a record 102% utilization in a high-margin period.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Brand Momentum: The flagship Steve Madden brand saw a resurgence, with global online searches up 71% and branded wholesale business up 20% in Q2.
2. Significant Margin Expansion: Consolidated gross margin increased 460 bps to 46.5%, driven by higher ASPs, lower promotions, and a reduced mix of private label business.
3. Robust EPS Growth: Diluted EPS more than doubled to $0.44 from $0.20 in the prior-year quarter, significantly beating expectations.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Private Label Weakness: The private label business continues to struggle and is projected to be down mid- to high-teens for the full year.
2. Increased Freight Costs: Management incorporated an additional $0.06 of EPS pressure for the second half due to higher air freight costs to chase best-sellers.
3. International Softness: International comp sales were impacted by conflict in the Middle East, rising only 1% versus a 17% increase in the U.S.
rows.key_quote: Our flagship brand, Steve Madden, was the highlight, continuing to gain momentum as consumers responded enthusiastically to the trend-right assortments.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Ferri and Boot Drive solutions revenue more than doubled sequentially, now representing nearly 30% of total revenue, up from 4% a year ago.
2. Achieved record revenue of $451M, a 127% YoY increase, beating the high end of guidance, with growth across all core markets.
3. Guided Q3 operating margin to expand to 27.5%-28.5% as the new MonTitan enterprise SSD business scales with 5 additional Tier 1 customers in 2H.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Broader consumer markets are challenged; smartphone units are expected to be down 10-15% in 2026 due to rising component costs.
2. NAND supply scarcity is expected to persist until 2028, creating challenges for OEMs and delaying the availability of cost-effective high-capacity QLC SSDs.
3. The transition from PCIe 4 to PCIe 5 in the PC market is proceeding more slowly than anticipated as OEMs prioritize cost-saving measures.
rows.key_quote: Ferri and Boot Drive solutions more than doubled sequentially and represent near 30% of our total revenue, up from 4% a year ago.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. **Transformative Macro Environment**: Global conflicts have taken over 5 million barrels/day of refining capacity offline, creating tight product supply and a "dramatic and constructive" margin environment. 2. **Massive Deleveraging**: Reduced net debt by over $1.4 billion in Q2, dropping net debt-to-cap ratio to 15% from 36% in Q1. 3. **Turnaround Deferrals**: Strategically pushed planned Q4 turnarounds at Toledo and Chalmette to 2027 to maximize uptime during the high-margin period.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. **Operational Incidents**: Suffered an unplanned outage at the Toledo FCC, driving lower throughput, and a loss of containment event at Chalmette that reduced gasoline yield. 2. **High RINs Costs**: Management noted the RFS program still imposes a significant ~$14 per barrel cost, creating a financial headwind. 3. **Upcoming Turnarounds**: The company faces a hydrocracker turnaround at Martinez in Q3 and a crude unit turnaround at Paulsboro in late fall, which will affect operations.
rows.key_quote: The disruptions around the world have resulted in over 5 million barrels of refining capacity offline, a portion of which has suffered physical damage.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Significant EPS guidance raise: Full-year guidance was increased to $0.90-$1.10 from $0.70-$1.00, reflecting strong performance and outlook.
2. Strong operating leverage in Truckload: Earnings more than doubled sequentially on only 2% revenue growth, driven by pricing, productivity, and cost cuts.
3. Rapid market improvement: A 'supply-led' recovery with faster-than-expected capacity attrition has created a driver-constrained market with strong pricing momentum.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Driver market constraints: Driver availability is tight, impacting tractor count, creating recruiting/retention challenges, and putting upward pressure on capacity costs.
2. Loss of a major customer: The company anticipates the loss of a large dedicated customer, which will become more evident in H2 2026 results.
3. Intermodal growth constraints: Drayage has become the primary constraint for Intermodal, forcing the company to decline growth that would require expensive third-party capacity.
rows.key_quote: In truckload, we more than doubled earnings sequentially on 2% revenue growth, possible through executing price, productivity, and cost reductions.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Secured 6 GW of new large load contracts in Q2, including a 3.2 GW, 25-year deal with OpenAI, bringing the total contracted pipeline to over 17 GW.
2. Data center electricity usage grew 55% year-over-year, driving a 22.8% increase in adjusted EPS and a guidance raise to the top of the full-year range.
3. The prospective pipeline for new large load projects remains above 75 GW, with another 8 GW in late-stage negotiations, indicating massive future capital investment opportunities.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Acknowledged ongoing financing needs to support growth, sourcing an additional $700 million in equity during the quarter to maintain credit metrics.
2. Management noted the presence of 'noise all across the country about data centers', indicating potential political or social headwinds that require proactive communication.
3. The massive 17+ GW load buildout creates significant long-term execution risk related to construction timelines and regulatory approvals for new generation.
rows.key_quote: Data center usage was 55% higher compared to the second quarter of 2025, primarily due to accelerating load ramps from our large load customers.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. **Core Business Acceleration & Margin Expansion:** Core revenue (ex-divestiture) grew high-single digits, driven by accelerating 1P ARPU growth. Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin is guided to expand by ~300 basis points.
2. **Strong AI (MAX) Progress and Monetization Path:** The AI agent MAX is showing tangible ROI in beta (e.g., catching a $290k invoice failure) and is rolling out to all fulfillment customers. A clear monetization strategy is planned for late 2026 via paid autonomous agent bundles.
3. **Strategic Divestiture:** Sold the lower-margin, less strategic 3P revenue recovery business to sharpen focus on the core 1P supplier network, which has better cross-watch opportunities and a cleaner business model.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. **Sequential Customer Count Decline:** Core 1P customer count declined by approximately 200 sequentially due to the timing of retail enablement programs. Management expects to be flat-to-slightly positive for the full year.
2. **Muted Reported Revenue Growth:** Overall reported revenue growth was 6% and is guided to ~5% for the full year, dampened by the divestiture of the 3P business which reduces H2 revenue by $10.5M.
3. **Slower Analytics Business:** The analytics business, while receiving a platform refresh, grew only about 1% in the first half of the year, with demand still viewed as more discretionary.
rows.key_quote: Core business grew high single digits, driven by accelerating 1P customer ARPU growth from continued upsell and cross-watch momentum.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Enterprise Growth: Cloud revenues grew 18.1% YoY, now comprising 45% of enterprise service revenues, marking the 16th consecutive quarter of growth for the segment.
2. Accelerating Underlying Profitability: Underlying Group EBITDA after lease growth accelerated to over 9% in Q2, up from 4.5% in Q1, driven by pricing discipline and cost efficiencies.
3. Solid Financial Position: Equity free cash flow was positive by over €1.0 billion in the quarter, supported by a ~€1.0B concession fee reimbursement, with leverage stable at 1.94x.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Wholesale Provider Issues: Management explicitly cited 'deteriorating service quality' from its main wholesale fiber provider (FiberCop), which negatively affected commercial momentum and fixed net additions.
2. MVNO Transition Headwind: A temporary MVNO transition phasing effect reduced H1 revenues by €80 million and EBITDA after lease by €84 million, obscuring stronger underlying performance.
3. Competitive Fixed-Line Market: Fixed ARPU growth is being diluted by the gap between higher back-book pricing and aggressive front-book offers from competitors, notably energy providers.
rows.key_quote: Cloud revenues increased by 18.1% year-on-year and now account for 45% of enterprise service revenues, confirming its role as the main growth engine.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Resort segment strength: Resort RevPAR increased 12% and hotel EBITDA grew 18.5% with 216 bps of margin expansion, driving portfolio performance. 2. San Francisco market recovery: RevPAR grew 16% and hotel EBITDA increased 24.6%, with 250 bps of margin expansion, continuing its strong rebound. 3. Strong cost control: Total expenses rose only 3.8% on 4.8% revenue growth, leading to a 67 bps portfolio-wide margin expansion to 30.6%.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Weakness in specific urban markets: Downtown San Diego RevPAR declined 9.1% and Washington, D.C. RevPAR declined 9.9% due to tough comps and weak government demand. 2. Lagging non-room revenue: Total RevPAR growth of 4.7% trailed RevPAR growth of 6.5%, primarily due to a 20% decline in urban banquet and catering revenue. 3. Overall urban EBITDA decline: Despite strength in SF/LA, total urban hotel EBITDA declined 1% due to weaker convention calendars in other cities.
rows.key_quote: Nearly 3/4 of our RevPAR growth came from rate, a meaningful shift from recent quarters when occupancy gains did most of the work.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Industrial costs improved by over €1.9 billion, driven by manufacturing efficiencies, purchasing savings, and non-repeat of prior year warranty costs. 2. Net revenues grew 13% YoY to €43.5 billion, powered by a 10% increase in shipments. 3. Industrial free cash flow improved by €1 billion YoY to positive €1 billion, and full-year guidance was reaffirmed.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Extremely weak North American profitability, with an AOI margin of only 1.6% despite a 38% YoY increase in shipments. 2. Significant net pricing pressure of negative €456 million, primarily impacting Europe which posted an AOI loss. 3. Total inventory increased 20% YoY to 1.4 million units, reflecting a large build-up at US dealers.
rows.key_quote: The biggest items to improve the AOI in North America are material cost and quality improvement.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Financial Performance: The second quarter was the strongest in company history, with adjusted EBITDA over $300M and adjusted net income of $243.7M, driven by record TCE rates.
2. Balance Sheet Transformation: Net debt was reduced by $4.2B since 2021 to reach a $1.3B net cash position, significantly de-risking the company.
3. Strategic Cost Reduction: Refinanced high-cost debt with new convertible bonds yielding ~1%, lowering the daily cash breakeven to a company-low of ~$11,000 per day.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Geopolitical Uncertainty: Management repeatedly cited ongoing conflict and fragility in the Middle East and Red Sea as a source of market volatility and unpredictable risk.
2. Rate Moderation from Peaks: Rates have moderated from the "exceptional levels" and record highs experienced earlier in the year, although they remain strong.
3. Declining Seaborne Volumes: Refined product export volumes declined 11% year-over-year in June, a negative trend that was offset by longer voyage distances.
rows.key_quote: Refinery dislocation has been a key component in driving ton-mile demand, one we expect to continue.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Delivered strong adjusted like-for-like growth of 6.5%, outperforming the global market (4.5%), driven by an innovation strategy that contributed 250 basis points from new products. 2. Exceptional growth in Haircare (+15.6%), Professional Products (+11.6%), and Dermatological Beauty (+10.6%). 3. Impressive acceleration in the SAPMENA-SSA region (+13.8%), powered by standout performances in India (+70%) and Vietnam (+50%).
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Reported sales were negatively impacted by a -2.8% headwind from foreign exchange rates. 2. The Makeup category grew by only 2.5%, penalized by service level issues in the Americas. 3. The mass market in China turned slightly negative, and the Consumer Products Division's skincare segment has not yet delivered a significant acceleration.
rows.key_quote: The change in sales contribution from new products has been accelerating each semester... to 250 basis points in the first half of 2026.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Raised full-year guidance for adjusted EBIT, EPS, and free cash flow due to strong operational execution. 2. SendTech segment achieved significant year-over-year margin expansion from operational improvements and a tariff refund. 3. Presort segment is winning market share, evidenced by new business wins and a robust sales pipeline.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Presort profitability was materially impacted by a $6 million hit from higher transportation and fuel costs. 2. SendTech revenue continues to decline due to non-core customer exits and intentionally shrinking the bank's balance sheet. 3. Consolidated revenue growth is not expected until 2027 or later as management prioritizes profitability over near-term top-line expansion.
rows.key_quote: despite the headwinds we faced, execution has been even better than the unexpected headwinds.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Exceptional Revenue Growth: H1 organic growth of 14% (Q2 at +16.5%), driven by booming data center demand (systems business +28%) and a strong rebound in Industrial Automation (+11% in Q2).
2. Significant Margin Expansion: Adjusted EBITA margin expanded 120 bps organically in H1, fueled by accelerating price realization (€280M net price in H1) and strong industrial productivity (€535M).
3. Upgraded Full-Year Guidance: Revenue guidance raised to 10-13% organic growth (from 7-10%), and adj. EBITA margin expansion guidance increased to +70-100 bps (from +50-80 bps).
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Subdued Residential Market: Management identified the residential market as the only end market that continues to be subdued amid broad-based strength elsewhere.
2. Geopolitical Uncertainty: The Middle East situation was cited as a source of volatility, impacting regional growth and posing potential supply chain inflation risks for H2.
3. Gross Margin Mix Pressure: Strong growth in the lower-margin systems business created a negative mix impact, partially offsetting strong gains from pricing and productivity.
rows.key_quote: Our systems business... continued with high demand and strong execution, translating into sales of 28% growth driven by data center.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Industrial Services segment delivered record adjusted EBITDA of $34.4M (vs $7.7M prior year), driven by the Phoenix acquisition and a surge in terminal handling volumes to 6.7M tons.
2. Raised full-year consolidated adjusted EBITDA guidance to $250-$265 million, signaling strong confidence in H2 performance.
3. Domestic Coke profitability improved, with EBITDA up to $42.5M, due to favorable coal-to-coke yields and the Middletown turbine returning to service.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Domestic Coke sales volumes declined to 878,000 tons from 943,000 tons year-over-year due to the Haverhill One shutdown.
2. Quarterly operating cash flow was negative (-$27.2M) due to the delayed receipt of ~$65 million in payments until July.
3. Management expects Q2's "extraordinary" terminal volumes to normalize to lower, albeit still strong, levels in the second half of the year.
rows.key_quote: Our industrial services segment delivered the highest adjusted EBITDA since the acquisition of Phoenix, substantially higher handling volumes at our terminals.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Backlog grew to a decade-high of $451 million, supported by a strong 1.2x book-to-bill ratio.
2. Downhole Technologies segment revenue reached its highest level since Q2 2023, while Completion & Production Services revenue grew 13% sequentially.
3. Strategic shift toward long-cycle markets, with over 70% of H1 revenue from offshore/international activity, up from ~50% in 2023.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Geopolitical conflict in the Middle East contributed to delays in expected drilling and production facility contract awards.
2. Revenue expected in 2026 will be pushed into 2027 due to the contract award delays, tempering the full-year outlook.
3. Downhole Technologies segment margins were pressured by elevated raw material costs for tungsten, explosive powder, and copper.
rows.key_quote: The delay in receiving these awards will push some revenue recognition into 2027 that was originally expected in 2026.

rows.positive_highlights:
Exceptional H1 order intake of €12.7 billion, leading to a record backlog of €25 billion, providing strong medium-term visibility.
Diversification strategy paying off with ~75% of awards in the last 24 months originating outside the Middle East, increasing backlog resilience.
Strong balance sheet with record gross cash of €4.8 billion and a net cash position over €900 million, supporting shareholder returns and investment.
rows.negative_highlights:
Project Delivery EBITDA margin fell 350 basis points to 4.3% due to higher costs and logistical challenges from the Middle East conflict.
Full-year Project Delivery margin guidance was lowered to '5% plus' assuming difficult operating conditions persist for the rest of the year.
First-half group recurring EBITDA was down by approximately one-third year-over-year due to the impacts on the Project Delivery segment.
rows.key_quote: EBITDA margins were impacted by operational challenges and higher costs mostly linked to the prolonged conflict in the Middle East.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record C&I segment revenue of $558M, up 42% YoY, driven by strong demand in data centers and industrial projects.
2. Consolidated gross margin improved to 13.2% from 11.5% YoY, due to better productivity and favorable job closeouts.
3. Record total backlog of $3.16 billion, up 20% YoY, including two new large T&D projects for Xcel Energy valued over $200 million.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Free cash flow was negative $26 million, a significant decline from positive $12 million in the prior year.
2. The negative cash flow was caused by unfavorable timing of tax payments (approx. $30 million higher YoY) and project-related billings.
3. Management guided for a potential headwind to cash flow in H2 as record-low Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) are expected to normalize upwards.
rows.key_quote: The increase in gross margin was primarily due to better-than-anticipated productivity, favorable job closeouts and an increase in scope on certain projects.

rows.positive_highlights: Core Services (ex-Trust and Safety) grew +2.3% like-for-like in H1, driven by vendor consolidation and new AI-powered solutions. The full-year cost savings target was increased from €100M+ to €150M-€170M due to SG&A controls and internal AI efficiencies. Net free cash flow (before restructuring) increased to €299 million, well above the prior year, due to better working capital discipline.
rows.negative_highlights: Consolidated like-for-like revenue remained negative at -1.2% in Q2, an improvement from -2.2% in Q1 but still a decline. The Trust and Safety vertical experienced 'increased softness' due to AI automation and offshoring, significantly dragging down overall growth. Americas region EBITA margin declined due to adverse currency effects (strong Colombian Peso) and rising labor costs.
rows.key_quote: When we exclude the Trust and Safety [business], we would be growing at group level at +1.7% for the H1.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. EBITDA margin expanded 16 bps to 6.8% with all banners improving margins, driven by better mix, scale, and cost control despite deflation. 
2. Strong volume-led growth across all banners, with Biedronka achieving over 4% volume growth in Q2, successfully offsetting significant basket deflation. 
3. Ara in Colombia delivered exceptional sales growth of 30.2% in euros (21.1% in local currency), with a 6.8% like-for-like increase.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant basket deflation in Poland, which intensified in Q2 to approximately -6% at Biedronka, leading to a negative like-for-like of -1.6%. 
2. Market conditions proved more demanding than expected and are not anticipated to improve in H2, with persistent consumer caution and intense competition. 
3. Cash flow before dividends was negative at EUR 332 million, weighed down by deflation impacting sales growth and trade payables at Biedronka.
rows.key_quote: Volume-led growth, combined with careful margin mix and reinforced focus on efficiency drove group sales up by 5.1% and EBITDA to increase 7.6%.

rows.positive_highlights:
Digital streaming (TF1+) advertising revenue grew almost 20% to €109 million, with monthly streamers up 20% to 42 million.
Group COPA of €77 million was above market expectations due to agile cost management in Q2, demonstrating discipline in a weak market.
Maintained a strong balance sheet with a net cash position of €432 million, providing strategic flexibility for digital transformation and shareholder returns.
rows.negative_highlights:
Consolidated revenue declined 6% like-for-like, driven by a 9% drop in media advertising revenue due to a weak linear ad market and competition.
The decline in high-margin linear advertising revenue was the primary cause for the media segment's COPA falling by €44 million year-on-year.
Group net profit fell significantly to €51 million, impacted by lower revenue and an exceptional tax surcharge of €5 million.
rows.key_quote: The EUR 44 million decrease year-on-year [in media COPA] mainly reflects the decline in high-margin linear advertising revenue.

rows.positive_highlights: Sustainable Technology Solutions (STS) backlog reached a record $5.5 billion, up 40% year-over-year, with a Q2 book-to-bill of 1.5x. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 60 basis points year-over-year to 13.0%. The planned separation of the Mission Tech business (to be named Trinzic) is firmly on track, with leadership teams being established.
rows.negative_highlights: Mission Tech's (MTS) reported backlog does not yet reflect $10.6 billion of awarded work currently under protest, creating timing uncertainty. Q2 cash flow was negatively impacted by collections timing in the STS Middle East business. STS adjusted EBITDA declined $11 million year-over-year due to a higher mix of lower-margin equipment procurement activity.
rows.key_quote: STS backlog ended the quarter at a record $5.5 billion, and that is up 40 percent year-over-year, providing strong visibility.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong organic growth of 4.7%, the best in two years, driven by outperformance in the U.S., Italy, Spain, Australia, and China.
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved by 90 bps to 25.8%, with all three regions contributing significantly due to operating leverage and the Fit4Growth program.
Adjusted free cash flow surged by approximately 70% in H1 vs. the prior year, driven by higher profitability and lower Net CapEx.
rows.negative_highlights:
The Fit4Growth program had a negative impact on revenue growth of -3.5% due to store closures and the termination of a managed care agreement.
The U.S. insurance channel remains soft, declining by approximately 4%, which partially offset strong growth in the private pay segment.
The French market is normalizing with lower growth after annualizing the strong performance from the prior year's regulatory reform.
rows.key_quote: Adjusted EBITDA margin... increased by 90 basis points versus last year, driven by operating leverage and the continued execution of our Fit4Growth program.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Secured a $500M, 5-year global co-exclusive licensing deal with Netflix for "The Walking Dead" universe, providing significant revenue and cash flow visibility.
2. Raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue (to $2.4B-$2.45B), AOI (to $410M-$420M), and free cash flow (to ~$220M).
3. Renewed distribution agreements with 4 of the top 5 major domestic MVPDs in the last 12 months, including Comcast, DirecTV, DISH and YouTube.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Q2 net revenue declined 9% YoY to $547 million, with AOI at $46 million, representing the expected "low point for the year".
2. Domestic affiliate revenue declined 17% YoY in Q2, and domestic advertising revenue fell mid-single digits (excluding a one-time issue).
3. Streaming subscriber acquisition was slower than anticipated in the first half of the year, weakening the outlook for subscription revenue.
rows.key_quote: With a license period of 5 years and total contracted license fees of $500 million, this agreement provides us visibility over a multiyear time horizon.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong cash generation: Free cash flow increased 39% to €294 million, leading to an upgraded full-year cash conversion guidance to 50-60%.
2. MRO revenue surge: Commercial MRO revenues grew 29% in USD, driven by GTF work which now constitutes 46% of the MRO segment.
3. GTF recovery progress: Powder metal-related Aircraft on Ground (AOG) levels declined 25% year-to-date, with MRO output for the engine up 40% year-over-year.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Commercial OEM revenue decline: H1 commercial OEM revenue fell 9% due to an exceptionally strong prior-year comparison for spare engine sales and FX effects.
2. MRO margin pressure: The 8% MRO EBIT margin was held back by the higher mix of less profitable GTF MRO work and ramp-up costs at new facilities.
3. Ongoing GTF cash impact: GTF AOG-related compensation payments amounted to a cash outflow of $110 million in the first half of the year.
rows.key_quote: GTF MRO remained the key growth driver, accounting for approximately 46% of total MRO revenues.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Data center sales surged approximately 45%, driving strong growth in the CSS (18% sales growth) and EES (11% sales growth) segments. 
2. Record total backlog increased 60% year-over-year, with all business units posting record levels (CSS +95%, UBS +80%, EES +30%), providing strong future revenue visibility. 
3. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 60 basis points to 7.3%, with all three business units achieving strong profitability (CSS at 10.2%, EES at 9.2%, UBS at 10.0%).
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Full-year free cash flow guidance was lowered to $300M-$600M due to increased working capital requirements needed to support higher-than-expected double-digit sales growth. 
2. Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin is guided to be 'slightly lower sequentially' due to an anticipated shift in business mix, despite expected continued sales growth. 
3. Public power competitive dynamics within the UBS segment continue to be a 'margin headwind in the near term,' even as the overall segment recovers.
rows.key_quote: Wesco data center solutions increased approximately 45% driven by broad-based growth across our data center customer base.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Completed a $600M sale of a 27% stake in its Pinnacle midstream unit, validating the Western Haynesville asset and significantly strengthening the balance sheet. 2. Strong well performance with 11 Western Haynesville wells and 22 Legacy Haynesville wells both averaging an initial production rate of 31 MMcfe/d. 3. Production increased 16% sequentially from Q1, while unit operating costs improved by $0.16/Mcfe, driving EBITDAX margin to 74%.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Lower natural gas prices were the primary driver of weak financial results, with a pre-hedge realized price of only $2.54. 2. Western Haynesville drilling costs rose 13% per foot in Q2 due to steering difficulties, and completion costs increased 5% due to higher proppant loading. 3. Overall leverage remains elevated at 3.0x, though the balance sheet has been substantially de-risked by the Pinnacle transaction.
rows.key_quote: Eleven Western Haynesville wells turned to sales so far in 2026... with a per well initial production rate of 31 million cubic feet per day.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Market Performance: Las Vegas Strip gaming revenue is ahead of last year with high operator occupancy (MGM at 93% in Q2), and regional gaming markets have shown an "amazing rebound" in the last six months.
2. AFFO Growth & Guidance Raise: Q2 AFFO per share grew 4.6% to $0.62, and the company raised its full-year 2026 AFFO per share guidance by increasing the low end of the range.
3. Strategic Portfolio Expansion: Completed the $1.16 billion Golden Entertainment transaction and added three new tenants (Clairvest, Golden Entertainment, Club Med), including its first build-to-suit investment.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Loan Portfolio Credit Issues: A $90 million loan required a modification, including a maturity extension and rate reduction, although it remains cash-paying.
2. Increased Credit Loss Allowance: The CECL allowance was increased after a private tenant issued new debt with a lower credit rating than the proxy previously used for modeling.
3. Tenant M&A Uncertainty: Significant M&A activity involving major tenants like Caesars creates uncertainty and could delay strategic discussions regarding lease resolutions.
rows.key_quote: Strip gaming revenue is running ahead of last year, with room rates continuing to demonstrate the pricing power of this market.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Total revenue grew 13.3% (6.4% excluding Downtown), driven by 16.6% growth in subscription streaming revenue.
2. Announced a major strategic initiative in India to window new releases on paid-only tiers for 72 hours to drive subscription growth.
3. Finalized new or strengthened 'Streaming 2.0' agreements with nearly all major partners, including recent deals with TikTok and Pandora.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Adjusted EBITDA margin (ex-Downtown) declined 1.3 percentage points to 21.5% due to unfavorable revenue mix, a tough prior-year comparison, and a loss in merchandising.
2. Merchandising revenue declined 11% year-over-year, resulting in an adjusted EBITDA loss of €5 million for the quarter.
3. Management guided for Music Publishing growth to slow to "mid-single-digit" for the immediate future, down from prior high-single-digit growth.
rows.key_quote: UMG's new releases will be launched exclusively to paid streaming subscribers for their first 72 hours on both global and regional streaming services.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Lumber Performance: Adjusted EBITDA of $145M, up $116M sequentially, driven by improved pricing from leaner inventories and transportation constraints.
2. Balance Sheet Strength: Available liquidity improved by $215M to $1.2B, supported by strong earnings and a working capital unwind.
3. European Improvement: European lumber business delivered $37M in adjusted EBITDA, reflecting higher pricing, increased shipments, and log cost relief.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Pulp & Paper Segment Loss: Reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $12M, reflecting weak global pulp markets, elevated inventories, and maintenance downtime.
2. Major Restructuring & Closures: Announced closures of Northwood pulp mill, Fox Creek sawmill, and two Swedish mills, resulting in significant upcoming impairment charges (~$65M in Q3).
3. Cautious Near-Term Outlook: Management cited global economic uncertainty, trade disputes, and affordability challenges impacting near-term demand.
rows.key_quote: Our lumber business generated solid EBITDA...with improved pricing driven by leaner inventories, industry capacity rationalizations...and ongoing transportation constraints in the U.S. South.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong RevPAR growth of 5.9% exceeded expectations, driven by high-end leisure travelers and a 6.7% increase in the U.S. 2. Reached a record development pipeline of 154,000 rooms (up 10% YoY) and grew gross fees by 8%, supporting the asset-light model. 3. Luxury and lifestyle brands gained nearly 3 points of RevPAR index, demonstrating significant market share growth.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Middle East RevPAR declined 36% due to regional conflict, and all-inclusive net package RevPAR fell 1.2% due to issues in Mexico. 2. Full-year net rooms growth outlook was adjusted to ~6% due to potential Q4 opening delays into 2027. 3. The planned sale of the Hyatt Grand Central New York is no longer expected to close in 2026, delaying a key asset disposition.
rows.key_quote: Our luxury and lifestyle portfolios increased RevPAR index by nearly 3 points with a large proportion of our hotels gaining share.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Reduced SG&A by $26.6M and initiated a new plan for $100M in incremental annualized savings. 2. Grew same-store used vehicle unit sales by over 5%, gaining market share. 3. Expanded Good Sam services and plans gross margin to 61.8% from 59.5% a year ago.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Lowered full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance significantly to $230M-$270M due to market weakness. 2. New vehicle gross margin compressed to 10.9% from 13.8% and used vehicle margin fell to 16.5% from 20.5% due to aggressive inventory clearing. 3. New RV retail market weakened, with new retail registrations declining 16% through May and trends remaining soft into July.
rows.key_quote: The new RV market weakened, and we moved through aged inventory. That decision pressured vehicle gross profit, but it was the right call.

rows.positive_highlights:
Software solutions sales grew 7.8% to a record $99.4M, led by ActiveDisclosure which grew 29% for the fourth consecutive quarter of 20%+ growth.
Capital markets transactional revenue rebounded strongly, increasing 36% to $47.3M, exceeding expectations due to improved market conditions for IPOs and M&A deals.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded by 170 basis points to a record 36.7%, driven by a favorable sales mix shift to higher-margin software and disciplined cost control.
rows.negative_highlights:
Print and distribution net sales continued their secular decline, falling 15% (approx. $6M) due to reduced demand for printed proxies and reports.
A new proposed SEC rule, Regulation E-Delivery, is expected to further accelerate the industry's migration away from print, potentially materially reducing demand from 2028 onwards.
Arc Suite software growth was modest at 1.8%, a continuation of a slower growth rate outside of periods with major regulatory changes.
rows.key_quote: Our second quarter software solutions net sales growth continues to be led by the performance of ActiveDisclosure, which grew approximately 29% year-over-year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Q4 revenue guidance of $362M-$392M, representing 23% YoY growth at the midpoint, driven by the video distribution patent program (VDP), auto, and wearables.
2. Significant new licensees for the video distribution program, including Meta and Alibaba, demonstrating strong early traction and momentum for this new revenue stream.
3. Full-year non-GAAP operating margin improvement guidance raised to approx. 100 bps, up from a previous range of 50-100 bps.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Reported Q3 results were just "within range," with better-than-expected areas offset by deal timing issues and lower foundational audio revenue.
2. PC market revenue is expected to be down low single digits for the full year due to lower unit shipments and recoveries.
3. Management is closely watching rising memory chip costs, which significantly impact the mobile and PC markets and could be an offset to future growth.
rows.key_quote: Q4 guidance reflects a 23% YoY revenue increase, driven by momentum in our video distribution patent program, including a large deal with Meta.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong operational metrics: Achieved same-property NOI growth of 3.8% driven by record leased occupancy approaching 97% and cash rent spreads over 10%.
2. Raised full-year guidance: Increased same-property NOI growth forecast by 40 bps and now expect core operating EPS growth to exceed 5%.
3. Robust development pipeline: Raised expected 2026 development starts to nearly $400 million, with a $680 million in-process pipeline yielding ~9%, creating value above market acquisition prices.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Non-cash revenue outlook lowered: Guidance for non-cash revenue was reduced due to some leases moving to a cash basis and lower-than-expected below-market rent amortization.
2. Competitive acquisition market: Management noted that transaction cap rates are compressing significantly, with some deals 'starting with a 4,' making accretive acquisitions more challenging.
3. Minor tenant pullback: An EV operator terminated 11 future leases, though this was offset by a significant termination fee covering four years of rent.
rows.key_quote: We are building premier shopping centers at yields that represent substantial spreads to market cap rates, allowing us to generate earnings accretion while growing NAV.

rows.positive_highlights: Adjusted EPS grew 46% year-over-year, driven by accretive share repurchases. The new excess workers' compensation product launched successfully, generating $4 million in premium in July. Underwriting expenses declined 7% to $40 million due to expense management and innovation.
rows.negative_highlights: Net premium earned declined 12% and gross premiums written decreased 20% due to deliberate underwriting actions. Management cited 'fierce competition' and 'irrational behavior' in the middle market, leading them to walk away from business. Policies in force declined 5%, reflecting the strategic pullback in volume.
rows.key_quote: These amounts reflect the pricing and underwriting actions we have put in place to prioritize profitability over volume.

rows.positive_highlights:
Record EBITDA: Achieved a record $2.8 billion in EBITDA, a 17% year-over-year increase, driven by strong global demand and market volatility.
Exceptional Volume Growth: Total pipeline volumes grew 8% and marine terminal volumes surged 33% year-over-year, handling a record 14.7 million barrels per day.
Significant Growth Project Sanctions: Approved construction of two new Permian gas processing plants (11 & 13) and a new NGL fractionator (Frac 15) to support future growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
Potential LPG Export Oversupply: Management acknowledged new market capacity could lead to "lower rates than we've seen in the last couple of years" for LPG exports.
ATEX Pipeline Rate Reset: Confirmed that existing tariffs on the ATEX pipeline are uneconomic and that "some degree of a rate reset" is required in shipper negotiations.
Increased 2026 CapEx Guidance: Raised 2026 growth capital expenditure guidance by over $700 million to a net range of $2.9-$3.4 billion to fund newly sanctioned projects.
rows.key_quote: During April and May, we saw an acute global demand for U.S. energy... for the quarter, it resulted in around $200 million.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record CAP grew to $7.4 billion, providing strong revenue visibility.
2. Revenue increased 29% to $1.5 billion, driven by 18% organic growth and acquisitions.
3. Data center-related CAP surged from $65 million to $223 million year-over-year, validating the strategic expansion into this market.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Materials segment gross profit margin decreased 800 basis points due to severe weather and quarry development costs.
2. Consolidated gross margin declined year-over-year due to margin compression in the Materials segment.
3. Recorded a non-operating charge of $363 million related to convertible notes settlement and remeasurement.
rows.key_quote: Data center-related CAP is increasing from $65 million 1 year ago to $223 million at the end of the second quarter.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Raised the lower end of full-year EPS guidance to a range of $5.61-$5.72, reflecting strong H1 performance. 2. Smokeable segment adjusted OCI grew 2.4% with margins expanding to 64.8%, driven by strong Marlboro pricing. 3. Cigarette industry volume declines moderated to an estimated 5%, attributed to reduced consumer movement to illicit e-vapor products.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Oral Tobacco segment adjusted OCI decreased 8.0% due to strategic investments in on! PLUS and a difficult prior-year comparison. 2. Persistent economic pressure on consumers from inflation and gas prices drove trade-down, causing Marlboro's retail share to fall 1.5 share points YoY. 3. on! brand shipment volume declined 4.2% year-over-year, attributed to trade inventory movements.
rows.key_quote: Smokable price realization for the quarter was 4.5%, driven by strong net pricing for Marlboro, partially offset by mix impact of basic volume growth.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong clinical consumables growth of 15% (ex-China), with the U.S.-Canada region growing over 20%. 2. Significantly elevated instrument placements, with over 95 NovaSeq X systems sold, driven by clinical customer capacity expansion. 3. Raised full-year 2026 guidance, increasing rest-of-world organic revenue growth to over 5% and EPS by $0.12 at the midpoint.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Persistent weakness in research markets, with sequencing consumables declining 7% (rest of world) due to cautious customer spending. 2. Cost headwinds from higher-than-anticipated freight and memory costs, which the company had to absorb. 3. Slower growth in Europe, Middle East, and Latin America, which slightly moderated the strong overall clinical performance.
rows.key_quote: Sequencing consumables revenue in clinical markets grew 15% ex-China, with the U.S. Canada region continuing to grow above 20%.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong demand in infrastructure and heavy non-residential sectors, with data center-related bidding activity up 90%. 2. Exceptional cost management, with controllable organic COGS growth of only 2.1%, which would have been flat excluding energy headwinds. 3. Strategic portfolio transformation with the NFM acquisition and pending LNA combination, shifting focus to higher-margin, durable upstream materials.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Reported aggregates pricing (ASP) declined 2% due to dilutive acquisition and geographic mix, creating a significant optical headwind. 2. Continued energy cost headwinds are offsetting underlying EBITDA performance, leading to a reaffirmed, not raised, EBITDA guidance despite higher revenues. 3. Reported aggregates gross profit was negatively impacted by a $52 million non-cash inventory step-up charge, obscuring strong organic profit growth.
rows.key_quote: if we hadn't seen the spike in energy, we actually would have seen cost of goods sold flat for the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Upgraded Guidance: Raised full-year 2026 targets for RoTE (>15%), EPS (>€1.4), and NII growth (to mid-single-digit). 2. Strong Loan & Fee Growth: Performing loans grew €2.1B YTD (+13% YoY), and fee income grew 10% YoY in H1. 3. Strategic Execution: Completed a 5-year core banking system replacement and announced a new fee-generating real estate partnership with Dromeus Capital.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Rising Operating Costs: Operating expenses increased 8% year-on-year, driven by strategic investments in technology and people. 2. Ongoing Spread Compression: Management expects loan spread compression of 15-20 basis points for the full year. 3. External Volatility: The company continues to operate amidst a 'highly challenging external backdrop' and geopolitical uncertainty, though the local economy is resilient.
rows.key_quote: NII increased nearly 3% quarter-on-quarter... on the back of solid performing loan expansion and a positive trajectory in benchmark rates.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Net revenue grew 12% driven by strong demand for user research studies related to AI-enabled product development.
2. A large user research study significantly outperformed, contributing 4% of net revenues versus an expected 2%.
3. Raised full-year guidance for net revenue growth to 9%-10% and EBITDA margin to 27.8%-28.1%, signaling strong confidence.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. G&A expenses increased 20% year-over-year due to higher travel, recruiting, and business development activities.
2. Interest income decreased due to lower cash balances following significant share repurchases.
3. The expected full-year tax rate is guided to be higher at 28.5% compared to 28.0% in 2025.
rows.key_quote: Our proactive work experienced strong growth led by demand for user research studies as clients accelerate the development of AI-enabled products.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. GIS bookings grew 35% year-over-year with a 1.11x book-to-bill ratio, driven by large deal wins. 2. Early traction in new AI products, with prospects for the OASIS platform reaching contract stage in under 6 weeks. 3. CES segment revenue declined only 3%, outperforming expectations due to stronger project revenues in GrowthX and DXC Engineering.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Total revenue declined 6.7% year-over-year and adjusted EBIT margin fell 180 basis points to 5.0%. 2. The GIS segment was the primary driver of weakness, with revenue declining 11% due to softer discretionary project work. 3. Q2 guidance anticipates a continued organic revenue decline of 5.5% to 6.5%, highlighting a challenging near-term environment before a projected second-half recovery.
rows.key_quote: Revenue in Q1 continued to be impacted by softer levels of discretionary project work that have a more immediate impact on our quarterly revenue.

rows.positive_highlights:
Networks segment EBITDA grew 14% YoY driven by new, favorable regulatory periods in Iberia and investment growth in Brazil.
Upgraded full-year recurring net profit guidance by 12% to €1.4 billion, citing outperformance across all business platforms.
Surging electricity demand in Portugal, driven by data centers (4.6 GW of grid requests), is creating significant long-term growth opportunities.
rows.negative_highlights:
FlexGen & Clients segment EBITDA declined 5% YoY due to lower electricity prices and higher ancillary costs versus an exceptionally strong prior year.
Net debt increased to €17 billion from €15.4 billion at year-end, primarily due to dividend payments and investments ahead of H2 cash inflows.
Generation in Brazil continues to be negatively impacted by curtailment, with management still assessing the adequacy of a proposed compensation plan for past losses.
rows.key_quote: Starting with networks, EBITDA increased 14% year-on-year. That was driven by the new regulatory periods in Iberia... but also growth in Brazil.

rows.positive_highlights:
Digital accelerators revenue grew 31% YoY (35% YTD), significantly outpacing targets and acting as the primary growth driver.
Secured a key credit card processing agreement with Unibanca in Peru, validating the CoreCard acquisition and its competitive advantage in winning new business.
Maintained shareholder returns by repurchasing approximately $50 million in company shares during the quarter.
rows.negative_highlights:
Cross-border payments segment revenue declined 5% and operating income fell 35%, driven by lower U.S. to Mexico remittance volumes due to U.S. immigration policies.
ATM transactions were softer than expected, attributed to U.S. to Europe airline bookings being 5%-8% below the prior year's peak.
Cross-border segment profitability was negatively impacted by a difficult comparison to Q2 2025, which had a non-recurring high-margin fee rebate in Pakistan and favorable FX opportunities.
rows.key_quote: Our digital accelerators were our primary growth driver, with revenue growing 31% year-over-year, highlighting the benefits of our diversified model.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Enrollment Growth: Year-to-date new and total enrollments grew 10% and 6% respectively, driving a 7% timing-adjusted, constant currency revenue increase. 2. Raised Full-Year Guidance: Outlook increased by $28M for revenue and $0.03 for adjusted EPS at the midpoint, citing operational outperformance and favorable FX. 3. Increased Capital Return: Announced a $150 million increase to the stock repurchase program after watching back $181 million in the first half.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Mexico Margin Pressure: YTD adjusted EBITDA in Mexico decreased 2% (adjusted for timing) due to investments and costs for the new Puebla campus. 2. Online Price/Mix Headwind: Strong growth in lower-priced fully online programs partially offset pricing gains from face-to-face programs. 3. Back-Half Weighted Margin Expansion: Margin accretion for the year is expected to be weighted towards the second half of 2026, particularly in Mexico.
rows.key_quote: Year-to-date new and total enrollments were up 10% and 6%, respectively, driving 7% growth in revenue on a timing adjusted constant currency basis.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Profitability & Guidance Raise: Adjusted EPS grew 21% to $1.42, and full-year EPS guidance was significantly raised to $5.12-$5.30 from $4.80-$5.05.
2. Aftermarket Growth: Aftermarket revenue increased 24% year-over-year, contributing to margin expansion and now representing ~25% of ESG revenue.
3. Acquisition Performance: Recent acquisitions (New Way, Mega) are exceeding profit expectations, with the company tracking ahead of its cost synergy plan for New Way.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. SSG Margin Contraction: The Safety and Security Systems (SSG) group's Adjusted EBITDA margin declined to 25.1% from a record 26.9% last year due to unfavorable product mix.
2. Backlog Decline: Total backlog decreased 8% YoY to $1 billion, though most of the decline ($75M) was from the planned discontinuation of a third-party product line.
3. Increased Corporate Costs: Corporate operating expenses rose by $2.1 million YoY due to higher post-retirement expenses and medical costs.
rows.key_quote: Growth in our aftermarket business, leveraging the power of our platform to drive internal margin initiatives and proactive price-cost management were all meaningful organic contributors.

rows.positive_highlights: North America outperformance driven by market share gains, with watch-through up high-single-digits. Strong demand in Southern Europe, with sales up ~8% due to good weather and tourism. Efficiency plan delivered ~€15 million in savings YTD, offsetting inflation and protecting margins.
rows.negative_highlights: Demand for new pool construction remains soft across most markets. Sales impacted by geopolitical instability in the Middle East (~3% of group sales), causing delays in commercial projects. Gross margin faced pressure from inflation and an unfavorable product/geographic mix.
rows.key_quote: In North America, watch-through across our channels was up high-single-digits, outperforming the market, which reflects consistent and continued market share gains.

rows.positive_highlights:
New active ingredients sales doubled year-over-year, highlighted by the first new herbicide (Isoflex) approval in the EU since 2019.
