Progress on ~$1 billion debt reduction target, with the sale of the India business in late stages and expected to sign in May.
Strong early orders in Brazil (32% of H2 direct sales secured by April) validate confidence in the significant second-half recovery plan.
rows.negative_highlights:
Revenue declined 4% and the company posted an adjusted loss per share of $0.23 in Q1.
Price declined 6%, with lower sales to diamide partners accounting for nearly half of the drop, reflecting post-patent strategy and competition.
Q2 guidance is very weak, with revenue expected to fall 17% and adjusted EPS to decline 70% at the midpoint.
rows.key_quote: These partners accounted for nearly half of our overall price decline of 6%.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Capital Returns: Repurchased $395M in shares; committed to exceeding a $300M quarterly floor, citing share undervaluation. 2. Disciplined Underwriting Outperformance: Global Wholesale & Specialty attritional loss ratio improved 390 bps; property cat portfolio rates declined only 10% vs. market declines of 15-20%. 3. Strategic Initiatives Progressing: Launched Annapurna Re casualty sidecar to enhance ROE and capital flexibility; third-party capital AUM up 89% since the start of 2025.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Casualty Reserve Strengthening: Took a reserve charge of just under $200M for North America casualty reinsurance due to elevated loss trends in older accident years. 2. Softening Property Market: Acknowledged market-wide property pricing was down 15-20% at renewals, increasing competitive pressure. 3. Strategic Premium Reduction: Gross written premium declined 7-9% as the company deliberately cut exposure, notably reducing reinsurance casualty lines by 19%, signaling unattractive market conditions.
rows.key_quote: We have continued to decrease our exposure to U.S. casualty lines and selectively reduce business where pricing or structure did not meet our return thresholds.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Accelerated Net Sales: H1 net sales surged 35% YoY, with a further 40% YoY estimated increase in July, driving broad-based revenue growth.
2. Upgraded 2026/2029 Outlook: Guidance was raised due to better-than-expected net sales, resilient deposits in a rising rate environment, and an expected deceleration in cost growth from AI initiatives.
3. Strong Brokerage Growth & Initiatives: Brokerage revenue grew 15% YoY, and new initiatives like securities lending (40% of assets opted-in) and order internalization are expected to provide significant future upside.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Increased Operating Costs: Adjusted operating costs rose ~6% YoY, with an additional €15M planned for growth initiatives and €5M for the pan-European platform setup.
2. Deposit Outflows in July: Deposits saw a negative flow of ~€300 million in July, though management noted this was offset by the positive impact of rising rates on NII.
3. Pan-European Launch Timeline: The full launch of the pan-European platform is now slated for early 2027, following a "family and friends" phase at year-end 2026.
rows.key_quote: The better outlook is driven by a combination of better-than-expected net sales with all the mix components contributing positively to revenues.

rows.positive_highlights: AI revenue grew 54.6% YoY, reaching 30.7% of total company revenue. The TMT vertical expanded 36.4% YoY, driven by vendor consolidation at key technology clients. Non-GAAP gross margin improved by 220 basis points to 36.9% due to operating leverage and efficiency.
rows.negative_highlights: Total headcount declined 3.5% year-over-year, from 5,013 to 4,838, primarily from rationalizing non-billable roles. The Retail vertical was flat year-over-year, indicating stagnation in a major segment. The non-AI portion of the business experienced an implied decline as AI growth significantly outpaced total company growth.
rows.key_quote: AI revenue reached 30.7% of the total company revenue in the second quarter, growing 54.6% year-over-year.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record funds flow ($1.4B) and free funds flow ($925M) driven by high oil prices and production beats. 2. Full-year production guidance raised by 5,000 BOE/d to 385,000 BOE/d with no capex increase. 3. Operating costs fell 13% YoY, with full-year cost guidance reduced by $0.50/BOE, adding ~$70M to free cash flow.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Weak AECO natural gas prices, which averaged only $1.63 per Mcf during the quarter. 2. Management prioritizing debt reduction ($2.5B net debt) over share buybacks in the near-term despite record free cash flow. 3. Planned Q3 downtime of 10,000 BOE/d incorporated into guidance.
rows.key_quote: The combination of crude oil and condensate pricing and continuing to lower operating costs resulted in a robust operating netback of $43.84 per BOE.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong core revenue growth: Net Interest Income (NII) surged 30% to €478.5M, while Net Commission Income grew 10% to €706M. 2. Excellent commercial results: Acquired 110,000 new customers, total net inflows were €6.37B (+4%), and total assets grew 16% YoY. 3. Improved profitability: Operating margin increased 20% YoY, and the cost-income ratio dropped to 36.1% from 37.6% for FY2025.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Increased loan impairments: Impairment on loans rose from €14M in H1 2025 to over €20M in H1 2026. 2. Higher acquisition costs: The ratio of acquisition cost to growth commissions ticked up to 35.8% from 34.8%, attributed to a timing mismatch. 3. Market headwinds: Management noted ongoing uncertainty from geopolitical tensions and volatile markets as a persistent external factor to navigate.
rows.key_quote: Net interest income was once again a very strong contributor... coming in at EUR 478.5 million, up 30%.

rows.positive_highlights:
Raised full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook to 35% YoY, up from a prior ~25% view.
High Performance Computing (HPC) customer pipeline expanded to an $850 million annual opportunity, driving a 150% YoY increase in computing system orders.
Core business recovering as semiconductor test utilization hit 80%, an inflection point for capex, with industrial orders up 87% YoY.
rows.negative_highlights:
Automotive segment continues to underperform the broader recovery, with orders declining 24% year-over-year.
Higher input costs and longer lead times for certain components, particularly memory, present a potential headwind to profitability.
Production capacity for HPC handlers is a near-term constraint, limiting further upside in 2026 until the Malaysian factory expansion is complete.
rows.key_quote: Computing led with 46% of system orders, a 150% year over year increase driven by Eclipse growth in high performance computing.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Demand stabilization: The underlying book-to-bill ratio surpassed 1.0 for the first time since Q2 2024, signaling a bottom in the market downturn. 2. New growth vectors: Management highlighted a ~$300M long-term annual revenue opportunity in data center applications and secured a EUR 127.4M EU Chips Act grant. 3. Segment strength: Medical revenue surged 39% YoY to $21M and Wide Bandgap revenue grew 34% YoY to $10.6M, showing resilience in key areas.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Core market decline: Automotive revenue fell 19% year-over-year to $116 million due to ongoing inventory normalization across the supply chain. 2. Overall revenue contraction: Total quarterly revenue was down 7% year-over-year to $199.8 million, reflecting broad market softness. 3. Margin pressure from underutilization: Low capacity utilization of 60%, driven by automotive weakness, negatively impacted profitability, resulting in a 16.8% EBITDA margin.
rows.key_quote: Our underlying book-to-bill ratio returned above 1.0 for the first time since Q2 2024, an encouraging sign demand conditions are gradually improving.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Financial Performance: Adjusted EPS grew 32% to $1.41 on 18.6% revenue growth, driven by a 19% YoY increase in AUM&A to $622 billion. 2. Broad-Based Net Inflows: Achieved $2.2 billion in consolidated net flows, with IG Wealth recording its 8th consecutive positive quarter and Mackenzie securing $5 billion in new institutional awards. 3. Strategic Investment Growth: Wealthsimple's AUA surged 84% YoY on record $17 billion in net flows, and Rockefeller's client assets increased 31%.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. ChinaAMC Outflows: ChinaAMC experienced CNY 145 billion in net outflows as the government's 'national team' withdrew stabilization funds from passive ETFs. 2. Ongoing Fee Rate Pressure: Management guided for Q3 advisory fee rate declines at IG Wealth (0.25-0.5 bps) and Mackenzie (~0.7 bps overall) due to mix shift. 3. Restructuring for AI Investment: Announced a restructuring charge to create capacity for significant investments in AI, indicating a need to reallocate existing resources to fund future growth initiatives.
rows.key_quote: Higher average AUM&A supported earnings, reflecting $2.2 billion in net flows and strong investment returns.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Screening (Shield) revenue surged to $53M (from $15M YoY) on 66k tests, driven by strong commercial momentum. 2. Secured a landmark coverage decision for Shield from UnitedHealth Group, providing access to ~70 million commercial lives. 3. Oncology test volume grew an accelerated 63% YoY, led by >100% growth in Reveal MRD tests and >30% growth in Guardant360 Liquid.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Full-year free cash flow burn guidance was increased by $10M to a range of $195M-$205M to fund accelerated lab capacity investment. 2. Adjusted EBITDA loss widened slightly to $56M from $52M YoY due to heavy reinvestment in the Shield commercial launch. 3. Biopharma & Data segment grew a modest 9% YoY, lagging the significant acceleration seen in Oncology and Screening.
rows.key_quote: The tremendous 63% growth in Oncology volume represented another quarter of acceleration, reflecting the increasing strength of our portfolio.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Merchant Services (80% of revenue) regained momentum, with a second consecutive quarter of accelerating growth (+2% external revenue in Q2).
2. Adjusted EBITDA guidance of €630-€650M was maintained despite a revenue revision, highlighting strong cost discipline and benefits from the 'North Star' transformation.
3. Balance sheet significantly strengthened, achieving the net leverage target of <2x EBITDA six months ahead of schedule through divestments and capital raise.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Full-year revenue guidance was marginally lowered due to a slower-than-expected commercial rebound and longer sales cycles in Financial Services.
2. Financial Services remains a major drag, with revenue declining 7.9% in Q2, offsetting growth in the core merchant business.
3. Net revenue growth lagged external revenue (-2% vs +2% in Q2 for Merchant Services), indicating gross margin pressure from adverse geographic and channel mix.
rows.key_quote: Our profitability is starting to improve, especially on Merchant Services, supported by disciplined cost management and the first benefits of our transformation program.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. WVE-007 (Obesity): Positive Phase I data showed durable silencing (up to 88% Activin E reduction), a 16.5% improvement in Visceral Fat-to-Muscle Ratio (VMR), and fat loss without muscle loss; Phase IIa trial initiated. 
2. WVE-006 (AATD): FDA granted a meeting for the end of summer 2026 to discuss a potential accelerated approval pathway based on compelling clinical data. 
3. Strong Balance Sheet: Ended Q2 with $490.6M in cash, providing a robust operational runway into Q3 2028 to fund pipeline advancement.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Revenue Decline & Widening Loss: Revenue fell to $2.3M from $8.7M YoY, and net loss increased to $69.4M from $50.5M due to higher R&D and G&A spending. 
2. DMD Program De-prioritization: Shifted strategy for the N531 DMD program to seek partnerships *before* a potential NDA filing, citing the evolving regulatory landscape, suggesting a delay or reduced internal commitment. 
3. Increased Cash Burn: Operating expenses rose significantly, with R&D up to $51.3M (from $43.5M YoY) and G&A up to $24.8M (from $18M YoY) to support the expanding pipeline.
rows.key_quote: With a single dose of 007 in our Phase I population, we already observed a 16.5% improvement in VMR [visceral fat-to-muscle ratio].

rows.positive_highlights: Upgraded long-term outlook to "9-plus percent EPS growth on average through 2030". Secured $6 billion in new generation investments from the SPS RFP, bringing the incremental investment pipeline to over $10 billion. Strong data center demand with 4 GW of new load expected to be secured by year-end 2027.
rows.negative_highlights: Rising financing costs negatively impacted EPS, with higher interest expense decreasing earnings by $0.12 per share. Significant operational risk from Colorado wildfires requires extensive and costly mitigation efforts. A massive $70B+ base capital plan plus over $10B in incremental projects carries inherent execution risk.
rows.key_quote: Higher electric revenues due to nonfuel riders and sales growth increased earnings by $0.17 per share.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Loan Growth: Achieved $856 million in net loan growth, a 16% annualized rate, driven by broad-based originations across C&I, specialty CRE, and other commercial categories. 2. NIM Expansion: Net interest margin increased 6 basis points sequentially to 4.84%, with guidance to remain at the high end of its target range. 3. Positive EPS Outlook: A change in California tax law is expected to reduce the corporate tax rate by 3 percentage points starting next quarter, providing a direct boost to future EPS.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Loan Pricing Pressure: Management noted that "new loan yields are coming in slightly lower" in many categories due to heightened competition. 2. One-time Tax Charge: Recognized a $5.5 million one-time non-cash deferred tax impairment charge during the quarter. 3. Increasing Operating Expenses: Stated that the hiring of a new floor plan financing team will add $1 million in quarterly expenses, in addition to upcoming annual merit increases.
rows.key_quote: Asset based lending, commercial real estate specialty equipment leasing, lender finance, and single family warehouse had strong originations and net loan growth this quarter.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Same-property RevPAR grew 5.6%, driven entirely by a 5.7% increase in ADR, demonstrating strong pricing power.
2. Raised full-year adjusted EBITDAre guidance by $7M, driven by strong forward-looking indicators, including a 12% increase in H2 group room revenue pace.
3. Strong transient demand, with transient RevPAR up 6.9%, and projected overall July RevPAR growth of approximately 10%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Same-property hotel EBITDA margin declined 65 bps to 28.7%, primarily due to lapping a $1.5M real estate tax refund from Q2 2025.
2. Total RevPAR growth of 3.3% significantly lagged RevPAR growth of 5.6% due to softer group demand and lower out-of-room spend.
3. Reported a GAAP net loss of $19.3 million resulting from a noncash impairment charge related to the sale of the Kimpton RiverPlace Hotel.
rows.key_quote: Group room revenue pace for the second half was up 12% at the end of June, versus the year prior.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. New Category revenue accelerated to 18% growth, driven by a 66% surge in Modern Oral (Velo).
2. The U.S. region delivered strong multi-category performance with total revenue up 8.5% and adjusted operating profit up 10.1%.
3. Full-year EPS guidance was upgraded to the middle of the 5-8% range due to lower finance costs and strong cash flow.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Heated Products (glo) revenue declined nearly 12% due to inventory movements and competitive pressure.
2. APMEA region recovery was slower than expected, with revenue down 6.3% due to regulatory headwinds and illicit trade.
3. Vapour revenue declined in AME (-14%) and APMEA (-28%) due to regulatory changes and strategic market exits.
rows.key_quote: New Category revenue growth accelerated to 18%, driven by another outstanding performance from Modern Oral, which was up 66%.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Secured a landmark patent license agreement with Amazon for devices and services, including Prime Video, which contributed $110M in Q2 revenue. 2. Raised full-year revenue guidance by $85M at the midpoint to $775M-$845M due to strong momentum. 3. Won two significant injunctions against Disney from the European Unified Patent Court for HEVC patents, with the court finding Disney an 'unwilling licensee'.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Ongoing litigation costs remain elevated due to enforcement actions against other parties, despite the Amazon case moving to more efficient arbitration. 2. The final value of the Amazon agreement is subject to an 18-24 month arbitration process, creating long-term uncertainty on the final deal size. 3. A final licensing agreement with Disney has not been reached, indicating a continued and costly dispute despite recent legal wins.
rows.key_quote: We have agreed to enter into a patent license agreement with Amazon, covering Amazon's devices and services, including Amazon's Prime Video.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. LTL Operating Ratio Improvement: Achieved a record adjusted operating ratio of 79.9%, a 300 basis point YoY improvement, outperforming seasonality by over 100 basis points.
2. Raised Full-Year Guidance: Increased full-year margin improvement outlook to "at least 200 basis points" from a prior 100-150 bps, driven by strong volume and pricing.
3. Strong Volume Acceleration: July tonnage per day grew over 6% YoY, a significant acceleration from Q2 and outperforming seasonality, signaling strong market share gains and improving demand.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Inflationary Pressures: Management acknowledged mid-single-digit inflation, primarily from wages and benefits, which they are currently mitigating with productivity but remains a headwind.
2. Tightening Driver Market: Management noted "we are seeing the hiring market tighten," which could pose a challenge to scaling the workforce if demand accelerates sharply.
3. Challenging European Macro Environment: Although the European business is performing well, management noted the overall European economy is "flattish, slightly slow," which constrains the timing for a potential sale of the asset.
rows.key_quote: In North American LTL, we grew adjusted operating income by 36% on a 15% increase in revenue, highlighting the scalability of our network.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. North American sales grew ~20% (constant currency) driven by market share gains in high-horsepower tractors (Fendt).
2. Successfully reduced dealer inventory across all major regions, with North American units down 7% in the quarter.
3. Resilient Precision Ag (PTX) business is on track for flat to modest growth, outperforming the broader equipment market.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Lowered full-year revenue and EPS guidance due to weaker-than-expected demand in Europe, Brazil, and North American small ag.
2. European sales missed expectations, driven by a German market that was ~15% weaker than anticipated.
3. Adjusted operating margin fell 170 bps to 6.6% due to lower production volumes and a $50M year-over-year headwind from tariffs.
rows.key_quote: The German market was down probably about 15% more than we had anticipated, and given our market share, that was a big driver.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Q2 revenue of $845.5 million (up 7.8%), driven by broad-based growth across all asset classes.
2. FMX UST platform market share grew to a record 42%, while FMX futures ADV increased 16-fold year-over-year.
3. Strong Q3 guidance issued, projecting ~9% revenue growth and ~17% pre-tax adjusted earnings growth at the midpoint.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Asia Pacific revenues decreased by 2.9%.
2. ECS segment growth was partially offset by lower oil and refined product volumes due to the Strait of Hormuz closure.
3. Equities growth was muted by lower European equity derivative activity.
rows.key_quote: This growth was broad based across every asset class reflecting the durability diversification, and the strength of our global platform.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Q2 Performance: Achieved record Q2 adjusted EPS of $1.90 and record recurring revenues of $1.4 billion (up 8%).
2. Strategic Acquisition: Announced a $5.7B agreement to acquire MarketAxess, aiming to create an integrated global fixed income network from retail to institutional clients.
3. Strong Segment Growth & Raised Guidance: The rates business grew 24%; FIDS recurring revenue guidance was raised to 7-8% from mid-single-digits due to strong data demand.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Increased Expense & CapEx: Full-year adjusted operating expense guidance was raised to fund growth initiatives, and 2026 CapEx guidance was increased to $850 million.
2. Temporary Leverage Increase: The all-cash MarketAxess acquisition is expected to temporarily increase gross leverage to approximately 3.4x pro forma EBITDA post-close.
3. Softer Energy Volumes: Energy volumes were softer compared to the prior year's highly volatile quarter, though management emphasized strong underlying structural open interest growth.
rows.key_quote: Our rates business once again delivered exceptional performance, growing 24% versus the year-ago period, as investors... actively manage their duration exposure.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Confirmed long-term strategic EBIT margin corridor of 8% to 10% and a clear restructuring plan to achieve it.
2. The joint venture in China remains profitable despite significant market headwinds and volume declines.
3. Favorable year-on-year warranty cost trends are expected to continue into the second half of the year.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Unexpected and severe market deterioration in China was the primary negative driver of performance.
2. A major restructuring program was announced, with an expected EBIT impact of up to 1.25% of auto sales for the full year, primarily in H2.
3. Residual values are on a 'less positive' trend compared to the prior year, indicating pressure on the used car market.
rows.key_quote: The production footprint is... quite balanced... so the only market which gave us a surprise was China.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Commercial Aerospace sales grew 18.3%, driven by rising production rates for the A350, 787, and narrow-body aircraft.
2. Gross margin increased to 26.1% from 22.8% year-over-year due to strong operating leverage from higher volumes.
3. Raised full-year guidance for sales (to $2.025B-$2.125B) and adjusted EPS (to $2.30-$2.40) on strong commercial demand.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Defense, Space & Other sales decreased 7%, primarily due to the divestiture of an Austrian industrial business.
2. Management guided for a softer second half on margins and EPS due to Q3 seasonality, increased hiring, and line restart costs.
3. Foreign exchange created a 90 basis point headwind to operating margin in the quarter.
rows.key_quote: higher sales volume generated greater operating leverage through improved cost absorption, which resulted in adjusted operating margins of 13.9%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. **Strong Earnings & Raised Guidance**: Non-GAAP EPS grew 14% to $1.27. Management issued a new outlook for full-year EPS growth of 20-25%, signaling strong second-half acceleration. 
2. **Accelerating Workplace Demand & Synergies**: Workplace organic orders grew 5% in Q2 and accelerated into Q3. Steelcase synergy estimates were effectively raised, now seen as "at least $120 million".
3. **Exceptional Margin Expansion**: Residential Building Products operating margin expanded 470 bps to 20.4%, and the company projects another double-digit EPS growth year in 2027 based on locked-in cost savings.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. **Residential Building Products Revenue Decline**: Segment revenue fell 1.6% due to weakness in the new construction channel, which offset remodel/retrofit growth.
2. **Ongoing Housing Market Softness**: Management expects continued new construction weakness for the remainder of 2026 due to interest rates and affordability concerns.
3. **Acquisition-Related Debt**: Net leverage stands at 2.4x due to the Steelcase acquisition, though the company is actively paying down debt and expects to return to pre-acquisition levels within 18-24 months.
rows.key_quote: We project double-digit EPS growth again next year, driven by expected synergies from Steelcase and legacy network optimization projects.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Free cash flow increased 67% in H1 to $233 million, prompting a 50% increase in the 2026 share repurchase target to $300 million. 
2. North America boiler sales grew an exceptional 21% in the quarter, driven by residential momentum and a return to commercial growth. 
3. North America segment achieved 3% organic sales growth, supported by strong boiler performance and carryover pricing actions.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. China sales plummeted 28% in local currency due to broad market weakness, causing Rest of World segment margin to collapse to 5.2%. 
2. Softer-than-expected North America residential water heater demand led to a reduction in full-year sales and EPS guidance. 
3. North America segment margin declined 100 bps to 24.4% as a ~20% YoY increase in Q2 steel costs offset pricing and growth benefits.
rows.key_quote: North America adjusted segment margin was 24.4%, a decrease of 100 basis points... largely offset by higher steel and other input costs.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Growth portfolio revenue surged 14% to $7.6 billion, now comprising nearly 60% of total revenue, with strong contributions from Reblozyl (+29%) and Camzyos (+59%).
2. Eliquis delivered exceptional demand-driven growth of 21%, leading to a full-year guidance raise for the product to 20-25% growth.
3. Full-year 2026 guidance for both total revenue and adjusted EPS was increased, reflecting strong first-half momentum and confidence in the second half.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. The pivotal readout for milvexian in atrial fibrillation is delayed from late 2026 to Q1 2027 due to a slower-than-projected pace of clinical events.
2. Top-line data readouts for the key Cobenfy (KarXT) ADEPT program in Alzheimer's psychosis are now expected to begin in early 2027, a delay from previous expectations.
3. Opdivo revenue decreased 4% to approximately $2.5 billion, primarily driven by continued market conversion to the newer therapy, Qvantig.
rows.key_quote: Growth portfolio revenue rose 14% to $7.6 billion, now representing nearly 60% of total revenue, offsetting legacy portfolio decline.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Retail Growth: Retail channel grew +19.3% at constant exchange rates, with double-digit increases across all markets.
2. Key Geographic Momentum: Americas revenue grew +20.6% and Asia grew +14.1%, with China's contribution being particularly significant.
3. Margin Expansion: EBIT margin improved to 17.1% from 16.6% YoY, and gross margin increased by 50 basis points due to a favorable sales mix.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Muted Wholesale Performance: The wholesale channel grew only 2.7% at constant exchange rates, significantly lagging retail.
2. Slower Growth in Europe: Europe was the slowest-growing region at +5.3%, weighed down by the weaker wholesale channel.
3. Increased Net Debt: Net financial debt rose to €225.1 million from €197.2 million YoY due to H1-concentrated investments and dividends, though a significant year-end reduction is expected.
rows.key_quote: Excellent results allow us to raise revenue growth estimates for the full year... we expect growth between +10% and +11% in 2026.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised full-year ATM revenue growth guidance to 35% due to insatiable AI-driven demand across both LEAP and general packaging, leading to widespread capacity constraints.
2. ATM gross margin expected to exceed the 30% structural ceiling in Q4, signaling a fundamental step-up in profitability and a potential upward revision of long-term targets.
3. Announced plans to double LEAP revenue in 2027 and increased 2026 CapEx by $2B to $10.5B to support a multi-year growth cycle.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Near-term growth is gated by the physical ability to build facilities and install equipment, with the company "just trying to keep up" with demand.
2. Heavy CapEx is causing negative free cash flow, a situation expected to persist "for some time" as the company continues its aggressive investment cycle.
3. EMS business margins declined sequentially due to product mix and higher component costs, with a large portion of its projected 40% Q3 revenue growth being a pass-through of memory price hikes.
rows.key_quote: Hardware infrastructure is a bottleneck. With AI, the hardware requirement is new, insatiable and more complicated and more complex.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Core 'New Keppel' net profit grew 25% YoY to SGD 530 million, driven by strong performance in the Infrastructure segment and higher recurring income. 2. Surpassed the end-2026 Funds Under Management (FUM) target, reaching SGD 106 billion, which will accelerate future asset management fee growth. 3. Established a clear monetization pathway for legacy rigs via a fund with a USD 1.5B commitment from Apollo, de-risking the balance sheet and unlocking capital.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Consolidated net profit dropped 59% YoY to SGD 155 million, dragged down by a SGD 375 million loss from the noncore portfolio. 2. A significant accounting loss of SGD 165 million was recognized from the impairment of 13 legacy rig assets. 3. The Real Estate segment recorded a net loss of SGD 19 million, impacted by lower contributions from its Aermont investment and a loss from the dividend-in-specie of Keppel REIT units.
rows.key_quote: Net loss from the noncore portfolio was SGD 375 million, mainly due to an accounting loss of SGD 165 million from legacy rig impairments.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Announced a landmark $303M joint venture for an advanced technology facility for a Fortune 20 tenant, with a high straight-line yield of 11.6%. 2) Raised full-year 2026 AFFO per share guidance to a midpoint of $1.56, representing nearly 5% growth over 2025. 3) The build-to-suit pipeline now stands at $645M, providing visibility into over 10% ABR growth from projects stabilizing by H1 2027.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Same-store 'Other' revenue declined 1.6% due to an office asset being taken offline for redevelopment. 2) Incurred a $1.6M cost for a build-to-suit option that was not pursued, showing some execution risk in the development strategy. 3) The ultimate path and timeline for the large-scale 'Project Triboro' remains under evaluation, with a decision targeted by year-end.
rows.key_quote: Our build-to-suit pipeline will generate $46 million of incremental ABR... equating to over 10% growth on our current portfolio, a rare forward visibility.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. CAC Acquisition Outperformance: CAC grew 23% with 59% sales velocity, booking over $80M in new business YTD, up 43% YoY, significantly ahead of plan.
2. Strong MGA/TPA Growth: The MGA/TPA segment delivered 56% organic revenue growth, driven by strong performance in multifamily and admitted home products.
3. Margin and Cash Flow Expansion: Adjusted EBITDA margin increased 110 bps to 23.7% and adjusted free cash flow surged 437% to $46M, driven by the accretive CAC merger.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Weak Headline Organic Growth: Consolidated organic revenue growth was only 2%, held back by multiple transitory headwinds.
2. IAS Segment Decline: The core Insurance Advisory Solutions (IAS) segment reported a 2% organic revenue decline due to integration-related attrition and market headwinds.
3. Softening Insurance Market: Management confirmed a 240 basis point headwind from softening insurance rates, describing the property market as 'very deeply soft'.
rows.key_quote: Excluding idiosyncratic noise... and including new partnerships, organic revenue growth would have been 8% in the second quarter.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Reached a decisive agreement with the French state on the Economic Regulation Agreement (ERA) for 2027-2034, providing long-term visibility and supporting an €8.2B investment program.
2. Attributable net income more than tripled to €312M, driven by a €257M gain from the partial monetization of the GMR Airports stake.
3. Implemented cost-saving measures expected to deliver €40-€60M in 2026 to protect margins amid a challenging environment.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Revised full-year guidance downward, with Paris traffic growth now forecast at only ~0.5% and recurring EBITDA lowered to a range of €2.3B to €2.35B.
2. The operating environment became more challenging due to the indirect effects of the Middle East conflict, which softened demand and suppressed traffic growth.
3. Recurring EBITDA declined by 1% year-over-year, indicating pressure on operational profitability.
rows.key_quote: The Middle East conflict’s indirect consequences have spread more broadly, affecting traffic growth and airline behavior, and ultimately, demand trends.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strategic portfolio rotation: Received $1.2B in repayments on seasoned loans and originated $1.4B in new investments focused on residential, industrial, and net lease sectors.
2. New growth vector: Entered the $200B home builder finance sector via a JV, targeting granular loans with mid-to-high teens levered yields.
3. Strong capital markets execution: Issued $450M of senior secured notes at the tightest new issue spread in company history, extending debt maturities with none until 2029.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant impairments and reserves: Took three new impairments on office-related loans, driving a $0.80/share increase in CECL reserves and a GAAP net loss of $0.48/share.
2. Book value and earnings decline: Book value per share fell 4% to $19.31, and management guided for lower Distributable Earnings in Q3, putting the dividend under review.
3. Increased borrower stress in legacy portfolio: A $1B subset of watchlist office loans is experiencing increased pressure from higher rates, causing previously supportive borrowers to default.
rows.key_quote: Higher rates impacted legacy watchlist assets; this dynamic was at play this quarter as we took three new impairments on previously supported loans.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong organic growth: Consumer checking household growth accelerated to 5.7% YoY, with the expansion strategy adding a third of the bank's total customers since 2018.
2. Raised full-year guidance: NII growth guidance increased to 4.75-5.25% (from 3.5-5%), non-interest income growth to 7.5-8.5% (from 4-5%), and expense growth guidance was lowered.
3. Robust loan pipeline: The 90-day weighted loan pipeline reached a record $2.17 billion, up 11% from Q1, indicating strong future lending momentum.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Increased non-performing assets: NPAs rose to $114 million from $73 million in Q1, primarily due to a single $54 million multifamily CRE loan being moved to non-performing status.
2. Intensifying competition: Management noted increased competition in Texas, particularly on loan structure for commercial real estate and on deposit pricing for large balances.
3. Rising deposit costs: The cost of interest-bearing deposits increased 6 basis points sequentially to 1.61%, reflecting the competitive environment and deposit mix shifts.
rows.key_quote: During the expansion, consumer checking accounts have grown 47%... a third of our customers are new to Frost since the expansion began.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Announced a major new strategic partnership with Canva, creating a significant new customer acquisition channel and growth driver. 2. Raised the fiscal 2028 adjusted EBITDA target to at least $615 million, up from a prior $600 million, driven by M&A contributions. 3. Issued strong fiscal 2027 guidance, projecting adjusted EBITDA growth of over 13% to at least $520 million and adjusted free cash flow of ~$200 million.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Missed Q4 profitability expectations due to ~$10 million in negative one-off items that occurred at the end of the quarter. 2. Specific negative impacts included a $4.7 million write-off of a Canadian duty drawback receivable and $7.1 million in higher start-up costs for manufacturing build-out. 3. Lowered the fiscal 2028 net income guidance to at least $192 million from a prior target of $200 million, citing higher non-cash amortization and depreciation.
rows.key_quote: The continued variable gross profit per customer growth in Vistaprint... which... increased 9% year-over-year, continuing that multiyear trend.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong new client momentum: Launched 10 new clients in Q3 and a record 25 year-to-date, including a new Tier 1 lender in U.S. Title. 2. U.S. Title segment hyper-growth: Revenue surged 70% YoY, driven by a 127% increase in refinance origination revenues from market share gains. 3. Significant operating leverage: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA increased 117% YoY to $0.7 million on a 13% revenue increase.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. U.S. Appraisal margin pressure: Net revenue margins in the core U.S. Appraisal segment decreased by 160 basis points YoY to 24.6% due to unfavorable mix. 2. Continued U.S. Title losses: The fast-growing U.S. Title segment still posted an adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.3 million. 3. Canadian segment weakness: Revenue in Canada declined 5% YoY due to a lower addressable mortgage origination market.
rows.key_quote: U.S. Title revenues increased 70% year-over-year...driven mainly by...market share gains with existing and new clients.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. R2 Launch Success: Started R2 deliveries with reservation-to-order conversion rates "meaningfully higher than what we expected" for the premium $58,000 Launch Edition.
2. Raised Guidance: Increased full-year delivery guidance by 3,000 units to 65k-70k and improved adjusted EBITDA loss guidance by $50M at the midpoint.
3. Gross Margin Improvement: Automotive gross loss improved by $299 million year-over-year to a loss of only $36 million, helping drive consolidated gross margin to a positive 11%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. R2 Ramp Costs: The R2 production ramp incurred approximately $100 million in incremental cost of revenue in Q2 and is expected to negatively impact automotive gross profit again in Q3.
2. Macro Headwinds: Management cited increasing costs for commodities, memory, and logistics, as well as macro and geopolitical uncertainty, as creating complexity.
3. Slower Commercial Adoption (Non-Amazon): Adoption of the Electric Delivery Van (EDV) by fleets other than Amazon "has taken longer than we would have expected".
rows.key_quote: That conversion rate from reservation to orders has been meaningfully higher than what we expected, which is a great signal.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record June quarter revenue of $109.4B (+16% YoY) driven by exceptionally strong iPhone (+22%) and Mac (+29%) sales.
2. Phenomenal early reception for the new Siri AI, which management is "off the charts excited about" and sees as a major future growth driver.
3. Services revenue hit a June quarter record of $30.7B (+12%), with the install base reaching 2.5 billion active devices and paid subscriptions surpassing 1.5 billion.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Supply constraints are expected to "increase significantly sequentially" in Q4, affecting iPhone, Mac, and iPad production due to demand for advanced SoCs outstripping forecasts.
2. Rising memory costs, described as a "100-year flood," are pressuring gross margins, with costs expected to be even higher in the next quarter.
3. Foreign exchange is a growing headwind, expected to negatively impact the Q4 year-over-year growth rate by an additional 2.5 percentage points sequentially.
rows.key_quote: The root cause is a demand forecast issue, where the iPhone and Mac are doing remarkably better than we thought they would do.

rows.positive_highlights:
Adjusted EBITDA grew 33% YoY with margin expansion of 240 bps, driven by strong execution, favorable program mix, and program risk retirement.
Organic revenue growth accelerated to 10% with a book-to-bill ratio of 1.2x, leading to a record funded backlog.
Full-year profit guidance was raised, and the company announced the strategic acquisition of RAFT to expand into multi-domain AI and mission software.
rows.negative_highlights:
Full-year revenue guidance was maintained, not raised, with second-half performance contingent on material receipts and milestone achievement.
Full-year CapEx is expected to be elevated in the mid-4% range of revenue, impacting free cash flow conversion.
Management expects a continuing resolution to govern the federal budget in Q4, which introduces macro uncertainty despite their stated confidence.
rows.key_quote: Execution, favorable program mix, and the retirement of program risk, were the linchpins of our success.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong YTD financial performance driven by regulatory decisions and lower interest expense, leading to reaffirmation of 2026 EPS guidance ($5.90-$6.20) and long-term 5-7% growth.
2. Significant wildfire mitigation progress, with ~90% of distribution lines in high-risk areas hardened, including nearly 7,200 miles of covered conductor.
3. Successfully completed a ~$2B Woolsey Fire cost recovery securitization and crossed the $1B threshold in Eaton Fire payments to access the state Wildfire Fund.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Massive uncertainty surrounding California legislative wildfire reform, which could lead to credit downgrades (utility is at BBB-) and significantly increase financing costs.
2. Inability to estimate a low-end for total Eaton Fire liability due to the high volume of potential claims (30,000+ in litigation) despite making over $775M in settlement offers.
3. Rating agencies have flagged that wildfire risks are increasingly impacting the broader California economy, complicating the political path to a favorable legislative solution.
rows.key_quote: A framework without sufficient predictability will increase Edison's financing costs, making SCE's investments for customers more expensive.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Remaining Performance Obligations (RPOs) of $17.14 billion, up 44% year-over-year, with 95% of the growth being organic, providing strong revenue visibility.
2. Exceptional performance in Electrical Construction, which grew revenue 24% while expanding operating margin by 210 basis points to an impressive 13.9%.
3. Consolidated revenue grew 19.8% (19.6% organically), driving a 35% increase in diluted EPS to a record $9.06 for the quarter.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Mechanical Construction operating margin declined 110 basis points to 12.5% due to a project mix shift towards lower-margin GMP and prime contractor roles.
2. Management expects a weaker-than-normal turnaround season for the Industrial Services segment in H2 2026 due to geopolitical factors requiring refiners to remain online.
3. Five newly announced acquisitions are expected to have a limited near-term EPS contribution due to acquisition-related intangible and backlog amortization.
rows.key_quote: Electrical Construction generated revenue growth of 24% year-over-year, while delivering an impressive operating margin of 13.9%.

rows.positive_highlights: Strong office leasing volume of 382,000 sq ft, reaching highest level since Q4 2021; Achieved 20th consecutive quarter of positive mark-to-market spreads on office leases at +17.8%; Commercial portfolio reached 94.9% leased, demonstrating strong demand.
rows.negative_highlights: Observation Deck NOI collapsed to $12.4M vs $24.1M YoY due to a 28.5% visitor decline; Full-year core FFO guidance was lowered significantly by $0.13 per share; Pass program visitor channel, a key source of traffic, saw a 45% year-to-date decline.
rows.key_quote: From 2024 year-to-date to 2026 year-to-date, we have seen a 45% decline in pass program visitors.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Exceptional Northern California performance with 6.5% blended rent growth, driven by limited supply and strong tech-sector demand.
2. Raised full-year Core FFO guidance by $0.20 at the midpoint, reflecting strong operational outperformance and a 70 bps increase in same-property NOI growth guidance.
3. Improving conditions in Seattle, which saw blended rent growth increase 340 basis points sequentially to 2.6% in Q2.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Southern California continues to lag with only 1.4% blended rent growth, tied to slower national economic trends and modest job growth.
2. Q3 guidance projects a $0.09 sequential decline in Core FFO per share from Q2, primarily due to seasonally higher operating expenses.
3. Disclosed an 'unusual' and costly settlement for a multi-year litigation dispute unrelated to RealPage.
rows.key_quote: ...a compelling supply-demand backdrop with limited housing deliveries and continued investments across the Bay Area from the technology sector propelling demand.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Delivered strong EPS growth of 10.3% ($0.43 vs $0.39 YoY) driven by rate recovery, leading to a reaffirmation of full-year guidance. 2) Proactively advancing tangible solutions to grid strain, including a new 500 MW battery storage project in New Jersey. 3) Successfully filtered speculative data center demand, solidifying an 11 GW high-probability growth queue backed by $1 billion in collateral via new Transmission Security Agreements.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Severe strain on the PJM grid, with record demand, emergency procedures, and a capacity auction that fell short of reliability needs by 6.8 GW. 2) Unprecedented weather challenges, with ComEd experiencing 16 major weather events, the most in over two decades, increasing operational stress and costs. 3) Regulatory uncertainty in Pennsylvania following the withdrawal of the PECO rate case due to affordability concerns from the governor's office.
rows.key_quote: The July heat event, auction results, and market price signals all point to the same conclusion: demand is growing faster than supply.

rows.positive_highlights: Pro sales outperformed the company, growing approximately 4% and accounting for 55% of total sales. Adjusted EPS of $0.58 was flat YoY, beating expectations despite a -2.1% comp. Comparable store sales showed significant sequential improvement, moving from a -5.1% decline in April to -0.3% in June.
rows.negative_highlights: Comparable store sales declined 2.1%, driven by softness in large discretionary projects. The laminate and vinyl category faces pressure from industry oversupply, which is expected to continue into 2027. Adjusted gross margin for the quarter decreased by 20 basis points year-over-year to 43.7%.
rows.key_quote: Sales to pros continued to outperform the company and grew approximately 4% from the same period last year, accounting for about 55% of sales.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Significant margin expansion, with adjusted EBITDA margin up 250 bps sequentially to 14.3%, driven by improved job mix and operational leverage. 2. Strong growth in Technical Services, particularly ThruTubing Solutions' downhole tools which grew revenues 10% sequentially on technology adoption. 3. Cudd Pressure Control revenue increased 8% sequentially, led by a 14% increase in snubbing and 6% in coiled tubing.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Pintail wireline revenues fell 16% sequentially due to aggressive competitor pricing and customer activity reductions. 2. Pressure pumping revenues declined 1% and management sees no meaningful pricing upside without a significant activity increase. 3. The overall market remains subdued, leading management to be cautious on near-term activity levels and customer investment uncertainty.
rows.key_quote: Our downhole tools business is benefiting from more complex and longer laterals that are well suited for our technology solutions.

rows.positive_highlights: AFFO per share rose by $0.01 YoY for both Q2 and the six-month period. Realized a $3.6 million gain on a property sale to a solar developer. The low end of full-year AFFO guidance was raised.
rows.negative_highlights: Net income declined significantly to $3.1M from $7.8M YoY due to fewer asset sales. Management noted tenant financial conditions are 'not ideal,' delaying lease renewals and expecting flat rents. Management described the California agriculture market as being in a 'terrible, terrible spot.'
rows.key_quote: We have held back...pushing lease renewals...because financial conditions are not ideal to say the least, among our tenants.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Revenue up 29% QoQ to $100 million, driven by a realized price increase to $69/BOE from $55/BOE in Q1. 2. Gross drilling activity surged 35% QoQ with 300 wells, supporting back-half production growth. 3. Well productivity improved significantly, up 30% YoY in Canada and 15% YoY in the U.S., enhancing asset value.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Permian gas faced negative pricing for most of Q2 due to infrastructure constraints at the Waha Hub. 2. Production growth from recent drilling is delayed, with contributions not expected until late 2026 and into 2027. 3. Management remains cautious on increasing shareholder returns (dividends/buybacks), prioritizing debt repayment and M&A flexibility despite a low 57% payout ratio.
rows.key_quote: In Canada, well productivity was up about 30% year over year, and in the U.S., it's about 15%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong pricing outperformance with full-year expectations raised to over 6%, driving top-line beat.
2. Significant underlying margin expansion of 125 basis points year-over-year, absorbing major headwinds from fuel costs and M&A.
3. Full-year guidance raised across the board for the second time, with adjusted EBITDA growth projected at over 15% and adjusted FCF at nearly 20% before the SECURE acquisition.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Volume weakness persists, particularly in C&D and special waste landfill, with tons down 10% in the quarter due to macro headwinds.
2. A significant rise in diesel prices (up nearly 60% YoY) acted as a major margin headwind due to the lag in fuel surcharge recovery mechanisms.
3. Negative FX translation from a weakening Canadian dollar increased reported net leverage by approximately 10-15 basis points.
rows.key_quote: Continued price strength together with higher surcharge revenue... more than offset the anticipated headwinds from volume and commodity prices.

rows.positive_highlights:
Net new orders increased 19% year-over-year to 1,079, driven by a 10% increase in sales pace to 3.3 per month per community.
Homebuilding gross margin was 29.8%, stated to be the highest among homebuilding peers, supported by a disciplined land ownership strategy.
Financial services segment revenue grew to $12 million from $6.3 million year-over-year, with mortgage loans funded up 257%.
rows.negative_highlights:
Home closings revenue declined 11.4% to $472 million due to a mix shift toward the lower-priced Trophy Signature Homes brand.
Diluted EPS decreased 8% year-over-year to $1.70 per share.
Backlog value decreased 24% year-over-year to $387 million, with the average sales price in backlog down 18% to $569,000.
rows.key_quote: The growth in orders was driven primarily by Trophy Signature Homes as we continue to see strong demand for affordable homes.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. EPS grew over 8% to $1.61, driven by rate increases from capital recovery while O&M costs remained flat year-over-year.
2. Successfully closed the Nexus Water Group acquisition ahead of schedule, adding 47,000 customers, with another 57,000 connections under agreement.
3. Advanced regulatory strategy with successful rate cases in 3 states and secured approvals in 3 states for the pending Essential Utilities merger.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. The Pennsylvania rate case approved a $75 million annualized revenue increase, significantly below the $160 million increase originally requested by the company.
2. Analyst questions highlighted concerns over affordability and political intervention in Pennsylvania, which could pose future regulatory challenges.
3. Only ~40% of Pennsylvania CapEx is currently recoverable under the faster DSIC mechanism, limiting interim recovery and lagging the ~90% eligibility in the electric sector.
rows.key_quote: Revenues were higher due to authorized rate increases...importantly, O&M costs were flat period over period, highlighting our continued focus on cost control.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Shipbuilding Revenue Growth & Guidance Raise: Shipbuilding sales grew 15.7% YoY, leading to a raise in full-year revenue guidance to $10.2-$10.4 billion.
2. Major Submarine Contract Wins: Secured approximately $25 billion in contracts for Virginia Class Block VI and Columbia submarine programs, ensuring long-term stability.
3. Operational Throughput Improvement: Achieved a 12% improvement in shipbuilding throughput year-to-date, on track to meet the full-year goal of 15%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Mission Technologies Revenue Decline: The segment's revenue decreased 3.9% YoY to $760 million, though this was against a tough prior-year comp.
2. Negative Free Cash Flow: Reported negative free cash flow of -$150 million ($31M used in ops + $119M capex) due to timing of receipts, though full-year guidance was reiterated.
3. Slow Hiring Start at Ingalls: Ingalls shipyard experienced a slow start to the year in labor growth and hiring, though trends are now positive post-union agreement.
rows.key_quote: our second quarter results which reflect our continued focus and progress on increasing throughput.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Underlying demand was 2 points stronger than scanner data indicated, driven by non-measured channels. 
2. Price elasticities are performing better than expected, showing consumer resilience. 
3. Management has good visibility into cocoa deflation for 2027, supporting confidence in long-term targets.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Salty snacks division faced supply chain challenges, particularly for Dots, leading to higher logistics costs and margin pressure. 
2. Full-year gross margin guidance was slightly lowered to 'just below 400 bps' expansion due to the salty snacks issues. 
3. Management acknowledged tough second-half comps due to last year's major innovation and competitive innovation driving some share loss year-to-date.
rows.key_quote: U.S. confection retail consumption of about 3% understated our real demand by about 2 points, primarily due to the nonmeasured channel growth.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record leasing of 5.4 million sq. ft. at 35% leasing spreads, resolving two major vacancies and increasing portfolio occupancy to 99%.
2. De-risked balance sheet by refinancing $1.6B of debt, resulting in 100% fixed-rate consolidated debt with no maturities until 2029.
3. Raised full-year normalized FFO guidance to $1.31-$1.39/share and doubled the quarterly dividend to $0.10/share, signaling strong confidence.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Leverage remains elevated, with a net debt to total assets ratio of 69.2% and a net debt to EBITDAre ratio of 11.5x.
2. Q2 Same Property Cash NOI growth was only 2%, negatively impacted by a one-time bad debt reserve for a tenant in Hawaii.
3. The major 2.2 million sq. ft. Hawaii lease includes a 3-year free rent period, delaying significant cash flow recognition from the deal until mid-2029.
rows.key_quote: These results were driven by a record leasing quarter in which we completed 5.4 million square feet at leasing spreads of 35%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Significant Margin Expansion: Gross margin improved by 400 basis points YoY to 64.1%, driven by manufacturing efficiencies and the G7 15-day system transition.
2. Strong Patient Growth: Global new customer starts remained at record levels, with a sequential uptick in the U.S. driven by share gains and broader access.
3. Positive CONNECT Trial Data: The trial showed a major A1C reduction in non-insulin Type 2 users, strengthening the case for expanded CMS coverage.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Foreign Exchange Headwind: Guidance includes an expected $15 million negative impact to international revenue in the second half of the year due to currency movements.
2. Toughening International Comps: Management acknowledged that year-over-year comparisons for the international business become more difficult in Q3 and Q4.
3. Upcoming Ireland Factory Costs: The ramp-up of the new Ireland facility in Q3 will add hiring and depreciation costs, creating a near-term headwind for gross margin.
rows.key_quote: This improvement was driven by continued manufacturing efficiencies in quality management, and a benefit from the initial customer switch over to G7 15-day.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Returned to profitability after 7 quarters, two quarters ahead of schedule, with KRW 204B operating income, driven by strong battery sales and AMPC benefits.
2. Surging demand for high-power batteries (UPS, BBU) from AI data center expansion, with projected YoY sales growth of over 70% in this category.
3. Strong momentum in US ESS market, with LFP battery order intake covering capacity through 2029, prompting capacity expansion reviews.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. US EV market demand slowdown is projected to continue in the near term due to elimination of consumer incentives and OEM strategy shifts.
2. While narrowing, losses in the EV battery segment remain a risk due to potential volume declines in certain existing projects.
3. High-power cylindrical battery production lines are running at full capacity, indicating a potential near-term bottleneck in meeting surging demand.
rows.key_quote: Battery business revenue grew, driven by expanded sales of high-power products like UPS/BBU for AI data centers and EV batteries for Europe.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. North American box volumes grew 1.7% year-over-year on a daily basis, outperforming the market. 
2. Mill performance improved by 500 basis points year-over-year due to reliability initiatives. 
3. Strategic projects advanced, with the Riverdale machine conversion completed on time and the NORPAC acquisition finalized.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. The expected negative impact from macro headwinds (inflation in freight, OCC, diesel) for H2 increased threefold to $150 million. 
2. The Pine Hill mill was shut down for repairs, forecasting an $85 million negative EBITDA impact in Q3. 
3. The second-half demand outlook was lowered from modest growth to stable due to concerns over inflation and consumer affordability.
rows.key_quote: We have reduced the top end of the range by approximately $50 million, primarily based on the macro environment and the prolonged Middle East conflict.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Broad-based commercial strength: Dupixent global sales grew 38% to $6B, EYLEA HD U.S. sales grew 52% to $596M (exceeding standard EYLEA for the first time), and Libtayo global sales grew 29% to nearly $500M.
2. Sanofi collaboration economics improving: The $3.1B Sanofi development balance is now fully repaid, meaning Regeneron will record its full share of collaboration profits starting Q3, significantly boosting reported revenue from the partnership.
3. Strong EYLEA HD momentum: U.S. physician unit demand for EYLEA HD increased 24% sequentially, and it now comprises ~60% of franchise net sales, demonstrating successful conversion and market share gains.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Standard EYLEA decline: EYLEA U.S. net sales declined 45% YoY to $412M, driven by conversion to EYLEA HD and competition. Management expects sequential quarterly demand declines in the low to mid-teens for the rest of 2026 due to upcoming biosimilar launches.
2. EYLEA HD prefilled syringe delay: The expected approval of the EYLEA HD prefilled syringe by the end of Q2 did not occur, with management now guiding for potential approval "before the end of the year."
3. Manufacturing interruption impact: GAAP gross margin was negatively impacted by unabsorbed costs from a "temporary interruption in bulk manufacturing production" at the Limerick, Ireland facility, though production has since resumed.
rows.key_quote: Dupixent, EYLEA HD and Libtayo all set new all-time highs for quarterly net sales and are carrying strong momentum into the second half.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Q2 results with 8% organic sales growth and 19% adjusted EPS growth, significantly boosted by an estimated $0.25 EPS benefit from customer pre-buys. 2. Solutions Group adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 150 bps year-over-year, driven by productivity initiatives and strong low-double-digit growth in the Embelex platform. 3. Company generated robust adjusted free cash flow of $365 million and returned over $210 million to shareholders via dividends and accelerated share repurchases.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. A major Q2 customer inventory stocking cycle is expected to reverse, creating a significant ~$0.50 sequential EPS headwind from Q2 to Q3. 2. Intelligent Labels platform growth was modest at low-single-digits, dragged down by double-digit declines in the logistics segment due to lapping tough prior-year comparisons. 3. Full-year organic growth guidance of 3-4% implies a significant slowdown in H2 as the inventory destocking impacts results.
rows.key_quote: We estimate that roughly half of the organic growth was from customer pre-watch activity.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Guidance Upgrade: Raised full-year guidance for sales (to 8-10%), EBIT (to 10-12%), and EPS (to 11-13%) growth.
2. Record Orders and Backlog: Secured GBP 16.4 billion in orders, pushing the backlog to a record GBP 84 billion, ensuring long-term visibility.
3. Strong European and Space Growth: Sales grew 30% in Europe, driven by Hägglunds and Bofors, while the Space business grew 29%, far outpacing the group average.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Maritime Margin Pressure: Maritime return on sales was low at 6.1%, constrained by early-stage, first-in-class programs, though improvement is expected.
2. Cash Flow Quality: H1 free cash flow of GBP 1.8 billion was heavily reliant on GBP 1.6 billion in customer advances, which are expected to partially unwind.
3. Lagging Segment Growth: The Cyber & Intelligence sector grew by only 3%, significantly underperforming other key segments like P&S (+12%) and Air (+11%).
rows.key_quote: P&S grew by 12%, featuring nearly 30% growth from Hägglunds and Bofors on sales to Europe.

rows.positive_highlights:
Structural margin improvement plan to reduce cash costs by over 25% by year-end 2028, adding $300 million in annual margin from expiring contracts and transport optimization.
Record quarterly production of 4.1 Bcfe/d (+21% YoY) and a 57% increase in adjusted EBITDA, driven by strong NGL prices, acquisitions, and lower operating costs.
Successful return to dry gas drilling after 12 years, with initial pad results showing a 67% improvement in EUR and a 28% decrease in cost per foot.
rows.negative_highlights:
Henry Hub natural gas prices declined 16% year-over-year, providing a headwind to overall gas price realizations.
Cost reduction plan will be partially offset by a projected $0.35/Mcfe decrease in price realizations as sales shift to more in-basin contracts.
Elevated VLGC freight rates due to geopolitical events are creating some headwinds for U.S. LPG exports, though new vessel builds are expected to provide relief.
rows.key_quote: ...the impact of increased scale, product diversity and lower cash operating expense led to our adjusted EBITDA increasing 57% over that period.

rows.positive_highlights:
Back-up Care revenue growth accelerated to 19% year-over-year, driven by strong growth in unique users and frequency, leading to an increased full-year segment growth forecast of 13-15%.
Adjusted EPS grew 20% to $1.28, exceeding expectations and prompting a raise in the full-year guidance to $5.05-$5.15 per share.
Consolidated adjusted operating margin expanded 95 basis points to 12.7%, with margin improvement in both the Full Service (+50 bps) and Back-up Care (+80 bps) segments.
rows.negative_highlights:
The Full Service segment continues to face a ~100 basis point revenue growth headwind from enrollment contraction in its Australian operations.
Strategic center closures are creating a drag on Full Service revenue, amounting to an expected headwind of ~200 basis points for the full year and 225 basis points in Q3.
Educational Advisory revenue was flat year-over-year, as growth in College Coach was offset by lower participant engagement in the EdAssist business.
rows.key_quote: Usage growth was strong across care types and was largely driven by more unique users, as well as an uptick in frequency of use.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. AWS revenue growth accelerated for the 5th straight quarter to 36.7% YoY, reaching a $169B annualized run rate.
2. Both the AI and custom chips businesses are now over a $25B annual revenue run rate, growing at triple-digit percentages YoY.
3. AWS backlog grew triple-digits YoY to $496 billion, reflecting massive future demand.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Raised 2026 cash CapEx forecast from ~$200B to ~$220B, driven by higher memory costs and supply chain inflation.
2. Management stated that even with increased investment, they "will still not have enough capacity to meet all the demand we have in 2026...and also be true in 2027."
3. Q3 guidance implies a sequential deceleration in revenue, primarily due to the timing shift of Prime Day from Q3'25 to Q2'26.
rows.key_quote: Our AI revenue run rate... is now also over $25 billion, growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.

rows.positive_highlights:
Same-store sales grew 6.5% driven by exceptionally strong 8.3% traffic growth, which significantly outperformed casual dining benchmarks by over 9 points.
Restaurant-level operating margins expanded 20 bps to 17.2% despite a 120 bps headwind from food inflation, thanks to a 90 bps improvement in labor costs.
Full-year guidance was raised for comp sales (to 3-4%), restaurant-level profit (to $228M-$235M), and Adjusted EBITDA (to $145M-$152M).
rows.negative_highlights:
Average check compressed by 1.8%, driven by promotional activity and high incidence of trial-driving items like the seasonal Pizookie.
Cost of sales increased 70 bps year-over-year due to ~5% commodity inflation, led by a 20% increase in beef costs.
General and administrative costs increased 90 bps, partly due to a $1.5 million expense related to a deferred compensation program liability.
rows.key_quote: Same-store sales increased 6.5%, driven by 8.3% traffic growth, continuing to significantly outperform Black Box casual dining benchmarks.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong revenue growth: Total revenue up 10% to $796M, driven by Affordable Medicines (+13%) and Specialty (+17%) with new launches contributing $45M. 2. Raised full-year guidance: Revenue outlook increased by $50M and EPS by $0.01, incorporating strong performance and a $12M annual interest expense reduction. 3. Strategic pipeline momentum: Strong uptake for CREXONT and BREKIYA, near-term launch expected for lanreotide, and the pending Kashiv acquisition creating a powerful biosimilar platform.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. India facility flood: A manufacturing site was impacted by severe flooding, resulting in an anticipated negative financial impact of $20M. 2. AvKARE segment decline: Revenue decreased 4% to $157M as growth in the government channel was offset by a decline in the low-margin distribution business. 3. Increased capital expenditures: CapEx guidance was raised by ~$40M to $150M to fund expansion for Women's Health and injectable products.
rows.key_quote: Affordable Medicines revenue up 13% to $490M, reflecting strength in Women's Health products, injectables and higher naloxone sales.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. 45Z Credit Value Uplift: Treasury's refined carbon intensity calculations increased annual monetization value to ~$40 million, leading to a targeted ~$90 million annual run rate combined with other environmental attributes.
2. Strong Operational Execution: Set 24-hour drilling records in the Utica, maintained stable well costs (~$1.7K/ft), and confirmed new Utica wells are performing as top-tier assets in the basin.
3. Confident Capital Allocation: Actively repurchasing shares, viewing the weak gas market as an opportunity, and expressing a bullish long-term outlook for Appalachian gas.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Weak Near-Term Gas Market: Management acknowledged the macro environment is soft, stating '2026 going into 2027 setting up to be a little bit soft.'
2. Lumpy Quarterly Cadence: Capital spending and production are not linear, with Q2 spending below expectations and a significant production 'surge' expected in Q4, creating analyst uncertainty.
3. No Immediate 45Z Expansion: Management is evaluating opportunities but has 'nothing definitive' planned for expanding the carbon capture system in 2026.
rows.key_quote: Treasury refined its carbon intensity calculations...which raised the value of our annual monetization to approximately $40 million a year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Reached an all-time high in paid Coinbase One subscribers, demonstrating strong engagement and recurring revenue growth despite a 'down market'.
2. Successful revenue diversification, with Bitcoin transactions falling to 12% of the total business, driven by new products like perpetual futures and prediction markets.
3. The 'Base' L2 network established a leadership position, becoming #1 in stablecoin volume (approx. $32 trillion in the last 12 months) and dominating early Agentic Finance activity.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Operated in a 'down market' with declining crypto trading volumes during the quarter, creating a headwind for the core transaction business.
2. Experienced several departures from the senior leadership team, raising questions from analysts about strategic continuity.
3. Faces a fragmenting competitive landscape with new L2s being launched by competitors like Robinhood, posing a potential long-term threat to Base's market share.
rows.key_quote: We saw crypto trading volumes down, but growth in Coinbase 1 memberships.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Adjusted EBITDA grew 30% YoY to $92M, driven by Lithium (EBITDA up from $3M to $31M) and Vanadium (EBITDA more than doubled).
2. Raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $230M-$250M (from $210M-$240M) on strong performance and favorable markets.
3. Acquired Zinnwald Lithium, opened a new US chrome facility, and strengthened the balance sheet with over $400M in cash post-quarter-end.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. AMG Technologies segment EBITDA fell to $27M from $53M YoY due to lapping an exceptionally strong Antimony performance in the prior year.
2. Management guided for a 'significantly down sequentially' Q3, as Q2 benefited from favorable, non-recurring phasing effects in Lithium and Vanadium.
3. Tax expense increased to $19M from $7M YoY, and cash tax payments were high at $30M, largely related to prior-year high Antimony profitability.
rows.key_quote: This is primarily due to the increasingly strong profitability from our vanadium and lithium segments, both of which benefited from significant phasing effects.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong International Growth: International business, representing over 40% of sales, grew 9% year-over-year, led by LAAP (+13%) and Europe direct (low double-digit %).
2. Significant Tariff Refund: Recognized ~$78M in IEEPA tariff refunds, boosting reported Q2 gross margin to 58.3% and leading to a raised full-year EPS guidance.
3. Encouraging Spring 2027 Order Book: Initial orders indicate low-to-mid single-digit percentage growth, with broad-based contributions from all brands, including a rebound in the U.S. and strong footwear performance.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. U.S. Market Weakness: U.S. net sales declined 4%, driven by a high single-digit % drop in wholesale and soft traffic in DTC stores requiring higher discounts.
2. Second-Half Shipment Shift: Expects a meaningful shift of fall shipments from Q3 to Q4 due to supply chain disruptions, creating greater risk by back-weighting the year.
3. Macroeconomic Headwinds: Management cited a 'more challenging' operating environment, with inflationary pressures impacting consumer discretionary spending, particularly in the U.S.
rows.key_quote: We now anticipate meaningful shifts in the timing of fall 2026 shipments from the third quarter to the fourth due to longer logistics lead time.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record SAO segment adjusted operating margin of 37.8%, up from 35.6% sequentially and 30.5% YoY, driving record company operating income. 
2. Raised FY27 operating income guidance by 21-25% over record FY26 results, with management suggesting this is a 'floor'. 
3. Strong Aerospace & Defense demand with sales up 17% YoY, driven by accelerating OEM build rates and strong customer demand for more material.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Medical end-use market sales were down 30% year-over-year, despite a slight sequential recovery. 
2. Energy end-use market sales declined 22% sequentially and 12% YoY due to order timing and production scheduling. 
3. Q1 FY27 operating income is guided to be sequentially lower ($195M-$200M vs $206.9M) due to seasonally elevated preventative maintenance.
rows.key_quote: The profitability was driven by the SAO segment, which delivered an adjusted operating margin of 37.8% in the quarter, another new record.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Adjusted EBITDA of $289M driven by a ~20% YoY increase in gathering volumes to 4.1 Bcf/day from the successful integration of HG Midstream assets.
2. Balance sheet significantly strengthened, with leverage reduced to 2.8x (below 3.0x target) following a $370M legal settlement payment, enabling the company to call its 2028 debt maturities.
3. Announced a major new growth project, the 'Eastside Express' pipeline ($200-$300M investment), to capitalize on a multi-billion dollar pipeline of regional infrastructure opportunities fueled by new power plant demand.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Disparity in growth rates, with Adjusted EBITDA growing only 2% year-over-year while gathering volumes grew by nearly 20%, indicating potential margin dilution from newly acquired assets.
2. Antero Resources plans to use minor production curtailments (~50 million a day) to manage gas prices, which will have a small negative impact on AM's throughput.
3. The company is increasing its capital intensity with the new $200-$300M East Side Express project, representing a significant multi-year spend.
rows.key_quote: we view this project as step 1 in positioning Antero Midstream to capture the incremental production needed to fulfill the visible demand growth.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong market fundamentals: Group 3 crack spreads nearly doubled YoY to average $44.91/barrel. 2. Excellent operational uptime: Crude utilization was 98% and ammonia plant utilization was 99%, driving high throughput. 3. Fertilizer segment strength: Adjusted EBITDA grew to $107 million from $67 million YoY with a strong demand book for H2.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Massive RINs expense: RINs cost $216 million, or $11.16/barrel, reducing the capture rate by ~25%. 2. Significant hedging losses: Realized derivative losses from crack spread swaps totaled $81 million. 3. Regulatory uncertainty: Management cited EPA's delinquency on SRE petitions and unmanageable RFS mandates as major headwinds.
rows.key_quote: RIN expense for the quarter... $216 million or $11.16 per barrel which negatively impacted our capture rate by approximately 25%.

rows.positive_highlights: Favorable California GRC decision resulted in recognizing $15.3M in retroactive IRMA revenue and secured a $1.45B capital plan. Invested a record $270M in H1, contributing to a ~12% compound annual rate base growth. Reached a full settlement in its Washington rate case, securing a 10.18% ROE and a $4.12M revenue increase.
rows.negative_highlights: Higher per-unit water supply costs of $6.3 million partially offset revenue gains. Incurred $7.9 million in costs related to the recognition of deferred RAM revenue. Experienced $7 million in higher income taxes due to higher pre-tax income and an increased effective tax rate.
rows.key_quote: The primary earnings drivers included $15.3 million of IRMA revenue related to the delayed 2024 California GRC, and...$15 million due to rate changes.

rows.positive_highlights:
Raised full-year Core FFO and AFFO per share guidance, driven by strong operations and the accretive repurchase of $600M in stock.
New lease rate growth accelerated for six consecutive months through June, and July renewal rent growth accelerated to 4.3%, indicating strong demand.
Legislative clarity from the ROAD to Housing Act has removed market uncertainty, and the supply backdrop is improving with slowing new supply growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
Same Store NOI grew a modest 1.5% as core operating expense growth of 1.9% slightly outpaced core revenue growth of 1.6%.
The contribution from the ResiBuilt development platform is expected to fall behind original expectations for 2026 due to project delays from prior legislative uncertainty.
New lease growth (1.2% in July) remains soft in certain Sunbelt markets like Florida and Phoenix due to lingering, though easing, supply pressures.
rows.key_quote: That is a significant discount compared to our year-to-date actual average sale price of $450,000 per home.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Adjusted EBITDA grew 5% to $293M, and full-year EBITDA guidance was reiterated, supported by strong cost discipline and margin expansion.
2. Tour flow grew 6%, with new buyer tours up at a high single-digit rate, indicating healthy underlying consumer demand.
3. Returned $150M to shareholders via share repurchases and closed a non-core asset disposition to reduce future costs.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Contract sales declined 3% to $810M, missing expectations, and full-year sales guidance was lowered.
2. VPG (Volume Per Guest) fell 9% to ~$3,400, driven by tough comps at Bluegreen and significant sales execution failures in Orlando and Myrtle Beach.
3. Q3 is expected to remain weak, with guidance for a mid-single-digit decline in contract sales and a high-single-digit decline in VPG.
rows.key_quote: Contract sales declined, reflecting faster than predicted VPG moderation at Bluegreen and sales execution that fell short of our expectations.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Transformative acquisition of Yapi Kredi Portfoy in Turkey, creating the #2 asset manager in the country with EUR 29B in combined AUM and projecting EUR 65M-75M in 2026 pro forma net income.
2. Net inflow guidance for the full year massively upgraded from EUR 10B to over EUR 35B, driven by M&A and strong organic momentum (EUR 8.1B inflows in H1).
3. Strong capital return program, highlighted by the launch of a new EUR 250 million share buyback tranche.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. A EUR 25 million "extraordinary nonrecurring write-off" on two proprietary venture capital investments impacted reported H1 net profit.
2. Temporary margin dilution in the global business due to the ongoing integration of the recently acquired NSI platform in the U.S.
