3. Management noted that market volatility could affect client risk propensity in H2, leading to a conservative stance on the organic portion of the inflow guidance.
rows.key_quote: Combining Yapi Kredi and Azimut Portfoy, we are creating a EUR 29 billion national champion... the second largest asset manager in the country.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Achieved record Q2 revenues, up 5.3% YoY, led by CorpFin, Tech, and FLC segments. 2) The Economics (Econ) segment showed strong sequential improvement exceeding expectations and is now forecasted to grow YoY in H2 2026. 3) CorpFin's Transformation practice grew 26% YoY, and the Technology segment saw an 18.4% revenue increase from M&A-related second request services.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Lowered full-year EPS guidance due to the Q2 earnings miss and an expected $70 million YoY increase in SG&A, including extraordinary litigation costs. 2) Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 10.5% from 11.8% YoY as revenue growth was offset by higher direct costs (talent investments) and SG&A. 3) Revenue performance was below internal expectations due to short-term project timing gaps in the U.K. and persistent geopolitical disruption in the Middle East.
rows.key_quote: When the revenue in a given quarter happens to not quite meet those aspirations...the shortfall versus expectations ends up going through to the bottom line.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. FFO grew 10% year-over-year to $702 million, driven by broad-based strength across segments. 2. The Data segment's FFO surged by 36%, propelled by contributions from a new U.S. fiber network and the Intel foundry partnership. 3. Generated nearly $1.2 billion in proceeds from asset sales in 2026, primarily through the successful IPO of its U.S. data center operation.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Growth was partially offset by foregone earnings from asset sales, including regulated businesses in Brazil and Mexico and a U.S. gas pipeline. 2. Management acknowledged growing "NIMBYism" and pushback against data center development in the U.S. and Europe, a potential future headwind. 3. Transport and utility segment growth was muted by the impact of multiple partial and full asset sales over the last year.
rows.key_quote: Growth was driven by inflation-linked rate increases, strong Transport and Midstream activity, and commissioning of new capital projects in our Data segment.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. DRPF flotation project was completed on time and on budget ($500M), has successfully produced 69% Fe material, and first contracts are signed. 2. Plant demonstrated strong iron recovery of 79% during the commissioning and ramp-up phase. 3. Maintained strong liquidity of $653 million despite completing a major acquisition and final project CapEx.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Sales volumes (3.3M tonnes) significantly trailed production (3.9M tonnes) due to intentional DRPF product stockpiling and vessel diversions, leading to a large inventory build. 2. EBITDA was severely impacted, falling to $33 million, primarily due to lower sales volumes against fixed costs. 3. C3 freight index rose 37% QoQ due to Middle East conflict, increasing costs and pressuring margins.
rows.key_quote: we have been stockpiling some material of the higher grade... to be able to watch our first cargo that will start loading in the next few weeks.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Favorable Loss Development: Realized a $43 million favorable loss reserve development due to better-than-expected cure activity on prior delinquencies, significantly boosting net income. 2. Strong Capital Returns: Repurchased $177 million in stock and increased the quarterly dividend to $0.17/share, signaling strong confidence and returning 124% of net income over the prior four quarters. 3. Expense Guidance Improvement: Lowered the forecast for full-year operating expenses to the low end of the prior $190-$200 million range, indicating successful cost discipline.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Ongoing Yield Compression: The in-force premium yield continued to decline, reaching 38 basis points, with management expecting this downward trend to persist. 2. Constrained Market Growth: Management highlighted that stretched housing affordability and high interest rates are limiting growth in the overall insurance-in-force portfolio, which grew only 2.6% YoY. 3. Normalizing Credit: The delinquency rate increased 16 basis points year-over-year to 2.37%, reflecting a continued, albeit slow, credit normalization from historical lows.
rows.key_quote: This favorable development primarily reflects better than expected cure activity on delinquency notices received in 2025.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Data Center segment revenue grew 90% YoY driven by strong demand from hyperscale and colocation customers. 
2. The company recorded its third consecutive quarter of record order intake, substantially increasing the backlog. 
3. Adjusted EPS grew 44% to $1.53, benefiting from strong revenue growth and a favorable tax item.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Consolidated gross margin declined 340 basis points to 20.8% due to issues across all segments. 
2. Data Center margins were negatively impacted by 450-550 basis points due to production inefficiencies from supply chain shortages. 
3. Free cash flow was slightly negative, impacted by higher capex and cash payments for restructuring and the pending spin-off.
rows.key_quote: The excess labor along with unfavorable overhead absorption... had a 450 to 550 basis point impact on margins during the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Surging by-product credits: Sulfuric acid contracts for Q3 were priced at $840/tonne, up 80% from the Q2 average of $465/tonne, providing a major margin tailwind. 2. Record zinc production: The Kipushi mine produced a record of over 70,000 tonnes of zinc in Q2 at a low cash cost of $0.90/lb. 3. Strong commodity pricing: The company realized a high copper price of $5.99/lb, which buoyed revenue despite operational challenges.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Significant cost inflation: C1 cash costs at Kamoa-Kakula rose to $2.84/lb, with an $0.18/lb increase quarter-over-quarter driven primarily by higher diesel prices. 2. Slower underground development: Dewatering issues at the Kakula mine have slowed development rates, delaying access to certain high-grade areas and impacting the near-term grade profile. 3. Logistical bottlenecks: Kipushi experienced a 14,000-tonne build-up of finished zinc inventory due to a shortage of trucks for transport to port, deferring sales.
rows.key_quote: Quarter 3, the 2026 contracts priced at 80% higher than quarter 2 at approximately $840 per tonne.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Rio Grande LNG Phase 1 construction is ahead of schedule, with Trains 1 and 2 now 74% complete and over 6,000 workers on-site, de-risking the path to first LNG in H1 2027.
2. Successfully refinanced ~$4.6 billion of project debt via a heavily oversubscribed $3.5B notes offering and a $1B term loan, improving the debt maturity profile and freeing up bank capacity for future expansion.
3. Gained clarity on the Train 6 expansion timeline with FERC setting a June 2027 date for the final Environmental Impact Statement, supporting a Final Investment Decision (FID) in H2 2027.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Analyst raised concerns about labor competition on the US Gulf Coast, but management stated this is not an issue for its Rio Grande Valley site due to a unique local labor pool.
2. The company is taking delivery of LNG vessel charters ahead of first production, creating a timing mismatch, but is managing this by sub-chartering vessels.
3. The company has no significant negative operational or financial highlights to report; all construction progress was reported as on-budget and ahead of schedule.
rows.key_quote: The ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz has taken almost 20% of the world's LNG supply off the market.

Ranpak reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated net revenue up 12.2% constant currency (14% reported), with automation revenue surging 139% year-over-year constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 13.9% constant currency to $19.1 million, with gross margin up 150 bps year-over-year. Management reiterated full-year automation revenue target of ~$60 million and automation adjusted EBITDA breakeven by year-end, while noting macro uncertainty and a temporary European surcharge to offset input costs.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded over 600 basis points to 36.6%, driven by pricing, favorable mix, and operational execution.
2. The Performance Materials segment delivered exceptional 53.6% EBITDA margins, benefiting from a structural shift to higher-value carbon solutions for hybrid vehicles.
3. Full-year adjusted EBITDA and EPS guidance was raised, reflecting strong first-half performance and management's confidence in durable earnings power.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. The outlook for the second half is weaker due to expectations of lower auto production and planned maintenance outages in the Performance Materials segment.
2. The Pavement Technologies segment faced headwinds from high asphalt prices, which caused project delays in international markets like China and South America.
3. Reported sales declined 5% year-over-year due to the divestiture of the Road Markings product line.
rows.key_quote: We benefit from a structural shift to hybrid vehicles, which require our most advanced carbon solutions and contribute a higher-value product mix.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Diamond Green Diesel (DGD) delivered exceptional performance, contributing $389M in EBITDA to Darling's share on sales of 350M gallons at $2.23 EBITDA/gallon, including a $51M tariff recovery. 2) The Core Feed Ingredients segment saw EBITDA rise to $353M, driven by rallied fat prices from robust biofuel demand and strong protein prices from tight fish meal supplies. 3) The company significantly de-levered, using $280M in cash from DGD to reduce net debt by $223M, improving its leverage ratio to 2.3x.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Working capital increased at DGD due to a strategic build-up of feedstock inventory, tying up cash that could have been used for further debt reduction. 2) Analysts raised concerns about RIN market volatility, though management expressed confidence it would not be a significant issue. 3) The company increased its 2026 maintenance CapEx forecast to $450M, partly to catch up on spending that was pulled back in 2024-2025.
rows.key_quote: Feed Ingredients segment delivered improved results as fat prices rallied, fueled by robust demand from the biofuel sector.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Financials: Achieved record revenue of $187.9M (+8.1% YoY), record net income of $106M (+10% YoY), and record adjusted EPS of $1.38 (+14% YoY).
2. Portfolio Growth: Grew primary insurance in force to a record $227.1 billion, fueled by $16 billion in New Insurance Written (NIW) for the quarter.
3. Strong Credit Performance: Claims expense was low at $13.1M, and management cited favorable development due to a constructive macro environment, a strong labor market, and high borrower equity.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Anticipated Seasonal Default Increase: Management expects the default population to 'trend a bit higher' in the second half of 2026 due to normal seasonal patterns.
2. Regional Housing Weakness: Acknowledged 'degrees of pressure' in markets like Florida, Texas, and the Sun Belt, where housing inventories are building.
3. Slight Persistency Decline: 12-month persistency decreased slightly to 81.4% from 82.2% in the prior quarter.
rows.key_quote: We generated $16 billion of NIW volume, ending the period with a record $227.1 billion of high-quality, high-performing primary insurance in force.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Exceptional Expense Control: Same-store operating expense growth was only 0.8% YoY, driven by operational discipline, lower expected property taxes, and a favorable insurance renewal with a 12% premium reduction.
2. Strong Resident Retention and Renewal Growth: Renewal lease rates were a robust 5.2% for the quarter, coupled with a record-low turnover of 39.6%, providing a stable revenue base.
3. Highly Accretive Redevelopment Program: The interior renovation program is yielding an average cash-on-cash return of approximately 25%, significantly outperforming the 19% target.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Slow New Lease Rate Recovery: New lease pricing recovery was slower than anticipated, primarily due to high supply in certain markets and cautious consumer behavior, prompting a reduction in full-year revenue guidance.
2. Persistent Supply Pressure: High-concentration markets including Phoenix, Charlotte, Raleigh, and Savannah continue to face challenges from elevated new supply, weighing on pricing power despite strong underlying demand.
3. Challenged Lease-Up Assets: Lease-up communities in Charlotte remain challenged due to market-specific supply pressures, requiring concessions of eight to ten weeks on certain floor plans.
rows.key_quote: While underlying demand remains healthy, the pace of recovery in new lease pricing has been somewhat slower than assumed in our prior guidance.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Distributable earnings of $0.25/share covered the dividend, aided by improved core net interest income and a strong conduit business contribution. 2. Book value per share increased to $14.24 from $14.18, driven by the repurchase of $16 million in stock at an average price of $8.70. 3. Maintained a strong balance sheet with nearly $800 million in liquidity and low recourse leverage of 0.7x.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Management walked back NewPoint's full-year origination guidance due to the "higher-for-longer" interest rate environment slowing transaction volume. 2. The quarter's earnings beat was described as unsustainable, with management guiding future earnings back to a lower range. 3. The company still has $250 million of equity tied up in underperforming assets, which acts as a drag on overall earnings.
rows.key_quote: The watch-watch transactional volume in the multifamily sector slowed, as the bid-ask spread between buyers and sellers is very wide in the current rate environment.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. INGREZZA sales grew 15% YoY to a record $716M, driven by all-time highs in new patient starts, leading to a full-year guidance raise. 2. CRENESSITY sales reached $184M, demonstrating strong launch momentum with its prescriber base nearly tripling YoY. 3. Total revenue grew nearly 40% YoY, strengthened by the successful acquisition and integration of VYKAT XR, adding a third major growth asset.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. VYKAT XR pro forma sales of $94M were sequentially flat, with growth from new starts being offset by discontinuations from the initial launch bolus. 2. Management faces the strategic challenge of accelerating VYKAT XR's growth trajectory now that it is post-acquisition. 3. Future revenue for INGREZZA faces pressure from IRA price negotiations set to begin in 2029, creating long-term uncertainty.
rows.key_quote: INGREZZA second quarter net sales were $716 million, up 15% YoY, driven by another quarter of record new patient additions and sustained demand.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Successful completion of major turnarounds, with the El Dorado plant already achieving its highest daily production rates since 2016, positioning the company for higher production in H2.
2. Favorable market conditions driven by geopolitical supply disruptions (Strait of Hormuz) and high European natural gas prices ($19-$20/MMBtu), creating a structural cost advantage for US producers.
3. Strong financial performance despite downtime, with adjusted EBITDA increasing 40% YoY to $53 million; excluding a $35-40M turnaround impact, illustrative adjusted EBITDA was ~$90 million.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Q2 results were significantly impacted by planned turnaround activity at the El Dorado and Pryor facilities, which reduced adjusted EBITDA by an estimated $35 million to $40 million.
2. SG&A costs are trending higher than initial guidance, on track for $50-$55 million annually versus the expected $35-$40 million, driven by inflation and non-cash compensation.
3. Nitrogen product pricing has moderated from first-half highs, with Tampa ammonia settling at $635/metric ton for August, though prices remain historically elevated and are expected to rebound.
rows.key_quote: We are already seeing the benefits... with El Dorado achieving some of the highest daily production rates since we went into production in 2016.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong revenue and earnings growth: Enterprise revenue grew 5.8% and adjusted EPS grew 14.9%. 
2. Significant margin expansion: Adjusted operating margin improved 70 bps, with Diagnostics up 50 bps and Biopharma Laboratory Services (BLS) up 130 bps. 
3. Raised full-year guidance: Raised revenue and EPS guidance driven by strength in Central Labs and improved outlook for Early Development.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Lower Year-over-Year Free Cash Flow: FCF was $314M vs $543M in the prior year, attributed to working capital timing and higher capex. 
2. ACA Headwind: A minor headwind of 20-30 bps to diagnostic volume was noted from ACA plan changes, although this was anticipated. 
3. Competitive growth questions: An analyst highlighted that Diagnostics organic growth of 3.6% lagged a key peer, prompting a discussion of Labcorp's focus on profitable, higher-margin business.
rows.key_quote: BLS segment adjusted operating margin expanded 130 basis points, driven by organic growth and operating efficiencies from strategic actions in Early Development.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. North America returned to positive organic growth (+0.5%) for the first time in nine quarters, driven by 2% growth in aftermarket collision. 2. Alternative parts usage (APU) hit a new record of over 40%, indicating a favorable market trend. 3. The Specialty segment delivered resilient organic revenue growth of 4.5%, outperforming its market.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. A problematic ERP implementation in Germany caused an estimated $140 million revenue decline and a $50 million EBITDA hit. 2. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was cut to $2.60-$2.90 from $2.90-$3.20. 3. Europe's organic revenue declined 12.6%, compounded by softer demand and competitive pressures in the U.K. and Benelux.
rows.key_quote: Europe parts and services' organic revenue declined 12.6%. The primary driver was the disruption related to the ERP implementation in Germany.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Advisory revenue accelerated to 21% growth, with U.S. investment sales revenue up 53%, nearly double the market. 2. Adjusted EPS grew 61%, and full-year guidance was raised significantly to $24.60-$25.90. 3. Generated $438 million of free cash flow (+52% YoY), supporting $410 million in H1 share repurchases.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Elongated investment sales timelines in parts of Europe due to geopolitical uncertainty. 2. Muted growth in Investment Management advisory fees due to dispositions in Asia Pacific. 3. Higher commission expenses from producers reaching high tiers early acted as a temporary margin headwind.
rows.key_quote: U.S. investment sales revenue growth of 53% for the quarter was nearly double the broader market, reflecting our talent, platform and data advantages.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong EPS Growth: Non-GAAP EPS grew 25% to $0.50, primarily driven by improved margin from new rates implemented in Montana. 2. Merger Progress: Secured key regulatory approvals from FERC, Nebraska, and South Dakota for the Black Hills merger, with a final Montana decision expected in Q4 2026. 3. Data Center Advancement: Expects to sign Energy Service Agreements (ESAs) with two of three key data center developers by year-end, progressing a major growth opportunity.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Unrecovered Colstrip Costs: Incurred a $0.12 per share negative impact from operating expenses for the incremental Colstrip ownership, which are not currently recovered in rates. 2. Data Center Siting Challenges: One of three prospective data center projects is delayed due to land procurement issues, and management acknowledged local community pushback. 3. Rate Case Uncertainty: The company is still awaiting a motion for reconsideration on its 2024 rate review and will need to file a new rate case to recover Colstrip costs.
rows.key_quote: ...noting that was really driven off of improved base rate recovery versus last year.

Republic Airways reported Q2 2026 adjusted net income of $41 million ($0.89 per diluted share) on revenue of approximately $571 million, up 8% sequentially as block hour production rose 7%. The company raised full-year guidance: block hours to ~880,000 (from at least 865,000), revenue to >$2.1 billion (from >$2 billion), and adjusted EBITDAR to $395-$405 million (from >$380 million). July weather has hurt completion factor to 91%, but management remains confident, citing strong partner demand and ahead-of-schedule Mesa integration. Integration benefits are expected to materialize in late 2027 into 2028.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised full-year AFFO guidance to $3.22-$3.26 per share, reflecting confidence in future growth.
2. Operator EBITDAR coverage for the core portfolio increased to 1.65x, the highest level in over a decade.
3. Executed strategic asset sales at a 6.7% cap rate, with proceeds funding a robust pipeline of higher-yield RIDEA and triple-net investments expected to accelerate in H2 2026.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant asset sales ($563M in Q2) and loan repayments are expected to create a temporary earnings headwind in Q3 2026.
2. The investment pipeline is heavily weighted toward the latter half of the year, indicating a slower pace of acquisitions in H1.
3. Proactively transitioned 20 facilities from operator Ciena due to poor portfolio performance (0.87x EBITDAR coverage on allocated rent).
rows.key_quote: These dispositions, sold at a 6.7% cap rate... set us up for strong earnings accretion once the proceeds are redeployed.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Enrollment Growth: Total university partner enrollments grew 7.6%, driven by a 7.8% increase in GCU online enrollments and an 18.5% increase at active hybrid sites.
2. Raised Guidance and Margin Expansion: Beat Q2 non-GAAP EPS estimates by $0.14, raised full-year guidance, and expanded operating margin to 22.0% from 20.9% YoY.
3. Clear Future Growth Initiatives: Launching a College of Construction and a Law School to drive ground campus enrollment to 50,000, and expanding high-margin hybrid healthcare programs.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. MSA Amendment Impact: The amended MSA with GCU will reduce annual service revenue by approximately $20 million, though the impact on operating income is expected to be immaterial.
2. Online RPS Pressure: Online revenue per student is slightly down year-over-year due to a mix shift towards programs with slightly lower net tuition rates.
3. Hybrid Growth Constraints: Hybrid enrollment growth is being impacted by 14 locations being at or near capacity, limiting new starts until regulatory approval for expansion is received.
rows.key_quote: Over 70% of GCU's online students are pursuing degrees in areas where a license is required; these degree and licensure requirements are not going to change.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Hard Discount Performance: Hard discount banners (Maxi, No Frills) delivered comparable sales growth near 4%, capitalizing on consumer demand for value.
2. Robust Pharmacy Growth: Drug retail same-store sales grew 4.6%, led by a 7.5% SSS increase in Pharmacy & Healthcare Services, driven by specialty (GLP-1) and chronic prescriptions.
3. Increased Capital Return: Boosted the full-year share repurchase plan by $200M to $2.1B while reaffirming high single-digit EPS growth guidance for the year.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Conventional Banner Weakness: Conventional food banners posted negative same-store sales (implied), lapping a difficult prior-year comparison where growth was exceptionally strong.
2. Ongoing Cost Headwinds: SG&A rate was flat as operating leverage was offset by costs from new store openings and the ramp-up of its automated distribution center.
3. Near-Term Transaction Drag: The sale of PC Financial will create a Q3 timing headwind, with only one month of earnings from the new EQB partnership being recognized.
rows.key_quote: Our hard discount banners continue to perform well... with comparable sales close to 4%, supported by strong execution in both existing and new stores.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Monetizations & Earnings: "The second quarter was the largest monetization quarter in our history," leading to record FRE, total operating earnings, and adjusted net income per share (up 38% YoY).
2. Exceptional Fundraising & AUM Growth: Raised $305 billion in 2.5 years, beating a 3-year target, with private wealth AUM up 70% YoY and overall AUM momentum accelerating.
3. Strong Margin and Operating Leverage: FRE margin reached 70%, with management stating "we do not view that as a ceiling" due to revenue growing faster than headcount.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Heightened Insurance Competition: "We have seen heightened competition. We've made the determination that we're going to allocate a little bit less capital to insurance based on what we're seeing."
2. Data Center Market Indigestion: Management acknowledged that "hyperscaler data center spreads have widened pretty meaningfully just over the last couple of weeks... it feels like there's indigestion."
3. Back-End Weighted Earnings Risk: Strategic holdings earnings for 2026 are "more back-end weighted," creating a 'hockey stick' profile for the year that requires significant activity in H2 to meet targets.
rows.key_quote: The second quarter was the largest monetization quarter in our history, with exits diversified across strategies, regions, and with strong returns.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Long-term growth supported by new Gen 8.6 OLED fabs from Samsung and BOE commencing mass production.
2. Significant growth runway in underpenetrated markets like IT, automotive, and TVs, where OLED share is in the low single digits.
3. Continued progress on phosphorescent blue emitter technology, with LG Display showcasing a prototype tablet using the material.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Full-year revenue guidance was effectively lowered, with expectations now at the low end of the $630M-$670M range.
2. Smartphone market softness is the primary headwind, caused by rising component (e.g., memory) costs pressuring unit volumes.
3. Q2 material sales declined to $66M from $89M YoY, driven by lower volumes, customer mix, and negative catch-up adjustments.
rows.key_quote: Rising memory costs and supply constraints continue to weigh on demand expectations, particularly within the smartphone market.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Adjusted EBITDA grew ~25% and margins expanded over 260 bps, driven by strong price/cost management and structural cost optimization, not market improvement. 2) Raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $615M-$635M and expects ~50% free cash flow conversion. 3) Increased dividend by 10.7% and announced a new $150M share repurchase plan, signaling high confidence in future cash generation.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Ongoing geopolitical disruption (Middle East conflict) continues to impact demand, creating a forecasted $20M headwind. 2) Broader industrial markets remain soft, with chemical and housing end-markets at historically low levels. 3) Fiber Solutions segment margins were lower year-over-year due to cost inflation, with a implemented price increase not yet reflected in the key RISI index.
rows.key_quote: Those results were not driven by stronger markets. They were driven by disciplined execution.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised Full-Year Guidance Significantly: Lifted revenue forecast to $528-$531M and adjusted EBITDA to $96-$98M, effectively achieving a 5-year strategic goal in the current year.
2. Strong Client Expansion & ARPU Uplift: New logos in 2026 are onboarding at nearly double the overall ARPU, driven by the Digital Sales & Service Platform (DSSP) and a growing mix of bank clients.
3. Robust ARR Growth: ARR grew 21% to $512 million, outpacing 15.9% revenue growth and indicating strong future momentum, with a $61 million ARR backlog.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Q2 Gross Margin Dip: Non-GAAP gross margin of 63% was a sequential step-down, attributed to lower one-time termination fee revenue and timing of direct costs.
2. Moderating ARPU Growth: ARPU growth normalized to 7% YoY, down from 9% in Q1, as the initial lift from the MANTL acquisition faded. Full-year outlook was tempered to "mid to high single digits".
3. Delayed Cost-Saving Project: A database migration project intended to reduce expenses was pushed into 2027 to prioritize investment in product development like the lending platform.
rows.key_quote: The RPU of clients launching in 2026 is expected to be nearly twice the average of our install base.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.35-$4.43 (12-14% growth) on the back of strong Q2 results and a confident outlook. 
2. Water Quality segment delivered standout 5.7% core growth, driven by strong industrial demand from data centers and their ecosystem, described as a 'strong double-digit growth' area for ChemTreat. 
3. Strong capital deployment execution, with ~$480 million in share repurchases (over 2% of the company) and a strategic acquisition (Alfaa UV) in a high-growth market.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. High-growth markets were flat, with the China water business shrinking and Latin America experiencing project delays. 
2. Q2 adjusted operating margin expansion was artificially inflated by a one-time $16 million tariff refund, which contributed 110 basis points; underlying performance was merely in line with guidance. 
3. The PQI segment lagged with only 2% core growth, with its recovery dependent on a second-half acceleration and easier Q4 comps.
rows.key_quote: In water, our industrial market demand continues to be strong, and this is really on the back of the data center demand.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record organic orders growth of 11.1% with a book-to-bill ratio of 1.15x, resulting in a record backlog of $23.9 billion.
2. Pharmaceutical Diagnostics (PDx) delivered exceptional performance with 14.6% organic revenue growth, driven by strong volumes in contrast media and U.S. radiopharmaceuticals.
3. Advanced Imaging Solutions (AIS) grew revenue 5% organically and expanded its EBIT margin by 90 basis points, driven by volume and price.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Patient Care Solutions (PCS) segment revenue declined 13.5% organically and reported negative EBIT due to "operational fulfillment challenges" and supply issues.
2. Consolidated adjusted EBIT margin fell 40 basis points year-over-year to 14.2%, dragged down by the poor performance in the PCS segment.
3. The departure of CFO Jay Saccaro was announced, creating an executive transition at a key leadership position.
rows.key_quote: We saw orders growth across all of our segments, with particular strength in several of our longer-cycle products in radiology.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record member and product growth: Added 1.1M new members and 2.2M new products, driven by an inflection in cross-watching, with 51% of new products from existing members.
2. Strong Financials: Revenue grew 40% YoY to $1.2B, with a 30% adjusted EBITDA margin, achieving a 'Rule of 40' score of 70.
3. Successful Product Launches: SoFi Plus exceeded 200,000 paid subscribers in one quarter, creating recurring revenue and driving significant cross-watch activity.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Higher Tax Rate: Full-year EPS guidance includes a negative impact of ~$0.05 per share from a higher-than-expected tax rate of 22%.
2. Reinvestment over Profit Upside: Management chose to reinvest revenue outperformance into new growth areas rather than raising EBITDA or EPS guidance.
3. Rate Headwinds: The company's outlook now incorporates 1-2 expected interest rate hikes, a reversal from the rate cuts anticipated at the start of the year.
rows.key_quote: We've reached an important inflection point with products per member accelerating... We are starting to hit escape velocity on our path to be the winner.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Education Technology Services (ETS) division revenue grew 15% with operating income up 30%, led by 32% subscriber growth at Sophia Learning. 2. U.S. Higher Education operating income surged 56% with a 500 basis point margin expansion to 15%, driven by cost controls and 8% growth in employer-affiliated enrollment. 3. Strong consolidated profitability with adjusted EPS up 16% to $1.76 and year-to-date operating cash flow increasing 18% to $117 million.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. The Australia/New Zealand segment saw enrollment decline 5% and revenue fall 3% due to a challenged international market and slow student visa processing. 2. A $13 million one-time charge was taken for a labor dispute in Australia, significantly impacting reported operating income. 3. Full-year revenue is expected to be below the company's long-term notional model target due to the headwinds in Australia.
rows.key_quote: Our Education Technology Services division grew revenue 15% to $42 million and operating income by 30% to $20 million.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Raised full-year guidance for Core FFO, acquisition volume, and same-store NOI growth. 2) Achieved strong leasing spreads of 19.8% cash and 33.7% straight-line. 3) Captured significant new demand from data center-related tenants, leasing 2.3M sq ft since early 2025 with 33% rent roll-ups.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Noted regional market softness in port markets like Savannah and Charleston, and in Reno. 2) Acquisition cap rates are compressing, with guidance for stabilized cap rates lowered to 6%-6.5%. 3) Leasing activity is slower in the Reno development project due to a lull in distribution tenant demand.
rows.key_quote: Industrial fundamentals continue to stabilize... vacancy has peaked... Net absorption was 69 million square feet this quarter, a meaningful acceleration from Q1.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $16.80 from $14.50, driven by strong H1 performance. 
2. Generated a 20% gain-on-sale margin on $1.4 billion of asset sales, highlighting strong asset values. 
3. Secured 15 scarce Boeing 787 delivery slots and repurchased $690 million in shares, demonstrating disciplined capital allocation.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Noted regional weakness in daily flight activity in the Middle East, Asia Pacific, and North America. 
2. Geopolitical challenges leading to higher input costs (e.g., oil) may put pressure on airline margins. 
3. Net maintenance contribution, a driver of H1 outperformance, is expected to normalize to lower levels in H2.
rows.key_quote: Aircraft and engine availability remain constrained while airline demand exceeds supply, reflected in our leasing activity, lease extensions, and asset values.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Total organic orders grew 28%, led by a 47% surge in the Health & Science Technologies (HST) segment from data center, semiconductor, and space/defense demand. 2. Raised full-year 2026 guidance for organic growth to 5-6% (from 3-4%) and adjusted EPS to $8.70-$8.85 (from $8.35-$8.55). 3. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 70 bps to 28.1%, with strong flow-through of approximately 40% in the high-growth HST segment.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Organic sales declined 1% in the Fire & Safety/Diversified Products (FSDP) segment, citing weakness in dispensing and European rescue markets. 2. The Fluid & Metering Technologies (FMT) segment had only 1% organic sales growth, with softness in agriculture, chemical, and energy markets. 3. Underlying margins in FMT and FSDP were pressured by unfavorable mix and volume deleverage, with reported results being partially masked by one-time tariff refunds.
rows.key_quote: The HST order growth is predominantly coming from growing demand in data center, semiconductor and space and defense markets.

rows.positive_highlights:
Operating EBITDA margin expanded 40 basis points, overcoming 100 bps of headwinds from wildfire comps and fuel, driven by strong pricing and cost optimization.
Free cash flow grew 35% in the quarter, supported by higher earnings and 18% lower capital spending.
Healthcare Solutions operating EBITDA margin expanded 200 basis points to 19% as integration synergies and cost controls take hold, with price expected to exit 2026 above 5.5%.
rows.negative_highlights:
Full-year revenue outlook was lowered by approximately 0.5% due to softer-than-expected volumes and delays at RNG plants.
Collection and Disposal volumes declined 0.4% (excluding prior-year wildfire impact), with the full-year outlook now expected to be a decline approaching 1%.
Commercial line of business experienced some volume negativity driven by lost national accounts.
rows.key_quote: Our SmartTruck... generates more than $300 million of annual run rate EBITDA through service upgrades, optimized routing and lower operating costs.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. AI-driven opportunity pipeline doubled year-over-year to nearly $10 billion, with the total Managed Services pipeline up 20% and SI&C up 30%. 2. Strong trailing 12-month book-to-bill of 108% ($17.8 billion), led by Managed Services at 115%. 3. GAAP diluted EPS grew 22.5% to $2.23, and the company generated $605 million in cash from operations.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Q3 revenue growth of 2.5% was driven almost entirely by acquisitions (approx. 2.5%), indicating flat to slightly negative organic growth. 2. Management confirmed continued delays in client decision-making on a couple of deals in the Nordics. 3. The effective tax rate increased to 26.5% due to a new corporate tax surcharge in France, with future guidance rising to 26%-27%.
rows.key_quote: The segment of the total pipeline with AI-based services is now nearly $10 billion, double in size since last year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. **Accelerating Organic Growth:** Revenue grew 14% organically, with Q3 guidance accelerating to 21%, driven by broad-based demand across data centers, industrial automation, construction, and a recovering HVAC market. 
2. **Significant Profitability Expansion:** Adjusted EBITDA margin increased 220 bps to 23.6% due to high volume leverage and favorable mix. Q3 adjusted EPS is guided to grow 68% YoY.
3. **Strategic Execution:** The newly acquired Basler business is outperforming, leading to a raised full-year outlook. Design wins were up double-digits across all markets, securing future growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. **Passenger Vehicle Softness:** Organic sales in the passenger vehicle market declined 2%, attributed to lower global production and ongoing sensor product declines.
2. **Consumer Electronics Decline:** The consumer electronics end market, which is less than 10% of company sales, saw a sales decline in the quarter.
3. **Transportation Margin Pressure:** The Transportation Products segment's adjusted EBITDA margin of 18.6% was noted as being "lower in the quarter," while other segments saw significant expansion.
rows.key_quote: Industrial segment sales increased 52%... with 16% organic growth, supported by strong data center, industrial automation and construction demand.

rows.positive_highlights:
Building Climate Solutions (BCS) revenue grew 24% (12% organic), driven by strong execution and share gains in emergency replacement and national accounts.
Full-year free cash flow guidance of $750M-$850M was maintained, reflecting confidence in working capital management and inventory reduction plans.
Company completed the bolt-on acquisition of Comfort-Aire, Century, and Coast-Air brands, expanding its distribution reach and product offering.
rows.negative_highlights:
Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was lowered to $23-$24 due to weaker residential volumes and associated manufacturing absorption headwinds.
Home Comfort Solutions (HCS) revenue fell 7% on a 12% volume decline, driven by walking away from low-margin new construction business and a muted market recovery.
The meaningful residential market recovery is now not expected until 2027, a significant delay from the previous H2 2026 expectation.
rows.key_quote: Stronger commercial demand is more than offset by lower expected residential volumes.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Profitability: Profit after tax increased 30% to $142 million, generating a 19.6% annualized return on equity.
2. Disciplined Cycle Management: Actively reduced catastrophe exposure by downsizing the inward retro portfolio and increasing reinsurance purchases, lowering PMLs.
3. Confident Guidance: Reaffirmed expectation to deliver a high-teens return on equity for the full year, despite market headwinds.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Softening Market: Management repeatedly cited a more competitive marketplace with pricing pressure, particularly in property lines, due to abundant industry capacity.
2. Lower Reserve Releases: Prior year favorable development was significantly lower than H1 2025, negatively impacted by adverse development on the Baltimore Bridge claim.
3. Stagnant Top Line: Insurance revenue was flat and gross written premiums were broadly stable, indicating a lack of growth as the company prioritizes discipline over volume.
rows.key_quote: We have strategically reduced our inward retro footprint... to manage earnings volatility and natural catastrophe exposure as we move through this phase of the cycle.

rows.positive_highlights:
Stars Program Improvement: Rate of improvement for BY'28 meaningfully outpaced the historical CAGR across 11 of 12 sample HEDIS metrics, boosting confidence in returning to top-quartile results.
Operational Efficiency: Realized hundreds of millions in value from operating model changes, contributing to a 120 bps YoY reduction in Q2 consolidated operating cost ratio.
MA Margin Progression: On track to double individual MA pretax margin in 2026 (excluding Stars headwinds) and planning for meaningful margin expansion in 2027 through strategic plan exits.
rows.negative_highlights:
Planned Membership Disruption: Strategic plan exits in 2027 will impact approximately 600,000 members to prioritize margin improvement over broad-based retention.
Persistent Drug Cost Pressure: Management noted that the high drug cost trend is expected to "tick modestly higher next year," remaining a headwind.
Stars Outcome Uncertainty: Despite strong operational gains, management cannot guarantee the final BY'28 Stars outcome as it depends on unknown, yet-to-be-released industry-wide performance thresholds from CMS.
rows.key_quote: Our rate of improvement outpaced and in many places, meaningfully outpaced the historical CAGR across 11 of the 12 [Stars] measures.

rows.positive_highlights:
Raised full-year EPS guidance to $4.40-$4.60, driven by a net IEEPA tariff refund benefit of ~$85 million for the year.
International Plumbing sales increased 4% in local currency, driven by strong growth in European markets, particularly Germany.
PRO paint sales continued to show momentum, growing mid-single digits in the quarter.
rows.negative_highlights:
Consolidated net sales decreased 3%, impacted by a weak comparison and strategic investments; North American Plumbing sales fell 6%.
DIY paint sales decreased high single digits due to challenging industry dynamics and a prior customer transition.
Management expects commodity costs to remain elevated in the second half of the year and acknowledged continued softness in the China market.
rows.key_quote: Operating profit was driven by the approximately $95 million net tariff refund benefit, pricing actions and cost savings initiatives.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong order growth and backlog expansion: Total Q2 orders up 40% (10% ex-M&A) and total backlog reached $1.1 billion, up nearly 40% YoY.
Momentum in nuclear power: Nuclear power orders grew 50% ex-M&A, driven by both the existing operating fleet and SMRs, including $49 million in new SMR orders.
Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 150 bps to 27.5% due to favorable product mix and pricing, which more than offset M&A dilution and inflation.
rows.negative_highlights:
Weak organic revenue growth: Q2 organic revenue grew only 1%, with the Medical segment declining 1% organically due to tough prior-year comps and delayed hardware demand.
Chinese order cancellation: An $18 million new build order booked in 2019 was unexpectedly cancelled, highlighting geopolitical and project timing risks, though management stressed it has no impact on guidance.
Lowered medical sub-segment outlooks: The full-year outlook for nuclear medicine was lowered to mid-single-digits (from double-digits) and dosimetry to negative (from flat) due to reduced hardware volume.
rows.key_quote: Nuclear power orders, excluding M&A, grew 50% in the second quarter with both the operating fleet and SMRs being key drivers.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Significant embedded FFO growth identified, with ~$0.29 per share upside from stabilizing the office portfolio, of which $0.14 is from already signed leases. 2. Strong retail portfolio performance, ending the quarter at 98% leased with comparable straight-line rent spreads of 20%. 3. Healthy office leasing pipeline with 200,000 sq ft of signed leases yet to commence rent and proposals out on nearly 150,000 sq ft of additional space.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Multifamily market softness due to new supply, resulting in a shift to occupancy focus and modest blended rent growth of 2-3%. 2. Mixed performance at the Waikiki property, where hotel NOI declined to $2.5M from $2.9M YoY due to rate competition and a mixed tourism backdrop. 3. Office lease-up timing is uncertain, described as "binary," as it depends on a few large deals that could be delayed into the next year.
rows.key_quote: At La Jolla Commons Tower 3, the building is currently 49% leased with proposals representing another 33% of the building.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Announced all-stock merger with Hornbeck Offshore, creating a diversified entity with expected annual revenue and cost synergies of $75M+ within 3 years. 2. Strong robotics market with trenching work booked out to 2030, a bid pipeline to 2032, and expecting full ROV utilization by year-end. 3. Improving conditions in the North Sea, returning to a 2-vessel well intervention operation with expectations of good utilization and slightly better rates.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Reported a Q1 net loss of $13 million on revenue of $288 million, reflecting seasonal weakness and project costs. 2. Gross profit was low at $9 million for the quarter, yielding a gross margin of approximately 3.1%. 3. Full-year EBITDA guidance ($230M-$290M) is negatively impacted by costs from the Q1 Thunder Hawk workover and an upcoming vessel docking (Siem Helix 1).
rows.key_quote: Our first quarter results reflect expected seasonal levels during the winter in the North Sea and Gulf of America shelf.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Held tire unit volumes flat and gained share in Tier 1 and overall tire category despite a weak market. 2. Drove comp sales growth in high-margin services, including an 8% increase in battery comps, through its ConfiDrive inspection tool. 3. Saw early success from a profit improvement toolkit rolled out to ~340 underperforming locations.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Comparable store sales declined 1.7%, driven by lower traffic and consumer deferral of high-ticket spending. 2. Adjusted diluted EPS was a loss of $0.09 compared to a profit of $0.22 in the prior year. 3. Gross margin decreased by 50 basis points due to sales deleverage on fixed occupancy costs.
rows.key_quote: Our comp store sales decline was driven by lower store traffic as well as consumers that continued to defer higher-ticket spending decisions in tires and brakes.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Electrification performance: Delivered 4.5% organic growth, driven by PWR-Grid (+4.9%) and PWR-Connect (+7.3%).
2. PWR-Transmission profitability surge: Adjusted EBITDA margin increased by almost 200 basis points to 13.7% with backlog loaded to mid-2028.
3. Raised FY26 EBITDA Guidance: Lifted guidance by €40M at the low end to a range of €770M-€840M due to strong H1 and acquisition contribution.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Group margin compression: Overall Group adjusted EBITDA margin of 11.9% was slightly below H1 2025 due to adverse mix effects.
2. PWR-Connect margin challenges: Resilient margins were constrained by a negative mix from a sluggish high-margin Nordic market and growth in lower-margin Italy.
3. Other Activities decline: Metallurgy segment experienced a 15% organic sales decline due to a tough comparison base from H1 2025.
rows.key_quote: Standard sales reached EUR 3.2 billion, up by 1.5% organically, driven by a strong Electrification performance with organic growth up by 4.5%.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Revenue grew 10.4% to $1.55B, marking a return to growth. 2) Operating Ratio improved 450 basis points to 70.1%, driving a 32.3% increase in EPS to $1.68. 3) Strong pricing power was the main driver, with LTL revenue per hundredweight (ex-fuel) increasing 5.5%.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) LTL tons per day decreased 4.1% year-over-year, indicating revenue growth was entirely driven by price/yield. 2) Operating ratio guidance for Q3 is weaker, expected to increase 150-200 bps sequentially after normalizing for a Q2 property gain. 3) Operating supplies expenses increased due to higher diesel fuel costs.
rows.key_quote: Our revenue results include a 15.2% increase in LTL revenue per hundredweight which was partially offset by a 4.1% decrease in our tons per day.

rows.positive_highlights:
North American sales grew 9% driven by 7% price and 2% positive volume growth, indicating resilient aftermarket demand and share gains.
Successfully completed a debt refinancing, extending maturities and reducing annual interest expense by ~$6 million, while lowering net leverage to a post-IPO low of 1.5x.
Maintained full-year guidance for ~5% sales growth and 9-13% adjusted EPS growth, reflecting confidence in second-half performance.
rows.negative_highlights:
Europe and Rest of World segment sales declined 8% (Rest of World -16%) due to macroeconomic weakness and geopolitical disruption.
Consolidated gross margin declined 50 basis points year-over-year to 48.7% due to inflationary pressures on materials and freight.
Overall company volume was described as 'stable', indicating that price realization, not broad volume expansion, was the primary driver of total company revenue growth.
rows.key_quote: North America net sales were up 9% to $278 million, driven by 7% price realization and 2% volume growth.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Commercial Truck Market Recovery: North American Class 8 orders increased 170% in Q2, with an industry backlog growth of 105%, signaling strong retail sales for H2 2026.
2. Strong Diversified Performance: Same-store retail auto units increased 5%, new vehicle GPU remained stable sequentially at $4,782, and equity income from PTS increased 7% to $57 million.
3. Robust Capital Management: Reduced long-term debt by $141 million, increased the quarterly dividend for the 23rd consecutive time to $1.44, and generated strong operating cash flow.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. SG&A Pressure: SG&A as a percentage of gross profit increased to 71.8% from 69.8% YoY, signaling consolidated margin compression despite growth in individual segments.
2. Challenging U.K. Market: The U.K. auto environment is impacted by higher taxes, consumer affordability, and electrification mandates, creating ongoing uncertainty.
3. Weakness in PTS Rental: Penske Transportation Solutions (PTS) experienced a 12% decline in its rental revenue segment as it continues to rightsize its fleet.
rows.key_quote: North American Class 8 orders increased 170% in Q2; we expect to see the benefit from the strong order book in H2 2026.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Overall sales grew 21% to $1.1B, with Aerospace up 19% and Industrial up 26%.
2. Significant margin expansion, with Aerospace segment margin reaching 24.0% and Industrial segment margin hitting 22.1%.
3. Raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $9.30-$9.50, reflecting an increase of 43% in quarterly adjusted EPS.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Free cash flow guidance was not raised with earnings due to intentional working capital builds in inventory and higher accounts receivable.
2. Defense OEM sales declined 6% due to a one-time revenue recognition adjustment, showing modest underlying growth.
3. Management highlighted future supply chain risks, particularly in castings, forgings, and rare earth metals.
rows.key_quote: We delivered significant margin expansion, primarily driven by pricing actions. We are also seeing productivity gains from our lean transformation start to flow through.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Delivered 15% base EPS growth year-over-year, leading to a strong base ROE of 19.3%.
2. Empower segment had an excellent quarter with base earnings up 34% (constant currency), driven by strong organic growth and operating margins improving over 600 basis points.
3. Capital and Risk Solutions (CRS) segment continued its strong performance with base earnings up 35% (constant currency), driven by a 54% YoY increase in run-rate insurance results from high demand for capital solutions.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Canadian operations base earnings decreased 9% YoY due to moderated long-term disability (LTD) experience, a trend that may continue in the near term.
2. Net earnings were negatively impacted by unfavorable market experience, primarily from interest rate movements and hedging ineffectiveness on share-based compensation during a period of strong equity market performance.
3. Empower's US wealth net inflows of $1.8 billion were the lowest in seven quarters, indicating a lower capture rate of rollovers from the retirement business.
rows.key_quote: delivering 15% base EPS growth driven by double-digit growth at both Empower and CRS.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong NIM expansion: Net interest margin increased to 3.47% from 3.18% YoY, with guidance updated for further expansion to 3.80-3.85% in 2027.
2. Significant future cost savings: Expecting over $100M in pre-tax cost savings from the full integration of three recent acquisitions.
3. Robust core earnings growth: Adjusted net income increased 20.4% and EPS grew 14.1% year-over-year, demonstrating strong underlying profitability.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Intense loan pricing competition: Management noted 'ridiculously low' pricing and credit spreads at '25- or 30-year lows', forcing them to pass on some growth opportunities.
2. Flat near-term loan growth: The company guided to 'flattish' loan growth for the remainder of the year due to their disciplined, profitability-focused approach in a competitive environment.
3. Integration execution risk: The top priority is the complex operational integration of three separate bank mergers, with final systems conversion not complete until March 2027.
rows.key_quote: credit spreads are at 25- or 30-year lows across the risk spectrum. I mean, some things out there are just getting to the point of being ridiculous.

rows.positive_highlights:
Adjusted EPS surged to $0.28 compared to $0.01 in Q2 2025, a 2700% increase.
Average time charter equivalent (TCE) rate increased to $20,642 from $14,875 in the prior-year quarter.
Quarterly dividend was increased for a second consecutive quarter to $0.075 per share, supported by strong financial performance.
rows.negative_highlights:
Potential for softer Chinese import demand in H2 2026 due to increased inventories and the property sector crisis.
Overall coal shipments are projected to decline by 1% to 2% in 2026.
Average number of vessels operated decreased slightly to 45.13 from 46.75 in Q2 2025 due to fleet renewal activities.
rows.key_quote: During the second quarter of 2026, we operated in an improved charter market environment... with increased revenues due to higher charter hires.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Metal Containers segment achieved 7% organic volume growth in wet pet food products. 2. Dispensing segment saw strong growth in high-value fine fragrance products, particularly in Europe. 3. Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS and free cash flow guidance was confirmed, with management confident in H2 performance.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Significant market softness in Brazil caused a 15% regional volume decline and an unfavorable mix, impacting Dispensing segment EBIT by approximately $5 million. 2. Unrecovered cost inflation, primarily from resin, negatively impacted Q2 results by approximately $10 million. 3. Metal Containers' overall volume was flat as pet food growth was offset by double-digit declines in vegetable and soup due to order normalization.
rows.key_quote: That $10 million... was a Q2 item... the net unrecovered inflation, primarily resin.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Aerospace & Advanced Technologies (AAT) delivered 13.3% core sales growth with backlog reaching a record of nearly $1.3 billion. 2. Recent acquisitions outperformed, prompting a raise in their full-year contribution forecast to $0.20 in EPS from $0.15 previously. 3. Total company adjusted operating margin expanded 180 basis points to a record 21.3%, driven by pricing, productivity, and cost discipline.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Process Flow Technologies (PFT) core sales declined 1.4% year-over-year, reflecting continued market headwinds in the first half. 2. PFT core orders were only approximately flat year-over-year, indicating a slow, rather than rapid, recovery in underlying demand. 3. AAT adjusted segment margin declined to 25.8% from 26.6% year-over-year due to the expected dilutive impact from the Druck acquisition.
rows.key_quote: Total company adjusted operating margin expanded 180 basis points to a record 21.3%... impacted by favorable pricing, strong productivity and disciplined cost management.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised Guidance: Full-year same-store revenue guidance raised 100bps to 1-2% and NOI guidance raised 200bps to 0.5-2.5%, lifting Core FFO outlook.
2. Accelerating NOI Growth: Same-store NOI grew 3.5%, accelerating 230 bps from Q1, driven by 2.4% revenue growth combined with a modest decline in same-store expenses.
3. Strong Retention & Improving Trends: Customer length of stay increased by 1.5 months year-over-year, and new supply is moderating across most markets, supporting an improving operating environment.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Implied H2 Deceleration: Raised guidance implies a flat to decelerating growth rate in the second half of the year due to tougher year-over-year comps and macro risks.
2. Steady but Not Growing Demand: Management stated customer demand is 'steady' and has not seen a pickup from the housing market, with gains coming from execution rather than market expansion.
3. Expensive Acquisition Market: Asset pricing remains elevated, with cap rates in the 'high fours to the high fives', limiting acquisitions to proprietary and relationship-based deals.
rows.key_quote: The pricing power we have been building over the past several quarters is now clearly flowing through our results.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Significant credit quality improvement, with nonperforming assets declining 47.3% following the strategic sale of a $73.8M delinquent mortgage portfolio. 2. Successful completion of a 45-year-old core system conversion, which is expected to drive future operating efficiencies and enable new product offerings. 3. Net interest margin expanded 3 bps sequentially to 3.84%, supported by strong deposit growth and solid loan originations.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Modest headline loan growth of 0.3% linked-quarter was significantly impacted by a $73.8M mortgage loan sale and $318M in CRE prepayments, which offset strong new originations. 2. Management anticipates near-term margin pressure in Q3 due to promotional campaigns and increased deposit pricing competition. 3. Non-interest expense increased 1.2% linked-quarter, driven by one-time costs related to the core deposit conversion and data center migration.
rows.key_quote: The sale drove a $47.1 million overall reduction in nonperforming loans and reduced the risk profile of our one-to-four family portfolio.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Investment Bank Strength: Record Q2 revenues of $3.7B (+31% YoY), driven by a 53% surge in Equities revenue with exceptional performance in APAC.
2. Wealth Management Growth: GWM pretax profit grew 38% YoY, attracting $36B in net new assets. FY26 GWM NII growth guidance was raised to ~10%.
3. Integration & Cost Control: Achieved $12.6B of a targeted $13.5B in gross cost savings; lowered NCL non-litigation opex exit rate guidance to ~$400M.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. U.S. Wealth Adviser Attrition: Ongoing financial adviser exits continue to create a lag and pressure on flows in the U.S. wealth business.
2. FRC Revenue Decline: Fixed Income, Rates, and Currencies (FRC) revenues in the Investment Bank fell 21% YoY due to an unfavorable mix and strategic capital shift to Equities.
3. Buyback Uncertainty: The new $3B share buyback has an extended timeline to Q2 2027, creating analyst uncertainty tied to pending Swiss capital requirement deliberations.
rows.key_quote: Global Markets delivered a record second quarter... Equities led the performance with revenues up 53% on strong client activity and exceptional momentum in Asia Pacific.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Colonial Life delivered a record earnings quarter with $131.4 million in adjusted operating income, 6% sales growth, and a 19.4% ROE.
2. The Unum US Group Life and AD&D business had a strong quarter with a favorable benefit ratio of 66% driven by lower mortality incidence.
3. The company saw strong top-line momentum with 14.3% year-to-date sales growth in the Unum US segment and overall strong persistency of 91.5% in total U.S. group.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. U.S. Group Disability was pressured by elevated claims in newer Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML) states, pushing the benefit ratio to 65.8%, above the 62-64% target range.
2. The Unum U.K. business experienced significantly unfavorable results, with its benefit ratio rising to 82.2% from 75% year-over-year due to higher average claim values in group income protection.
3. The overall Unum International segment's adjusted operating income fell sharply to $24.3 million from $41.6 million in the prior-year quarter.
rows.key_quote: U.S. group disability results were pressured by elevated experience in short-term disability, primarily from the newer paid family medical leave states.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong Balance Sheet: Ended the year debt-free with $187.5 million in cash and investments. 
Shareholder Returns: Declared a regular quarterly dividend of $0.39 and a special cash dividend of $0.25, the 6th consecutive year for a special dividend. 
One-Time Margin Benefit: Received a $5 million tariff refund, which boosted quarterly gross margin by 340 basis points.
rows.negative_highlights:
Weak Demand: Retail written orders fell 10.8% and wholesale orders fell 11.9% due to lower traffic and macroeconomic uncertainty. 
Operating Margin Pressure: Adjusted operating margin declined to 7.4% from 9.7% last year, due to lower sales and fixed cost deleveraging. 
Tariff Headwinds: Faces an estimated $15 million in total ongoing annual tariff exposure from new and existing tariffs.
rows.key_quote: Retail written orders decreased 10.8%... as lower traffic and macroeconomic uncertainty created near term pressure.

rows.positive_highlights:
Record Financials & Debt Reduction: Achieved all-time highs for operating margin ($5.9B) and adjusted funds flow ($5B), enabling a $2.7B net debt reduction in Q2.
Raised Production Guidance on Efficiency: Increased full-year production guidance by ~50k BOE/d at the midpoint with no change to capital spending, driven by outperformance at Christina Lake, Foster Creek, and Sunrise.
Lower Operating Costs: Reduced full-year operating cost guidance for oil sands, conventional, and Canadian refining segments due to higher production volumes and cost discipline.
rows.negative_highlights:
Lower Downstream Market Capture: U.S. refining market capture decreased to 67% from the prior quarter, impacted by rising gasoline prices and lag in secondary product prices.
Increased Feedstock Costs: U.S. downstream was impacted by temporary dislocations in domestic light crude prices (Bakken, Midland, WTI), which increased feedstock costs during the quarter.
Upcoming Major Turnaround: A significant turnaround is planned for the Lima Refinery in the second half of the year, which will impact downstream throughput.
rows.key_quote: With increased productivity at Christina Lake, Foster Creek and Sunrise, we are increasing our full year production guidance... with no change to our capital.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Q2 revenue of $1.6B (+8% YoY) and record Adj. EPS of $7.03 (+12% YoY) driven by strong execution despite macro headwinds.
2. CWT segment revenue grew 10% driven by share gain initiatives, with sequential Adj. EBITDA margin improving 380 bps from structural efficiency benefits.
3. Increased full-year share repurchase target from $1.0B to $1.2B, signaling confidence in cash flow and intrinsic value.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin outlook was lowered to flat YoY due to a lag between price increases and rapidly rising raw material/freight costs.
2. Q2 consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin declined 70 bps YoY, with a negative price-cost impact of approximately $40 million in the core CCM segment.
3. New construction markets remain soft, and the full-year outlook assumes no improvement, while geopolitical conflict continues to drive input cost inflation.
rows.key_quote: We expected to see negative price costs in Q2 as we work through committed quotes and the required notification period to customers.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised full-year revenue guidance from 1-2% growth to "2% or better" based on a solid Q1 and improved H2 visibility.
2. The North Face grew 4%, beating expectations, led by transitional outerwear and equipment.
3. Timberland saw continued strong growth in the Americas (up 10%), with overall brand revenue up 3%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Vans revenue continues to struggle, down 9% globally in Q1, with a similar decline expected for Q2.
2. The wholesale channel remains weak, declining 4% overall and significantly lagging the 5% growth in DTC.
3. International performance was weak, with EMEA revenues down 7% and APAC down 1%.
rows.key_quote: wholesale is going to be a lot better around the world. We're confident because we have much better visibility into our wholesale partners' plans.

rows.positive_highlights: Massive data center demand growth: preparing to serve a forecasted 2.6 GW increase from Microsoft and 1.3 GW from Vantage. Strong EPS performance: earnings up $0.15 YoY to $0.91, driven by $0.13 from grid investments for Very Large Customers (VLCs). Confident outlook: reiterated 7-8% long-term EPS growth, expecting acceleration to the upper half of the range from 2028.
rows.negative_highlights: Regulatory/legal risk with Oracle: collateral requirements for the Vantage/Oracle data center project are under legal challenge, though management is confident of resolution. Negative weather impact: Q2 earnings were negatively impacted by approximately $0.05 per share versus the prior year. Labor constraints in Illinois: a pipe replacement program is progressing slower than planned due to challenges in ramping up the workforce.
rows.key_quote: We are preparing to serve a forecasted demand increase of 2.6 gigawatts in this region through 2030 and an opportunity for further expansion.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong acceleration in Spain: Revenue growth hit 2.9% YoY, EBITDA grew 2.3%, and churn reached a record low of 0.7%.
2. Brazil outperforms: Revenue and EBITDA grew well ahead of inflation, driven by a 5.7% increase in mobile ARPU and strong demand for digital services.
3. Upgraded cash flow guidance: Adjusted operating cash flow after leases guidance was raised from 'over 2%' to 'over 3%' growth for 2026, reflecting strong operating leverage in Spain and Brazil.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Major weakness in Germany: Revenue declined over 11% YoY, dragged down by a 26% drop in handset sales, leading to a cautious full-year revenue outlook.
2. Significant German restructuring: A plan to reduce ~1,100 employees and close 60 shops was announced, with a €265 million provision taken in Q2.
3. Pressure in the UK: VMO2 results were weak due to competitive pressure and handset trends, with leverage rising to 5.8x, above the target range.
rows.key_quote: due to the weakness in handsets, mainly in Germany, we expect to be at the low end of our revenue growth range.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. EBITDA before special items grew 54% to €2.4 billion, driven by stronger prices and higher volumes across most segments, especially Materials, Chemicals, and Industrial Solutions. 2. Significant progress on restructuring, achieving a €2.0 billion annual cost savings run rate and reducing the workforce by approximately 7,000 since January 2024. 3. Successfully closed the €7.7 billion Coatings transaction with Carlyle and generated over €800 million in cash from the ongoing watch-down of its Harbour Energy stake.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. The Surface Technologies segment experienced a considerable decline in EBITDA, due to weaker performance in Precious Metal Services and the expiry of subsidies for Battery Materials. 2. Free cash flow was negative at -€189 million for the quarter, a significant decrease from +€533 million in Q2 2025, primarily due to increased working capital from higher prices and sales. 3. Agricultural Solutions faced headwinds from slightly lower prices and negative currency effects, though overall performance was described as robust with volume growth.
rows.key_quote: The increase was primarily driven by continued volume growth and higher specific margins.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. AI Adoption Driving Wins: Secured five new $1M+ customer deals in Q2, with 100% including AI services, as AI shifts watching behavior in Bandwidth's favor.
2. Strong Financials & Raised Guidance: Revenue grew 22% YoY to $220M and Adj. EBITDA grew 27% to $28M; raised full-year revenue and profitability outlook.
3. Large Customer Momentum: Commercial net retention rate was 113%; strong ramp from recent large wins and initial revenue flow from the strategic Salesforce partnership.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Voice Business Deceleration: Analyst noted a slowdown in voice growth to 9% YoY, which management attributed to the timing of customer implementations.
2. Lowered Political Revenue Forecast: Full-year expectation for cyclical political campaign revenue was revised down from $15 million to $13 million.
3. Gross Margin Below Some Expectations: An analyst noted gross margin was below their model, though management stated it met internal targets and would expand in H2.
rows.key_quote: AI is changing how enterprises watch communications infrastructure, shifting the decision toward providers that can support mission critical AI interactions.

rows.positive_highlights:
1) Improved pricing on new originations: Average spreads on new senior loans were 20 bps wider and upfront fees were 50 bps higher compared to Q4 2025.
2) Strong competitive positioning: Less competition from retail-funded lenders in the upper-middle market is allowing ARCC to secure better terms and underwrite larger deals, including a nearly $2 billion sole commitment in Q2.
3) Balance sheet optimization: Launched the first commercial paper program in the BDC sector, expected to lower funding costs by 50-100 bps on drawn amounts, reinforcing financial flexibility.
rows.negative_highlights:
1) Subdued Q2 transaction environment: Overall M&A market activity was slow for most of the quarter, although deal flow picked up significantly in June.
2) Slight credit deterioration: Non-accruals at cost increased from 2.1% to 2.4% with four new portfolio companies added to non-accrual status.
3) Lower deal quality reviewed: The quality of deal flow in Q2 dipped, causing the company to be more selective and resulting in a below-average closing ratio of approximately 5%.
rows.key_quote: The scale of our capital is driving enhanced economics, stronger terms, and more compelling risk-adjusted returns than we saw a year ago.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. PROPWR Growth: Increased contracted power capacity by ~46% to 350 MW and achieved positive EBITDA in the last two months of the quarter. 2. Completions Market Tightening: Activating a 13th fleet amid a tightening supply environment, leading to positive pricing momentum and a stronger outlook. 3. Strong Liquidity: Ended the quarter with $905 million in total liquidity, providing ample funding for the PROPWR growth strategy.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Q2 Operational Headwinds: Quarterly results were negatively impacted by weather disruptions, fleet deployment costs, and unexpected downtime on an out-of-basin project. 2. Widened Net Loss: Reported a net loss of $8 million ($0.07/share), a deterioration from the prior quarter's $4 million loss, despite higher revenue. 3. Delayed Data Center Contracts: Management acknowledged that negotiations for large data center contracts are taking longer than originally anticipated.
rows.key_quote: customers are increasingly recognizing just how many frac fleets have exited the market, and that's leading to increasingly constructive conversations around demand and pricing.

rows.positive_highlights: Asset-Based segment adjusted operating ratio improved 200 bps YoY to 90.8%, driven by a strategic focus on heavier freight. Asset-Light segment generated $6 million in non-GAAP operating income, a $5 million improvement YoY, with employee productivity up 35%. A new restructuring plan is expected to generate $40 million in annualized cost savings, simplifying the business and accelerating strategy.
rows.negative_highlights: The company recorded $76.5 million in noncash impairment charges related to restructuring, including the discontinuation of the U-Pack system and brand consolidation. Management noted they have "not yet seen a broad-based inflection in industrial demand" with overall freight demand remaining "muted". Revenue per hundredweight excluding fuel declined in the low single digits in July due to the change in freight profile.
rows.key_quote: The continued expansion of our digital quote pool is enabling greater selectivity... supporting higher weight, operationally efficient shipments that contribute meaningfully to profitability.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record non-GAAP gross margin of 62.3%, up 480 bps YoY, driven by the completed cloud migration. 2. Raised full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, supported by strong bookings (8 Tier 1/enterprise wins) and subscription revenue performance. 3. Ended the quarter debt-free after repaying convertible notes and announced a new $350 million share repurchase authorization, signaling strong balance sheet and confidence.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Ongoing pressure in discretionary professional services revenue, which is partially offsetting growth in other non-subscription areas. 2. Total ARR growth (13%) continues to lag subscription ARR growth (15%) due to the weakness in non-subscription revenues. 3. Management noted tougher year-over-year comps for the second half of the year, implying a modest deceleration in subscription growth metrics.
rows.key_quote: Technology spend is shifting from 'run the bank' to 'change the bank,' and we are at the center of that opportunity.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Massive capital return: Repurchased $1.2 billion in shares in Q2 (totaling $1.95B in H1), equal to ~94% of net income, signaling strong confidence.
2. Strong underlying profitability: Delivered an overall ex-cat accident year combined ratio of 82.5% and after-tax operating income of $893 million.
3. Segment resilience: Reinsurance delivered $410 million and Mortgage delivered $220 million in underwriting income, demonstrating the stability of the diversified model.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Softening market and declining revenue: Management confirmed entering the "early stages of a competitive market," driving Net Premiums Written down 5.1% in Insurance and 10.4% in Reinsurance.
2. Significant catastrophe losses: Incurred $201 million in net catastrophe losses, primarily from the Iran conflict which heavily impacted the insurance segment.
3. Margin compression: The overall ex-cat accident year combined ratio increased by 160 bps to 82.5% year-over-year, reflecting pricing pressure and a shift in business mix.
rows.key_quote: Reinsurance net premiums written were down 10% as clients retained more risk and increasing competition lowered rates, particularly in property.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Unit Growth Intact: Reaffirmed full-year global unit growth of 15-16%, supported by a record development pipeline.
2. Profitability Growth: Adjusted EBITDA increased 12.5% and net income grew 16.9% in Q2.
3. Successful Loyalty Launch: 'Club Wingstop' enrollments are 22% ahead of expectations, with loyalty sales representing nearly half of first-party digital sales.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Significant Sales Decline: Q2 domestic same-store sales fell 7.5%, missing expectations.
2. Guidance Lowered: Full-year domestic same-store sales outlook was significantly reduced to a decline of 4% to 6%.
3. Core Consumer Pressure: Management detailed a ~9% decline in digital visit frequency in its core urban trade areas due to macroeconomic headwinds for lower-income consumers.
rows.key_quote: Digital guest visits in those [urban] trade areas and correspondingly frequency declined by approximately 9% while visits in higher-income trade areas actually grew.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Equipment Group revenue grew 18% driven by a 72% increase in mining sales and a 43% increase in Power Systems sales. 2. Booked a $1 billion order for the AVL enclosure business for delivery in 2027, increasing the total backlog to $2.9 billion. 3. Consolidated gross profit margins expanded by 270 basis points, reflecting a favorable sales mix within the Equipment Group and improved rental utilization.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. CIMCO segment operating income fell 20% due to project timing, lower package revenue, and reduced gross margins. 2. Reported Net Earnings and EPS were flat year-over-year due to a $54.3 million purchase commitment expense related to the AVL acquisition. 3. Material handling equipment sales declined 32% and orders were down 51% compared to a strong prior-year period.
rows.key_quote: Total equipment revenue increased 72% in mining, Power Systems increased 43%.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Adjusted gross margin rose 620 bps year-over-year to 33.7%, supported by productivity, mix, and a 250 bps benefit from tariff refunds. 2. Power tools organic revenue grew an impressive 8% driven by strong demand generation and brand performance. 3.
