2. Kazakhstan Legal Dispute: The company is facing a $5 billion environmental fine in Kazakhstan, with the government pursuing enforcement actions despite an international tribunal's restraining order.
3. Ongoing Losses in Chemicals: The Versalis (chemicals) division "continued to reduce losses," confirming it remains unprofitable despite some operational improvements and better market conditions.
rows.key_quote: We delivered an outstanding 8% year-on-year reported production growth...fully offsetting Middle East volume losses thanks to efficient execution of major operated projects.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Originations Growth: Total originations grew 10% YoY, with auto finance up 19% and credit card accounts up 44%, supporting 7% growth in managed receivables.
2. Improving Delinquency Trends: 30-89 day delinquencies declined 7 bps YoY, an accelerating improvement which supports the outlook for significantly lower net charge-offs in H2 2026.
3. Expanding Profitability of Newer Products: The credit card business saw YoY declines in net charge-offs (down 186 bps) and delinquencies, while marginal operating costs per account fell 25%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Lower EPS YoY: GAAP EPS fell to $1.32 from $1.40, primarily due to a higher provision expense ($610M) driven by a reserve build for strong receivables growth.
2. Higher Net Charge-Offs YoY: C&I net charge-offs were 8.2%, up 63 basis points from the prior year, reflecting the roll-through of elevated delinquencies from previous quarters.
3. Stubborn 'Back Book' Drag: Loans originated before August 2022 represent only 4% of the portfolio but account for 12% of 30+ day delinquencies, a disproportionate drag on credit metrics.
rows.key_quote: Our 30 to 89 delinquency declined 7 basis points year over year... which supports our expectation for improvement in losses over the second half.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strategic derisking progress: Exposure to lower-income customers (income < BRL 4,000/month) was reduced by 30% over 12 months. 2. Growth in secured lending: Home equity portfolio grew 40% YoY and consumer finance for new/electric vehicles increased its share of originations from 7% to 22%. 3. Customer base expansion: Client base grew 6% YoY to 76.2 million, with the new Santander Rewards program driving higher engagement.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Profitability decline: ROE fell to 12.5% and recurring net income dropped, reflecting lower revenue and higher risk costs. 2. Spread compression: NII was negatively impacted by a ~10 basis point spread reduction due to the product mix shift and a lower CDI rate. 3. Elevated provisions: Loan Loss Provisions increased, impacted by BRL 700 million in one-off items and continued stress in lower-income, agribusiness, and SME portfolios.
rows.key_quote: This shift may have short-term impact on revenue, but it is essential for building a more balanced, resilient and predictable operation.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strategic repositioning of a $2.3B securities portfolio generated a 276 basis point yield pickup, expected to significantly expand future NIM. 2. Strong underlying franchise performance with 9% annualized loan growth and 12% annualized deposit growth. 3. Proactive credit risk reduction via an $825M loan sale led to a 56% decline in special mention loans and a 31% decline in classified loans.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Reported a large net loss of $251.3 million ($1.61/share) due to strategic repositioning costs. 2. The securities sale resulted in a $256.7 million pretax loss, driving the negative quarterly result. 3. Reported Net Interest Margin (NIM) declined 11 bps quarter-over-quarter to 3.13%, impacted by nonaccrual interest reversals and funding mix changes.
rows.key_quote: The repositioning of $2.3B in securities generated a 276 basis point yield pickup, which will drive net interest margin expansion and higher recurring earnings.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised 2026 FFO guidance by $0.05/share at the midpoint to $6.99-$7.05, driven by strong leasing.
2. Leased nearly 1.8 million sq. ft. in Q2, 29% above 10-year average, driving occupancy up 100 bps sequentially to 88.4%.
3. Development pipeline progressing well, with NYC's 343 Madison reaching 50% pre-leased and a 320,000 sq. ft. redevelopment lease signed with Boston Dynamics.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Continued lackluster demand in the life science/lab space market, as startup sector capital raising remains slow.
2. West LA remains the weakest market in the portfolio from a demand recovery perspective.
3. Accelerated asset sales program is expected to have a higher dilutive FFO impact in 2026 (~$0.11/share) than previously guided.
rows.key_quote: AI continues to be enormously beneficial to BXP's leasing activity, as clients are more often expanding than contracting their space requirements.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Revenue reached $756M (+18% YoY) and EPS was $0.75 (+36% YoY), beating guidance and leading to a raised full-year revenue outlook to a record $3 billion.
2. The Advanced Computing & Communications (AC&C) sector grew 71% YoY, driven by the production ramp of significant AI-related program wins.
3. Broad-based demand with strong double-digit growth in Medical (+22% YoY) and Semi-Cap (+17% YoY), and record bookings indicating future growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Aerospace & Defense (A&D) revenue declined 12% YoY due to planned program transitions, though future outlook is positive due to strong bookings.
2. Management noted a tightening supply chain environment, with lead times extending up to 12 months for some memory and complex components.
3. Industrial sector growth was only 'modest' year-over-year after excluding a one-time benefit from a facility wind-down.
rows.key_quote: Within AC&C, revenue grew considerably at 71% year-over-year and 21% sequentially, driven by the AI-related program wins David has spoken to.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Infrastructure services revenue grew over 45% to $1.2B, with data center services revenue up nearly 30% to over $700M.
2. Core EPS increased 30% on 16% revenue growth, with every business segment growing SOP by more than 25%.
3. Full-year core EPS guidance was raised to $7.80-$7.90, and management forecast at least 15% core EPS growth for 2027.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Capital raising in Investment Management ($1.6B) was below expectations due to caution from Middle East investors.
2. Mortgage origination growth was partly offset by lower agency lending activity.
3. Share buyback activity is expected to taper off in the second half of the year.
rows.key_quote: Infrastructure services revenue reached nearly $1.2 billion... increasing by more than 45%. Within infrastructure services, data center services revenue surpassed $700 million, rising nearly 30%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Processing Performance: Soybean Processing results were higher driven by North/South America, and Softseed Processing results increased across all regions, reflecting a favorable market and strong execution. 
2. EPS Guidance Raised: Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance was increased to $9.25-$9.75 from $9.00-$9.50.
3. Viterra Integration Success: The acquisition provided critical diversification and balance, particularly with the addition of Argentine assets, with cost synergies running ahead of plan.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Grain Merchandising Weakness: The full-year outlook for the Grain Merchandising and Milling segment was lowered due to a challenging environment with ample grain supplies. 
2. Geopolitical Uncertainty: Management stressed that geopolitical tensions and conflicts are creating a complex operating environment with limited forward visibility, particularly for Q4. 
3. Higher Costs: Net interest expense rose to $154 million due to the expanded footprint from the Viterra combination, and corporate expenses also increased.
rows.key_quote: If you think about soy, adding Argentina to that really gave us the global balance that we were missing before in our soy crushing.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Revenue Guidance Raised: Full-year guidance was flipped from a mid-single-digit decrease to a mid-single-digit increase, signaling a major turnaround. 2. Growth Portfolio Acceleration: The growth portfolio generated over $1B in revenue, up 24% YoY, and now exceeds the legacy MS franchise. 3. SPINRAZA High-Dose Outperformance: Conversion to the high-dose formulation is occurring 'much faster than we expected' in all markets, driving demand and some competitive switchbacks.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. EPS Guidance Lowered: Full-year EPS guidance was reduced to $12-$13, absorbing ~$3.85 in IPR&D charges and Apellis-related costs. 2. Operating Expenses Increased: Non-GAAP core OpEx rose 20% YoY, reflecting the Apellis acquisition and increased R&D investments in phase 3 programs. 3. Gross Margin Contraction: Non-GAAP cost of sales as a percentage of revenue increased from 21% to 22% YoY due to product mix, indicating slight margin pressure.
rows.key_quote: This performance was driven by our growth portfolio, which generated over $1 billion of revenue in the quarter, up 24% year-over-year.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Guidance Boost: Expects to finish in the upper half of revenue/EBITDA guidance and at/above the high end for EPS/free cash flow. 2. Strong Sales Execution: Bookings are 'nicely ahead of plan' with strong win rates and new logo acquisition. 3. AI Innovation: Launched one 'Agentic' AI product and announced four more, which are strengthening competitive positioning and leading to customer win-backs.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Moderated Revenue Growth: Q2 organic revenue growth was 3%, a slowdown due to a large renewal cohort and tough transactional comps. 2. Back-Half Weighted Results: Performance is heavily weighted to H2, particularly Q4, relying on factors like a new platform fee. 3. Expected Retention Dip: Management guided for a 'near-term dip' in gross dollar retention due to a 40% larger renewal cohort in 2026.
rows.key_quote: We're having a great year related to win rates, just beating our internal sales quota plans in a lot of areas in the company.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Q2 results beat estimates with 7% organic revenue growth and 15% adjusted EPS growth.
2. Strong performance in core businesses, with Interventional Cardiology growing 15% and Neuromodulation growing 12%.
3. Robust long-term pipeline with seven planned launches by 2028 in markets representing a $25B+ TAM, including IVL, hypertension, and potentially TAVR.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Slashed full-year 2026 guidance, forecasting a significant slowdown in 2H 2026.
2. WATCHMAN business facing a sharp market slowdown; now expected to decline mid-to-high single digits in 2H 2026.
3. Pessimistic outlook for 2027, with management expecting 'limited adjusted EPS growth' due to continued pressures in WATCHMAN and EP.
rows.key_quote: Our guidance reduction is concentrated in WATCHMAN, where the market slowed sharply, and EP, where we did not anticipate competitive share movement.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Reinsurance organic revenue grew 5% despite significant market rate pressure of 15-20%, driven by strong new business and demand for analytics. 2. Consistent new business generation across the firm contributed 10 points to organic revenue growth, highlighting strong client demand and retention. 3. High-growth areas showed significant momentum, with Construction delivering a fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth fueled by a record data center pipeline.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. M&A services revenue was lower year-over-year, tempering overall Commercial Risk growth in the quarter. 2. Fiduciary investment income declined 12% to $58 million due to the impact of lower interest rates. 3. The company is operating in a softer pricing environment for P&C and reinsurance, which creates a headwind for market-related revenue impact.
rows.key_quote: Treaty growth from strong new business activity more than offset 15% to 20% lower rates in the reinsurance market.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong new store performance, prompting an increase in the full-year opening target to 42 stores. 2. E-commerce sales accelerated, growing over 12% and representing 16% of total sales. 3. Sprouts' private brand continued to outperform, accounting for 26% of total sales.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Comparable store sales declined 1.0%, driven by cautious consumer behavior and difficult prior-year comparisons. 2. Gross margin decreased by 12 basis points to 38.7% due to loyalty investments and elevated fuel costs. 3. Affordability initiatives yielded mixed results and failed to meaningfully drive traffic, particularly from 'lower engaged' customers.
rows.key_quote: Sales growth was driven by strong new store performance, partially offset by a 1% decline in comparable store sales.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Strong Q4 financial results with 7% revenue growth, 140 bps of adjusted EBIT margin expansion, and 17% adjusted EPS growth. 2. Record sales execution, with Employer Services new business bookings growing 6% to $2.2B for the year, driven by record-high seller productivity attributed to the AI-platform 'The Zone'. 3. Excellent client retention at 92.1% in Employer Services, supported by a third consecutive year of record-high client satisfaction scores.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. PEO segment margins contracted 100 basis points in Q4, primarily due to faster growth in zero-margin pass-through revenues and higher expenses. 2. FY2027 revenue guidance of 5-6% and EPS growth guidance of 9-11% represent a slight moderation from FY2026's actual growth rates of 7% and 11%, respectively. 3. Management is forecasting a potential 10-30 basis point decline in ES retention for FY2027, citing near-record levels and risk from out-of-business rates.
rows.key_quote: We saw a record-high seller productivity in fiscal 2026 and we believe The Zone was a key contributor.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strategic Divestiture: Agreement to watch the Life Sciences & Healthcare segment sharpens focus and increases the pro forma recurring revenue mix to ~92%.
AI Product Momentum: Launch of AI-native platforms like Web of Science Research Intelligence (77 paying customers) and development of IP-1 are positioning AI as a key future growth driver.
Earnings Growth & Margin Stability: Adjusted EPS grew 5.6% to $0.19, and adjusted EBITDA margin was maintained year-over-year despite a decline in organic revenue, demonstrating strong cost discipline.
rows.negative_highlights:
Organic Revenue Decline: Q2 organic revenues declined by $9 million, as 1.5% recurring growth was insufficient to offset a drop in transactional revenues.
Weak Transactional Performance: Transactional revenues were a significant headwind, particularly in the Life Sciences segment, and are expected to be down slightly for the full year.
Lowered FCF Outlook: Free cash flow guidance was moved to the low end of the range, impacted by ~$70M in transaction costs for the LS&H divestiture.
rows.key_quote: Organic revenues declined by $9 million as recurring growth of about 1.5% only partially offset lower transactional revenues.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. AI-Driven Revenue Surge: The Computer end market grew to 33% of revenue (up from ~10% in 2024), driven by AI-related demand for SMT, TCB, and Photonics solutions.
2. Record Bookings & Strong Growth: Q2 bookings soared 97.6% YoY to $903.6M, leading to a book-to-bill of 1.43 in H1. Q2 revenue grew 52.1% YoY.
3. Margin Expansion: Q2 adjusted gross margin increased 284 bps YoY to 42.5% due to higher volumes and a favorable product mix towards high-end AI applications.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Supply Chain Constraints: Management cited longer lead times for certain materials, extending the booking-to-billing conversion time to an estimated 6 to 9 months.
2. HBM TCB Timing Uncertainty: Shipments for memory TCB are dependent on customers' HBM4 product rollout schedules, causing some near-term ambiguity.
3. SMT Bookings Expected to Moderate: Following a record-high Q2, management expects SMT bookings to moderate sequentially in Q3 due to the high base effect.
rows.key_quote: The computer end market was the largest contributor to group revenue at approximately 33%... driven mainly by SMT solutions, TCB, and photonics applications.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Insurance Segment Strength: Revenue grew 42% year-over-year, driven by strong carrier demand in a favorable market.
2. Strong Financial Health: Net leverage improved to 1.9x from 3.0x a year ago, supported by annual free cash flow of approximately $80 million.
3. Operational Efficiency: OpEx held flat year-over-year despite 25% revenue growth, attributed to successful AI-driven initiatives and cost discipline.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. SMB Lending Underperformance: The Small Business segment experienced a significant and unexpected drop in demand, which "drove the miss" against forecasts and led to a guidance cut.
2. Margin Pressure: Segment profit margins were soft, impacted by intense competition in Insurance and a negative mix shift away from the high-margin SMB business.
3. Muted Near-Term Outlook: Full-year guidance was lowered, reflecting the expectation that SMB merchant sentiment will remain soft through the second half of the year.
rows.key_quote: In all honesty, demand came in softer than we forecast, which drove the miss. Softness was initially driven by both merchant sentiment and lender pullback.

rows.positive_highlights:
Record Q2 performance with an operating ROE of ~20% and a combined ratio of 91.2%, a 1.3 point year-over-year improvement.
Personal Lines delivered an excellent ex-CAT combined ratio of 81.9%, a 2.9 point improvement, driven by earned pricing and favorable frequency, especially a 7.4 point improvement in the Homeowners loss ratio.
Net written premium growth accelerated to 4.6%, led by Core Commercial (+7.2%) and Specialty (+4.4%), with a successful July 1 reinsurance renewal providing substantial cost reductions.
rows.negative_highlights:
The company prudently increased liability loss picks in Core Commercial for 2026, acknowledging the uncertain environment and potential for legal system abuse.
Production in the Hanover Specialty Industrial business was subdued, reflecting disciplined underwriting in the face of a softening property market.
The expense ratio was modestly elevated at 31% due to higher-than-expected variable agent compensation and employee incentives tied to the strong underwriting results.
rows.key_quote: Our current accident year loss ratio, excluding catastrophes, was 55.8%, improving from the prior year quarter driven by Personal Lines.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Adjusted EBITDA grew 9% year-on-year (net of one-offs) to €1,572 million, driven by organic growth and acquisitions like OLT and Ravenna FSRU.
2. Energy security enhanced with LNG accounting for 32% of gas imports and storage levels at 70%, significantly above the EU average.
3. Full-year net debt guidance improved to €18.9 billion from €19 billion, reflecting strong working capital management and financial discipline.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Reported adjusted net income declined 2% to €733 million, impacted by higher D&A from new assets (€45 million) and increased financial charges.
2. Geopolitical uncertainty from conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East is creating market volatility and potential price pressure.
3. Regulatory uncertainty for the 7th period remains, with potential negative changes to the WACC gearing and remuneration of work-in-progress under discussion.
rows.key_quote: adjusted EBITDA of EUR 1,572 million. That is up 9% year-on-year, driven by organic growth and larger perimeter.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. AI Initiatives Driving Revenue: AI platform 'Amanda' is delivering a 4% service revenue uplift with less experienced managers, with 99% adoption across 188 vessels.
2. Strong High-Value Service Growth: Medi-spa services revenue grew 17% year-over-year, significantly outpacing overall company growth, with plans to expand offerings to more ships.
3. Robust Operating Metrics: Pre-booked revenue increased 14%, forward bookings are up 20%, and staff retention improved 4 percentage points to 81%, enhancing center productivity.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Decelerating Product Revenue: Product revenue growth slowed, partly attributed to the faster growth of medi-spa services which have minimal retail product attachment.
2. Destination Resort Decline: Revenue from the destination resorts business decreased by $1.3 million due to the closure of hotels where the company operated spas.
3. Increased Administrative Expenses: Administrative expenses rose, notably due to a $2 million increase in third-party fees resulting from an operational reorganization in the UK and Italy.
rows.key_quote: With our AI platform, Amanda, we are seeing a 4% service revenue uplift from its context, especially with our less experienced managers.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. **Atypical Backlog Growth:** Backlog grew 14% to $956M in Q2, the first Q2 backlog growth in company history, signaling a turn in demand. 
2. **Strong Freight Market Indicators:** Spot rates rose ~40% YoY and tender rejection rates reached their highest level since 2018, supporting improved customer profitability and future demand.
3. **Visible Margin Recovery:** Management guided for a 200-300 basis point improvement in material margin for Q4, based on new orders with higher pricing already in the backlog.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. **Persistent Profitability Lag:** The company posted an adjusted EPS loss of -$0.53 and guided for a Q3 loss of ($0.50)-($0.40) as pricing continues to lag accumulated material cost inflation.
2. **Weak Current Margins:** Despite revenue beating expectations, adjusted operating margin was negative at -5.6% due to the unfavorable price/cost dynamic on orders fulfilled during the quarter.
3. **Seasonal Q4 Revenue Dip:** Management expects Q4 revenue to decline compared to Q3 due to typical seasonality, although profitability is expected to improve.
rows.key_quote: We expect Q4 material margin to improve 200-300 basis points, backed by orders already in our backlog.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong earnings growth: EBITDA up 20% to €3.2B and Net Income up 41% to €1.5B, primarily driven by regulated businesses (networks and non-mainland generation). 
2. Upgraded Guidance: Full-year net ordinary income guidance raised to exceed €2.4 billion, comfortably above the original range, due to strong H1 results and high visibility. 
3. Favorable Regulatory Framework: A new regulatory framework for networks boosted EBITDA by 24% in the segment, and a Royal Decree significantly raised the investment cap for future distribution grid expansion.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. High Ancillary Service Costs: A significant increase in ancillary services costs partially offset margin gains and is expected to have a net impact of under €100 million for the full year. 
2. Highly Competitive Retail Market: The Spanish retail market remains highly competitive, leading to a strategic reduction in customer volumes to focus on portfolio quality and profitability. 
3. Challenging Stand-alone Renewables: The economics for stand-alone solar projects are becoming more challenging due to lower capture prices and increased price cannibalization from curtailment.
rows.key_quote: Network EBITDA increased by 24%, mainly supported by the new regulatory framework enforced since the 1st of January of this year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong revenue growth: Total revenue increased 28% to $60.8B, with advertising revenue up 27% YoY.
2. AI-driven ad performance: New models generated a 15.7% uplift in conversions on Facebook, leading to a 12% increase in global price per ad.
3. Robust engagement growth: Daily Active People reached 3.6 billion; Instagram time spent grew double-digits YoY, driven by AI context improvements.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Soaring expenses and investments: Total expenses rose 55% YoY, including $3.6B in legal/severance charges. Full-year CapEx outlook is massive at $130B-$145B.
2. Declining profitability: GAAP operating income fell 8% year-over-year, and operating margin was 31%, reflecting the heavy investment cycle.
3. Significant legal risks: Management noted ongoing youth-related trials in the U.S. that "may ultimately result in a material loss."
rows.key_quote: advancements generated an 8.3% increase in ad clicks and a 15.7% uplift in conversions on Facebook.

Quad's Q2 FY2026 results were in line with expectations and full-year guidance is reaffirmed. Net sales increased versus prior year, and strong free cash flow supported returning $13 million to shareholders. The company is expanding its packaging business with a new Salt Lake City facility and growing its in-store retail media network with new retailer wins and expansions. Management continues to manage cost pressures from ink and postage, while pursuing long-term growth initiatives.

PSQH reported Q2 FY2026 revenue up 108% YoY, with non-GAAP operating income turning positive at +$400,000 versus a -$2.7M loss a year ago. The company divested EveryLife for $5.5M in cash and is affirming full-year 2026 revenue of about $32M with positive non-GAAP operating income, targeting operating cash flow positivity in 2027. Payments volume grew 153% YoY, while credit GMV grew 32% YoY. Management emphasized disciplined cost cuts and a focus on core fintech operations.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. The Phase III VANQUISH program for subcutaneous VK2735 is fully enrolled and advancing on schedule. 2. Preparations for the Phase III trial of oral VK2735 are on track for a Q4 start, positioning it to potentially be the first oral dual GLP-1/GIP agonist. 3. Results from a novel maintenance dosing study of VK2735 are expected later in the current quarter, representing a key near-term catalyst.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Net loss widened to $128.1 million ($1.10 per share) from $65.6 million ($0.58 per share) in the prior-year period. 2. R&D expenses nearly doubled to $115.8 million from $60.2 million year-over-year due to increased clinical study costs for the obesity franchise. 3. Cash and investments decreased by approximately $204 million in six months to $502 million, indicating a significant cash burn rate.
rows.key_quote: With this timing, we believe that VK2735 is positioned to become the first oral formulation of a dual GLP-1 GIP agonist to reach the market.

Q2 FY2026 sales fell to $124.4M with adjusted EBITDA of $27.6M and adjusted EPS of $0.72, both above expectations though down YoY. Branded Spirits sales ex other products rose 3% with premium plus up 5%; Ingredient Solutions grew 2%, while Distilling Solutions sales dropped 42% due to oversupply. Management guided to higher putaway in H2, raised digital A&P to 15%, and rationalized 52 brands representing 47% of SKUs.

In Q2 FY2026, GBank reported strong SBA loan production of $131.4 million, with $61.3 million retained at an average yield of 8.01%, and gain on sale income rose from $5.1 million to $9.3 million for the first six months. However, net interest margin fell to 3.78%, and provision expense increased $2.8 million due to elevated non-performing assets, including SBA hotel loans and retail credit card delinquencies. Management provided no formal guidance but noted near-term allowance levels may remain elevated while fundamental credit quality is better than reported due to SBA guarantees. The company also highlighted new gaming fintech initiatives, including a BVNKROLL partnership with AXES and a Visa Prepaid Card planned for Q4 launch.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong Bookings & Large Client Wins: Secured a double-digit number of $1 million+ ACV bookings, driven by large provider organizations consolidating vendors onto Waystar's platform. Clients with >$100k revenue grew 15% YoY.
AI & Iodine Cross-Watch Momentum: AI-powered solutions comprised ~40% of bookings. The Iodine acquisition showed early success with over $6 million in bookings from existing Waystar clients purchasing its capabilities.
Raised Guidance & Margin Strength: Raised full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance. Q2 Adjusted EBITDA margin was strong at 43%, driven by a favorable solution mix and cost discipline.
rows.negative_highlights:
Slowing Volume-Based Revenue: Volume-based revenue grew only 3% YoY, a deceleration explained by tough comps from rapid client implementations in the prior year and a normalization of patient utilization trends.
Declining Net Revenue Retention (NRR): NRR stepped down to 108%, which management noted is within the historical range but lower than recent quarters, attributed to lapping rapid client onboarding and elevated utilization rates in 2025.
Increased Investment Drag: Capitalized software spend doubled YoY to invest in AI, and combined with tax payments, reduced the unlevered free cash flow conversion ratio to 47% of adjusted EBITDA.
rows.key_quote: Large platform deployments drove strong bookings, including a double-digit number of $1 million-plus ACV bookings, reinforcing the trend toward a connected platform.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong order acceleration in Q2, driving H1 constant currency order growth of 8% (OE +10%, AM +8%).
Significant market share gains in core products, winning over 90% of competitive pump trials and increasing ESCO major digger conversions by 40% YoY.
Acquisitions performing well, with Micromine on track for >25% ARR growth and the ESEL acquisition enabling direct market access in Chile.
rows.negative_highlights:
H1 operating margin decreased 100bps to 18.8% due to unfavorable product mix and operational inefficiencies.
Production transfers caused delivery deferrals and a 70bps margin headwind from higher costs.
Free operating cash conversion was weak at 41%, driven by a significant working capital build to support H2 deliveries and delayed debtor payments.
rows.key_quote: Original equipment orders grew 10% year-on-year, supported by a high bid conversion rate on projects and over 90% success rate in pump trials.

Q2 FY2026 revenue of $157 million hit the high end of guidance, and adjusted EBITDA of $10.7 million beat the high end, driven by Arcadia's 9% YoY and 19% sequential sales growth and margin expansion to 13.6%. DynaEnergetics was flat YoY but improved sequentially with a $1.5 million tariff refund; NobelClad sales fell 17% YoY but rose 15% sequentially. Q3 guidance is $158-168 million sales and $10-13 million EBITDA, with no tariff refunds assumed. Management emphasized continued end-market headwinds and discussed the upcoming put/call option on the remaining 40% Arcadia stake.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong Revenue Diversification: Revenues from services grew 42% YoY, now accounting for 32% of total revenues, driven by insurance, investment, and financing activities.
Robust Loan & NII Growth: Loan book grew 9% YoY, putting the bank on track to exceed its €3B net credit expansion target. Full-year NII guidance was upgraded to €2B.
Superior Profitability & Efficiency: Achieved a record H1 net profit of €617M, a 16% RoTBV, and a best-in-class cost-to-income ratio of 34%.
rows.negative_highlights:
Increased Cost of Risk Guidance: Full-year cost of risk guidance was raised to ~60 basis points from a previous ~50 bps, partly due to Q2 macro adjustments and a desire to fortify the balance sheet.
Unchanged EPS Guidance: Despite significant revenue upgrades, the full-year EPS target was held at ~€0.90, citing prudence amid geopolitical uncertainty and the higher cost of risk.
Uptick in Corporate NPEs: Corporate NPE inflows rose to €89 million in Q2 from €47 million in Q1, though management attributed this to a single, manageable case.
rows.key_quote: Core revenues grew 13% year-on-year with sustainable diversification of revenue mix towards fees, which now account for 32% of total revenues.

rows.positive_highlights:
Net Interest Margin (NIM) expanded by 9 basis points to 4.01%, with 6 basis points of the improvement driven by lower funding costs.
Core EPS increased by $0.07 quarter-over-quarter to $0.44, with a strong core ROAA of 1.46% and an efficiency ratio of 52.24%.
The Board approved a new $75 million share repurchase authorization, signaling strong capital levels and management confidence.
rows.negative_highlights:
Record commercial loan payoffs of approximately $740 million muted loan growth, which was only 1.97% annualized despite strong originations.
Charge-offs remained elevated as the bank continues to resolve identified problem credits, with one commercial credit resulting in a $3.4 million charge-off.
Deposit competition is intensifying, particularly for time deposits, which is expected to pressure funding costs and limit future NIM expansion.
rows.key_quote: The net interest margin improved by 9 basis points... About 6 basis points of the 9 basis points of improvement came from lower funding costs.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record Tenable One adoption at 50% of new business, with strong uptake of the higher-priced 'Advanced' tier (2:1 ratio vs Foundation). 2. Net dollar expansion rate increased to 106%, the first sequential increase in over 4 years, driven by strong expansion and renewals. 3. All guided metrics were exceeded, and full-year guidance for revenue, EPS, and cash flow was raised, reflecting strong business momentum.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Non-GAAP gross margin declined slightly year-over-year to 81.4% from 82.0%, though it remained within the historical range. 2. Guided Q3 revenue growth of 7.6% (midpoint) represents a slight deceleration from Q2's 8.6% growth. 3. An analyst questioned why the strong business momentum wasn't translating into an even larger acceleration in the revenue guidance for the second half.
rows.key_quote: Tenable One was a record 50% of new business... larger land and expansion deals with Tenable One helped drive average deal sizes higher.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strategic Shift: Pivoting capital from MSRs to higher-yielding (low-to-mid teens ROE) investments from its private label securitization program.
Securitization Momentum: Completed 6 private label securitizations totaling $2.2B in Q2, retaining $120M of new investments, with a strong pipeline for the year.
Raised Run-Rate Outlook: Increased run-rate earnings projection to $0.33/share per quarter from $0.31, reflecting the new strategy and higher rates benefiting MSRs.
rows.negative_highlights:
Earnings Below Dividend: Q2 EPS of $0.23 and projected run-rate earnings of $0.33 are both below the $0.40 quarterly dividend.
Segment Weakness: Credit Sensitive Strategies were hurt by market-driven value declines, while Aggregation segment income fell to $11M from $16M on lower volumes.
Book Value Decline: Book value per share decreased by 1% during the quarter to $14.83.
rows.key_quote: We are pivoting from MSRs, which have faced return headwinds, to higher-yielding credit-sensitive investments from our private label securitization program.

rows.positive_highlights: 1) Subscription revenue grew 8% OCC, driven by strong price realization from new product value like AI enhancements and platform modernization. 2) Significant momentum in AI adoption, with XactAI users growing nearly 10x to 7,000 licensees and new MCP connectors launched with Anthropic's Claude. 3) Underlying adjusted EBITDA margin expanded due to cost discipline, after excluding a 120 bps prior-year FX benefit.
rows.negative_highlights: 1) Transactional revenues declined 4.2% OCC, pressured by a soft commercial property market, low weather events, and international travel disruption. 2) The soft P&C market is causing lower transactional volumes, a headwind expected to persist in the second half of the year. 3) GAAP diluted EPS declined 3% to $1.75, driven by a prior-year divestiture, higher interest expense, and a higher tax rate.
rows.key_quote: The increased value in our products from AI functionality is improving price realization and the increased engagement from our clients.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Automotive segment delivered record revenue of $1.6B, up 61% YoY, and management raised the FY26 exit run-rate outlook to $7B.
2. Total non-handset QCT revenues grew 28% YoY, demonstrating successful execution of the company's diversification strategy.
3. Management confirmed data center custom silicon wins will start generating revenue in the December quarter, a key proof point for its new growth pillar.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Apple revenue decline is accelerating, with share in the next iPhone 'materially lower' than the previously guided 20%.
2. QCT gross margins are under pressure and below historical range due to rising input costs for wafers, memory, and assembly.
3. Handset revenues are weak ($5.1B), impacted by industry contraction, with the 2027 market TAM expected to be down low teens versus 2026.
rows.key_quote: In QCT Automotive, we delivered another record quarter with revenues of $1.6 billion, with 61% year-over-year growth driven by accelerating demand.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Glo Fiber Acceleration: Achieved a record 6,200 net additions and surpassed 100,000 data customers, with 31.3% YoY customer growth.
2. Fiber Revenue Dominance: Total fiber revenue grew 21.4% YoY and now represents 51% of consolidated revenue for the first time.
3. Strong Margin Expansion: Adjusted EBITDA grew 12.9% to $32 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin increased 200 basis points to 34.3%, with a 73% incremental margin.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Incumbent Business Decline: Incumbent broadband revenue fell $2.5 million, driven by a 14.1% decline in video RGUs and lower data revenue.
2. Incumbent ARPU Pressure: Data ARPU in incumbent markets declined 2.6% YoY due to competitive pricing actions and a new rate card in rural markets.
3. Legacy RLEC Weakness: RLEC revenue declined $1 million due to a 31% drop in DSL customers and lower government support revenue.
rows.key_quote: For the first time, our fast-growing fiber businesses represented 51% of consolidated revenue... exceeding the combined revenue for our incumbent Broadband and RLEC businesses.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Integrated Care adjusted EBITDA margin increased 190 bps year-over-year to 16.5%, beating guidance.
2. BetterHelp insurance revenue annualized run rate grew to over $110 million by the end of the quarter, up from $75 million in Q1.
3. Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised slightly, and projected stock-based compensation was cut by over 35% versus 2025.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Full-year consolidated revenue guidance was cut by 5% at the midpoint, driven by a faster-than-expected decline in BetterHelp's cash-pay business.
2. A rapid consumer shift to insurance created a provider capacity bottleneck, limiting the company's ability to offset the cash-pay revenue decline.
3. The company is deprioritizing near-term international investment for BetterHelp to focus resources on solving the U.S. provider capacity issue.
rows.key_quote: Cash pay revenue declined faster than anticipated, while insurance revenue could not increase at a level sufficient to offset the cash pay decline.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Clear Aligner Performance: Record volumes of 692,000 cases (+7.4% YoY) and 8.2% revenue growth, driven by double-digit expansion in APAC, EMEA, and LatAm.
2. Margin Expansion: Non-GAAP operating margin of 22.9% exceeded expectations, up 1.6 points YoY, due to operational efficiencies and higher Clear Aligner ASPs.
3. Increased Capital Return & Activist Agreement: Announced a strategic review with Elliott Management and increased the 2026 share repurchase commitment to $400M-$500M.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Systems & Services Weakness: Revenue declined 11% YoY due to a strategic shift to lower-priced scanners and rental models; full-year guidance for the segment was lowered to a 6-8% decline.
2. North American Softness: The key North American market remains sluggish, with strength in DSOs offsetting 'slower retail demand,' indicating continued challenges.
3. Unfavorable UK VAT Ruling: An overturned court decision resulted in a ~$37.5M liability and the re-imposition of a 20% VAT on UK products, creating a headwind.
rows.key_quote: We are giving up certain economics at the point of sale to expand patient access...and increase volumes and revenues on the back end.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Wealth Solutions performance: Income grew 43% YoY to $1.1 billion, attracting $9 billion in net new money from wealth in Q2.
2. Strong CIB momentum: Global Banking income rose 18% and Global Markets flow income grew 16%, driven by network activity and technology investments.
3. Upgraded guidance & capital returns: Raised 2026 income growth guidance to the middle of the 5-7% range and announced a $1 billion share buyback.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Increased credit provisions: Took an additional $44 million management overlay related to the Middle East conflict, bringing the total overlay to $234 million.
2. Episodic income decline: Global Markets episodic income was lower compared to a very strong prior-year quarter.
3. NII pressure: Expects NII headwinds in H2 from a shift to term deposits and the impact of portfolio optimization actions, despite upgrading full-year guidance.
rows.key_quote: Wealth Solutions delivered another record quarter with income of $1.1 billion, up 43% year-on-year.

rows.positive_highlights:
Bicarbonate and electronic grade peroxides achieved record sales levels, with electronic grade growth supported by semiconductor and AI demand. 

The Coatis business showed a clear sequential improvement with better pricing in both phenol and solvent product lines. 

Delivered EUR 26 million of structural cost savings in the quarter through operational excellence initiatives, which more than offset inflation.
rows.negative_highlights:
The conflict in the Middle East had a negative impact of around EUR 20 million on Q2 EBITDA, mainly from the shutdown of the peroxide plant in Saudi Arabia. 

Soda ash business remains under significant competitive pressure in export markets with lower pricing, particularly in the seaborne market, due to Chinese overcapacity. 

Underlying EBITDA declined 20% year-over-year, driven by the volume impact from the peroxide plant shutdown and a difficult comparison against a EUR 20 million one-off gain in Q2 2025.
rows.key_quote: Around half [of the EBITDA decline] relates to the consequence of the conflict in the Middle East, mainly due to the temporary shutdown of our peroxide plant.

rows.positive_highlights:
Non-regulated business revenue grew 50% (EBITDA up 81%) driven by a strong market environment in Energy Services and Equipment segments.
Group CapEx accelerated 20% to €1.6 billion, with 92% of business plan projects now covered by contracts, fueling regulated asset base growth.
Management fully confirmed 2026 guidance, citing strong H1 results, solid execution on major projects like the Tyrrhenian Link, and high visibility for H2.
rows.negative_highlights:
Group net income growth was only 1%, suppressed by a temporary 2 percentage point increase in the IRAP tax rate, which pushed the tax rate to 31.6% from 29.8%.
Total operating costs rose 21%, significantly outpacing revenue growth of 12%, driven by perimeter consolidation and higher volumes in the non-regulated business.
Net financial expenses increased by €17 million year-over-year due to a higher average cost of debt, impacting bottom-line results.
rows.key_quote: The [regulated revenue] growth was mainly driven by higher output-based incentives, the RAB increase and recognized depreciation from new assets entered on stream.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Revenue grew 9.3% to $3.3B, driven by positive transaction growth from the 'Recipe for Growth' strategy, including the successful Chipotle Honey Chicken LTO.
2. Operational improvements via HEEP equipment are boosting throughput by 2-3 entrees in peak periods, leading to 'hundreds of basis points' in comp sales improvement.
3. Digital sales grew to 38.3% of total sales, and the revamped Rewards program drove a nearly 20% increase in daily enrollments.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Restaurant-level margin fell 220 basis points to 25.2% due to inflation in beef and freight, and higher labor, marketing, and operating costs.
2. Recent sales trends softened by ~200 basis points in late July due to heightened consumer caution and industry-wide food safety concerns, leading to a modest +1% Q3 comp guide.
3. Cost of sales increased 80 bps and labor costs increased 30 bps year-over-year, outpacing menu price increases in the quarter.
rows.key_quote: We see HEEP restaurants outperforming the enterprise by 2 to 3 entrees in their peak 15-minute period.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Accelerated synergy realization: Raised 2026 run-rate synergy target to at least $85M, ahead of the original timeline.
2. Significant margin expansion: As-reported gross margin increased 620 bps to 62%, and the full-year adjusted EBITDA margin target was raised to ~14%.
3. Recurring revenue strength: Paid subscribers grew 44% to over 1.6 million, with over 85% of total revenue now from recurring subscription streams.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Organic revenue decline: On a normalized basis (including Udemy pre-close), total revenue declined 1% year-over-year.
2. Weak enterprise retention: Enterprise Net Retention Rate (NRR) fell to 91%, reflecting a mixed demand environment and budget pressures.
3. Consumer transactional pressure: Normalized Consumer segment revenue was down 5%, driven by weakness in non-subscription offerings.
rows.key_quote: We now expect to achieve at least $85 million of annual run rate net synergies by the end of 2026.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. R&D Solutions net new bookings grew 19.3% YoY to $3.15 billion, driving a strong book-to-bill of 1.22.
2. Company-wide organic growth accelerated to 6%, three times the rate of the prior year, with both R&D and Commercial segments showing significant improvement.
3. The demand environment improved significantly, with double-digit RFP flow growth and a doubling of EBP funding versus Q2 2025.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. FX tailwind for the full year is now expected to be 80 basis points less than previously guided.
2. Margin headwinds from higher pass-throughs created an 80 basis point drag on adjusted EBITDA margin in the quarter.
3. Gross debt remains elevated at nearly $16 billion, with a net leverage ratio of 3.59x.
rows.key_quote: What these metrics point to is a consistently improving demand environment as well as improving win rates for our R&DS business.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record net long-term inflows of $45.1 billion, a nearly 9% annualized organic growth rate, driven by ETF, China JV, and private markets. 2. Significant operating leverage drove adjusted operating margin to 37.5% (up 300 bps sequentially) and adjusted EPS up 25% QoQ to $0.71. 3. Balance sheet strengthened with leverage ratio improving to 1.9x from 2.7x YoY, including over $450 million in net debt reduction in Q2.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Continued net outflows of $7.7 billion in fundamental equities, despite bright spots in specific strategies like U.S. Value. 2. Net revenue yield declined slightly to 22.4 bps from the previous quarter, with an exit rate of 22.0 bps, due to mix shift toward lower-fee products. 3. Ongoing one-time costs for hybrid platform implementation, expected to run at ~$15 million per quarter for the remainder of the year.
rows.key_quote: Net long-term inflows during the period were a record $45.1 billion... representing annualized organic growth of nearly 9%.

rows.positive_highlights: Electronics segment grew 20% organically, driven by AI infrastructure demand, with the Semiconductor division leading at 31% organic growth. Adjusted EPS increased 27% year-over-year, driving a raised full-year guidance. Adjusted EBITDA margins (ex-metals) improved 120 bps to 27.8%, driven by a favorable product mix from high-value electronics applications.
rows.negative_highlights: Management anticipates headwinds from raw material and logistics inflation in the second half. Consumer and automotive end markets remain softer, though currently offset by AI-related strength. Management acknowledged a disappointing stock reaction to the recently announced proposed merger with Solstice.
rows.key_quote: Sales in our Electronics segment grew 20% organically as activity accelerated across our supply chain in support of the ongoing AI infrastructure build-out.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Refining segment EBITDA more than doubled to $1 billion, driven by strong margins from tight supply, favorable crack spreads, and high operational throughput of 640,000 bpd. 2. Renewables segment delivered a significant turnaround with $123 million in adjusted EBITDA, compared to a $2 million loss YoY, benefiting from higher RINs prices and PTCs. 3. Strong shareholder returns, including $265 million returned in Q2 via dividends and buybacks, and a 5% increase in the quarterly dividend.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Announced plans to retire the Mississauga base oil refining assets, citing long-term economic non-viability due to location, size, and competition. 2. Guided for lower Q3 refining throughput of 590,000-620,000 bpd due to a planned turnaround at the El Dorado facility. 3. Acknowledged negative impact from volatile crude pricing, which was the largest drag on capture rate, though it was offset by strong product cracks.
rows.key_quote: principally driven by strong Refining margins and volumes in the Mid-Con and West regions as a result of steady demand, tight supply...

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Contingent Commissions: Contingents grew by an impressive $40 million, driven by minimal storm claims and higher underwriting profitability, significantly boosting results. 
2. Retail Margin Expansion: The Retail segment's EBITDAC margin expanded 230 basis points, driven by higher contingents, disciplined expense management, and acquisition synergies. 
3. Strategic AI Partnerships: Announced new partnerships with McKinsey, Accenture, and Anthropic to accelerate AI deployment and rewire key business processes for future growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Negative Organic Growth: Consolidated organic revenue decreased 0.7% (excluding contingents), primarily due to significant downward pressure on CAT property rates, which fell 15-35%. 
2. Specialty Distribution Weakness: The Specialty Distribution segment's organic revenue fell 3.5% (ex-contingents), hit by property rate headwinds and a $10 million revenue timing delay. 
3. Ongoing Litigation Impact: A previously disclosed litigation issue is now expected to have a $50 million to $60 million negative revenue impact for the full year 2026.
rows.key_quote: In property, CAT rates continue to decrease 15% to 35%... there continues to be a significant amount of capital seeking to underwrite risk.

rows.positive_highlights: Record Infrastructure adjusted EBITDA of CAD 169 million, driven by stronger utilization and the Chauvin acquisition. Marketing segment had its strongest quarter since Q2 2024, with adjusted EBITDA of CAD 15 million, capitalizing on strong crack spreads. Improved macro environment in Canada is accelerating commercial discussions for new growth projects, particularly tank storage.
rows.negative_highlights: Net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio is temporarily elevated at 4.2x following the Chauvin acquisition, above the long-term target of 3.0-3.5x. Volatility in U.S. export markets is making it difficult for customers to sign long-term contracts at the Gateway terminal. Strong refined products results were partially offset by slightly weaker than expected asphalt demand.
rows.key_quote: We saw stronger utilization across the network, contribution from our newly acquired Chauvin asset, and the continued benefits from optimization initiatives.

rows.positive_highlights: System-wide RevPAR grew 3.9%, driven by a 5.7% increase in Business Transient RevPAR from strong small- to medium-sized business demand. Development pipeline reached a record 541,000 rooms after the second-largest signings quarter in company history (43,000 rooms). Full-year guidance was raised for both RevPAR (to 3.0-3.5%) and adjusted EPS (to $8.89-$9.01).
rows.negative_highlights: Middle East and Africa RevPAR decreased approximately 30% year-over-year due to regional conflict. RevPAR in China declined 2.2% due to government restrictions on group travel. Adjusted EBITDA was negatively impacted by $20-$25 million from significant renovations at three major owned hotels.
rows.key_quote: Business transient RevPAR was up 5.7%, a three-point step up globally...driven by midweek demand from small- to medium-sized businesses.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Revenue grew 6.9% YoY to $216.8M, beating guidance due to improving demand and market share gains.
2. Strong Q3 guidance with revenue growth accelerating to 10% YoY and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to ~20%.
3. Significant progress in new product development for AI/data centers, with positive customer feedback on microchannel coolers and high-frequency circuit materials.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Q2 Adjusted EPS of $0.92 was below the midpoint of guidance.
2. The EPS miss was driven by a >$0.10 impact from supply chain headwinds, a onetime facility event (fire), and higher operating expenses.
3. Q3 gross margin improvement is being partially offset by the underutilization during the ramp of its new China factory and increased commodity costs.
rows.key_quote: The stronger top line reflects both improving demand and share gains.

rows.positive_highlights: UHDMS project is 45% complete with the main tie-in on track, derisking long-term production. The new 'Full Potential' operational excellence program was launched to drive cost efficiencies. Collaboration with Transnet led to a successful maintenance shutdown, replacing 101km of rail to improve logistics reliability.
rows.negative_highlights: EBITDA fell 30%, with over 90% of the ZAR 5.1 billion impact attributed to external factors like a stronger rand and input cost inflation. Production decreased by 3% due to record-breaking rainfall and flooding at operations. The company's breakeven price has risen significantly from $68 to $81 per tonne, increasing sensitivity to price fluctuations.
rows.key_quote: External factors reduced EBITDA by 30%, accounting for more than 90% of the total ZAR 5.1 billion impact.

rows.positive_highlights:
- Investment Bank outperformance: Equities income surged 44% driven by derivatives and prime financing, while advisory fee growth hit 51%.
- Enhanced shareholder returns: Announced a £1 billion share buyback and an £800 million dividend, resulting in H1 distributions increasing 61% YoY to £2.3 billion.
- Raised 2026 guidance: Full-year income target was upgraded to circa £31.5 billion (from £30bn), with high confidence in delivering RoTE >12%.
rows.negative_highlights:
- U.K. product margin pressure: Barclays U.K. faced headwinds from a competitive ISA season and maturing higher-margin mortgages, although this is expected to improve in H2.
- Increased near-term costs: Announced up to £500M in additional structural cost actions for H2 2026 to drive future efficiencies, which will increase a short-term cost base.
- U.S. non-NII headwinds: Higher benchmark interest rates compressed margins on originate-to-watch loans in the U.S. Consumer Bank, pressuring non-NII.
rows.key_quote: Equities income was up 44%, driven by equity derivatives and prime financing, both focus areas whilst [...] was stable versus a strong comparator.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. ORV market share gain for the 5th consecutive quarter, driven by over 10% retail growth in utility products like Ranger.
2. Strong growth in the commercial business, fueled by demand from infrastructure and data center construction projects.
3. Operational adjusted gross margin expanded 82 bps and EBITDA margin expanded 180 bps due to volume, mix, and efficiencies, overcoming commodity headwinds.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. The recreational vehicle segment remains soft and the outlook is pressured due to cautious consumer spending, inflation, and high interest rates.
2. Marine pontoon retail was down high-single digits, with weakness in mid and lower-tier segments.
3. The company faces a $70 million headwind for the year from increased commodity costs, primarily steel and aluminum.
rows.key_quote: Ranger and commercial shipments were significantly above last year's levels supported by continued strength in utility demand across a range of categories.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Announced definitive agreement to acquire Taco Group for $1.4B, establishing a new growth platform in attractive commercial markets like HVAC and data centers.
2. Flow and Water Solutions segments delivered record return on sales (ROS), with Flow sales up 5% and Water Solutions segment income up 17%.
3. Reaffirmed full-year adjusted EPS guidance and achieved 50th consecutive year of dividend increases, maintaining its 'Dividend King' status.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Pool segment sales plunged 42% YoY, primarily driven by a massive $170 million channel inventory destocking.
2. Full-year sales guidance was lowered to be down 4-7%, with the Pool segment now forecast to decline 18-22%.
3. Management acknowledged losing aftermarket share and operational disruption from its 80/20 strategy implementation, which negatively impacted relationships with smaller dealers.
rows.key_quote: The reduction in sales and income was mainly driven by the $170 million channel inventory destocking in the quarter.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Major Marketplace Turnaround: Full-year pretax margin guidance was raised to 4.5%-5% from 3% after risk adjustment data confirmed a favorable acuity mix and the company received a $180M favorable 2025 reconciliation.
2. Substantial EPS Guidance Increase: Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance was lifted by over 40% at the midpoint, from >$3.40 to >$4.80.
3. Medicare PDP Strength & Favorable Medicaid Rates: The Medicare PDP full-year pretax margin outlook increased from 2% to over 3%, and the Medicaid full-year composite rate forecast improved from 4.5% to 5%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Accelerated Medicaid Attrition: Medicaid membership is now expected to decline 8-9% for the year, worse than the 6% previously forecast, bringing potential for negative acuity shifts.
2. Significant Non-Recurring Gains: Management noted ~$0.50 of Q2 EPS was from one-time prior-period settlements ($180M from Marketplace and $160M from Medicare) that will not recur.
3. Expected Second-Half Slowdown: The company guided for a breakeven Q3 and a net loss in Q4 due to normal business seasonality, despite the very strong first-half performance.
rows.key_quote: A thorough analysis of the June Wakely report confirmed our hypothesis about the relative acuity of our population, allowing us to revise our Marketplace outlook.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Massive Revenue Growth & Guidance Raise: Revenue surged 166% YoY to a record $1.065B, prompting a full-year revenue guidance raise to $3.9B-$4.2B (100% YoY growth at midpoint).
2. Accelerating AI Data Center Demand: The company has become a 'standard' for on-site power for AI in under a year, with all major US hyperscalers validating its solution due to its critical 'time to power' advantage.
3. Soaring Profitability & Strategic Financing: Operating margin expanded to 22.5% (+1536 bps YoY) due to strong operating leverage, and the strategic financing partnership with Brookfield was increased fivefold to $25 billion.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Revenue Concentration: Management acknowledged that quarterly revenue can appear concentrated to one or two customers due to the lumpy nature of large campus deliveries.
2. Inherent Execution Risk: The guidance relies on converting 'in-year bookings' to meet aggressive targets, implying significant execution risk to maintain the 'breakneck speed' of expansion.
3. Pulled Free Cash Flow Guidance: The company stopped providing a specific free cash flow target, explaining it as a reporting change, which reduces a layer of formal accountability on cash generation.
rows.key_quote: The proven success of our technology, coupled with an increasingly urgent need for power, has collapsed the time from first engagement to first order.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to at least SEK 900M from SEK 870M, driven by strong organic performance and the Overamstel acquisition. 2. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 19.2% from 16.8% year-over-year, and group gross margin increased to 46.3% from 45.3%. 3. The Publishing segment was a standout, with sales growing 32% in constant currencies and its EBITDA margin expanding significantly to 31.3% from 27.4%.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Subscriber net adds slowed to 11,000 in Q2, a decline from a strong Q1, attributed to campaign timing, though an H2 acceleration is expected. 2. ARPU in the Americas segment fell to SEK 129 from SEK 138 YoY, impacted by FX and a mix shift towards lower-priced LATAM markets. 3. Europe segment's gross margin saw a slight contraction due to mix changes towards faster-growing but lower-margin markets.
rows.key_quote: On the back of this solid organic performance and the acquisition of Overamstel, we are raising our 2026 full year guidance for adjusted EBITDA.

rows.positive_highlights: Recognized an unexpected $100 million net benefit from the Florida DPP program, boosting reported Q2 EBITDA. Acute care same-facility adjusted admissions rebounded, increasing 2.9% year-over-year. Accelerated share repurchase program to $320 million in Q2, signaling management's confidence in the discounted stock valuation.
rows.negative_highlights: Lowered full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance by ~$50M due to ~$200M in adverse items. Increased the full-year professional and general liability expense estimate by $50M due to higher claim severity. A Texas behavioral facility is facing recertification issues, resulting in an expected $50M negative earnings impact for the year.
rows.key_quote: Excluding the $100M Florida DPP benefit, our Q2 EBITDA fell short of expectations, primarily due to higher liability reserves and facility specific issues.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record volume performance: Underlying sales grew 5.8% in Q2, driven by 5.5% volume growth, the best quarterly volume result since 2010.
2. Power Brands outperformance: Grew 6.9% in Q2 with 6.8% from volume, significantly outpacing the group average and representing 78% of turnover.
3. Strong emerging markets momentum: Sales grew 8.3% in Q2 (7.4% from volume), led by India (+10%) and a strong recovery in Latin America (+8.9%).
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Gross margin pressure: H1 gross margin declined 70 basis points year-over-year due to commodity inflation headwinds.
2. US Foods underperformance: Condiments business in the U.S. lost market share due to increased competition in premium segments like avocado oil mayonnaise.
3. Subdued European results: Sales in Europe declined by 0.5% in H1 amid a softer market environment.
rows.key_quote: Our power brands... continue to outperform, delivering underlying sales growth in the second quarter of 6.9%, with 6.8% coming from volume.

rows.positive_highlights:
1) Double-digit EBITDA growth and margin expansion: EBITDA grew 10.9% YoY, with the margin expanding 1.3 percentage points to 41.8% due to disciplined cost management.
2) Strong fiber and postpaid mobile growth: Fiber connections grew 11.3% YoY to 8.2 million, and postpaid mobile accesses increased 6.9% YoY, driven by the success of the convergent 'Vivo Total' offer which grew 29.4%.
3) Robust revenue growth and monetization: Total revenue increased 7.6% YoY, with handset and electronics sales soaring 27.8%, and mobile ARPU reaching a new high.
rows.negative_highlights:
1) Gross margin pressure from hardware sales: Cost of goods sold rose 10.2%, outpacing revenue growth of 7.6%, primarily due to the strong performance in lower-margin handset sales.
2) Aggressive competition in specific segments: Management noted the competitive environment remains aggressive in some markets and that the prepaid segment, in particular, "could be more rational" on pricing.
3) H2 dependency for asset sales target: The company still needs to generate BRL 3.85 billion from copper and real estate sales to meet its BRL 4.5 billion goal, implying a significant acceleration is required in the second half.
rows.key_quote: Convergence was the key driver of this performance. Vivo Total reached 3.8 million customers, up 29.4% compared to last year.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. **Strong Margin Expansion & Profitability:** Adjusted EBITDA margin grew 150 bps to 23.3% driven by productivity, price, and mix, leading to a record EPS of $1.46 (+16% YoY).
2. **AI & Industrial Momentum:** Data center orders surged over 300% in Applied Water, with expected full-year data center revenue growth of ~200%. WSS secured a landmark 23-year contract with Dow.
3. **Healthy Demand & Backlog:** Ending backlog stood at $5.3 billion with a book-to-bill ratio "well above 1," supported by 41% orders growth in Water Solutions and Services (WSS).
rows.negative_highlights:
1. **Significant China Decline:** Revenue in China fell 27% due to economic headwinds and intentional 80/20 business walkaways.
2. **Measurement & Control Solutions (MCS) Weakness:** MCS revenue declined 1% and margins contracted 200 bps due to electric meter project delays, leading to a reduction in full-year revenue guidance.
3. **Flat Top-Line Growth:** Overall revenue grew only 1%, constrained by the China decline and a nearly 2% headwind from purposeful walkaway revenue.
rows.key_quote: The improvement was driven by productivity, price, and mix more than offsetting inflation and lower volume.

rows.positive_highlights:
Tekion Progress: Rollout is 70% complete; mature markets show strong productivity gains like a 10% increase in dollars per technician.
Capital Allocation: Repurchased 7% of shares YTD, prioritizing buybacks over M&A due to attractive valuation.
Used Vehicle Strategy: Used retail PVR increased 5% sequentially, with a strategic shift to drive more volume in H2 2026.
rows.negative_highlights:
Operational Disruption: The Tekion transition caused flat customer pay business and a slight decline in overall parts and service gross profit.
New Vehicle Weakness: Same-store new vehicle units declined 6%, hurt by transition effects and a 28% drop in the Stellantis portfolio.
Elevated Costs: Same-store adjusted SG&A-to-gross profit was 65.3%, reflecting duplicate DMS costs and inefficiencies during the tech rollout.
rows.key_quote: In June, stores on Tekion the longest grew units per salesperson by 12% and increased dollars per technician by 10%.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Booming Electronics division: Sales growth accelerated to +10% in Q2 (+8% normalized), and H1 project decisions reached over EUR 1 billion (1.5x all of 2025), driven by demand for AI. 
2. Strong Margin Expansion: Operating margin increased by 110 basis points (ex-energy) in H1, driven by record efficiencies of EUR 299 million and strong Industrial Merchant pricing of +5.2% in Q2. 
3. Record Future Growth Pipeline: Investment backlog reached an unprecedented EUR 6 billion, supported by a record EUR 2.9 billion in H1 investment decisions, providing high visibility on future growth.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Global Helium Shortage: The shortage created a "low single-digit" volume headwind for the Industrial Merchant business in the Americas and Europe. 
2. Weakness in Large Industries (ex-US): Demand in Large Industries remained low in EMEA and the Middle East, offsetting record-high volumes in the U.S. 
3. Currency Headwinds: Reported sales were negatively impacted by a -3.6% currency effect in H1, partially obscuring underlying growth.
rows.key_quote: The momentum is supported by a diverse mix of projects and geographies, almost all driven by artificial intelligence needs.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Successful FIFA World Cup Activation: Drove Trademark Coca-Cola volume up 5% (strongest growth in 17 years) and Powerade volume up 8%.
2. Strong Financial Performance: Delivered 6% organic revenue growth and 11% comparable EPS growth, exceeding expectations.
3. Margin Expansion & Raised Guidance: Expanded comparable gross margin by 120 bps and raised full-year comparable EPS growth guidance to 9-10%.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Uneven Consumer Environment: Management cited a globally uneven consumer backdrop with inflationary pressures and economic challenges in several markets.
2. Regional Profit Pressure: Profit declined in EMEA due to investment timing and in Asia Pacific due to strategic investments in affordability to grow the consumer base.
3. Second-Half Headwinds: The company faces tougher comparisons and six fewer days in Q4, which will moderate full-year growth metrics from the strong H1 pace.
rows.key_quote: Activating around the FIFA World Cup contributed to Trademark Coca-Cola volume growth of 5% for the quarter, its strongest volume growth in 17 years.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Semicon division delivered accelerated organic growth of 16% in Q2, driven by AI adoption, with management guiding for a similar growth rate in H2. 2. Industry segment outperformed the market with 6.4% H1 organic growth and a strong 18.6% EBITDA margin, driven by aerospace, defense, and power generation. 3. Portfolio rebalancing proved highly effective, with acquisitions contributing over 18% EBITDA margin versus ~8% for divested companies, boosting overall profitability.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Building segment performance was mixed, with weakness in French, UK, and Eastern European residential markets weighing on results. 2. A complete halt in shipments to the Middle East during Q2 negatively impacted the building division's revenue and inventory levels. 3. Organic EBITDA drop-through was weaker than expected, suppressed by lower profitability in the building segment and a EUR 3 million increase in holding costs.
rows.key_quote: So great dynamic overall, all driven by AI adoption in more and more applications.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Raised Full-Year Guidance: Sales forecast increased to JPY 743B and OP to JPY 156.5B, driven by a record level of orders.
2. Strong Market Outlook: Management expects ~20% WFE market growth in both CY2026 and CY2027, fueled by AI-driven investments.
3. Surging Demand: The company is experiencing a 'record high level of inquiry and order', with management stating demand is currently stronger than production capacity.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Weak Q1 Results: Sales declined 10.3% and operating profit fell 41.1% year-over-year, mainly due to a large project's revenue recognition being delayed to Q2.
2. Sharp Margin Contraction: Consolidated operating margin fell significantly to 11.8% from approximately 18% a year ago, driven by lower sales volume and utilization in the core SPE segment.
3. FT Segment Downgrade: The full-year sales forecast for the Finetech Solutions (FT) segment was reduced from JPY 47B to JPY 43B.
rows.key_quote: Mainly with AI investment, we witnessed a very strong demand, leading to a record high level of inquiry and orders.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Record Performance & Cost Control: Set records for Adj. EBITDA ($305M, +5% YoY) and Adj. EPS ($0.72, +13% YoY), driven by disciplined cost execution leading to 8 consecutive quarters of lower operating expenses.
2. Refinish Growth & Wins: Refinish sales grew 6% as channel destocking abated. Secured over 2,700 new net bodyshops year-to-date, including a major 800-location MSO win in North America.
3. Mobility & Commercial Vehicle Strength: Mobility hit record net sales, driven by Commercial Vehicle sales growth of 7% YoY due to improving North American Class 8 truck production and growth in commercial transportation solutions.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Maintained Guidance Despite Beat: Despite record Q2 results, full-year guidance was only maintained, citing prudence due to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and related uncertainty.
2. Industrial Weakness in North America: Industrial volumes were down 1% overall, with the company citing 'choppy and challenged' market conditions in North America tied to weak construction and consumer confidence.
3. Light Vehicle Decline: Light Vehicle net sales declined slightly, and overall Mobility volumes were soft, offsetting price/mix gains due to weakness in specific customer platforms in North America and China.
rows.key_quote: Refinish net sales increased 6%... driven primarily by the abatement of destocking this quarter and favorable price mix.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Enterprise segment momentum fueled by DEX turnaround, with total Enterprise ARR growing 8% YoY (constant currency) and highest-value customers (€200k+ ARR) growing 11%.
2. Announced a landmark multiyear strategic partnership with ServiceNow to integrate TeamViewer's technology, significantly expanding market access and validating its platform strategy.
3. Rapid AI adoption with AI-powered support sessions growing from 300,000 in March to over 500,000 in June, strengthening the data foundation for its autonomous endpoint management vision.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Consolidated revenue declined 1.4% YoY in constant currency to €183 million, reflecting lagging headwinds from prior strategic initiatives.
2. The SMB segment remains under pressure with ARR down 4% YoY (constant currency), acting as a drag on overall growth.
3. Free cash flow was negatively impacted by fewer customers opting for upfront payments on multiyear deals, which management attributed to a more cautious macro environment.
rows.key_quote: Total enterprise ARR grew plus 8% year-over-year in constant currency, supported by improving customer engagement, expansion activity and the recovery of the DEX business.

rows.positive_highlights:
Strong performance in Americas and Europe/Africa: Americas saw 13% organic revenue growth and 50bps operating margin expansion to 6.5%; Europe/Africa had 7% organic revenue growth and 20bps margin expansion to 5.1%.
Growth from Chinese OEMs: Volumes from Chinese OEM partners increased by approximately 40%, now representing 25% of the Group's total volumes, driving performance in the Americas and Europe.
Strong capital returns and cash flow: Share buyback program increased by £75M to £250M, supported by strong free cash flow conversion of 112% on a last-twelve-months basis.
rows.negative_highlights:
Significant underperformance in APAC: The region saw a 16% volume decline and a 290 basis point collapse in operating margin to 3.5%, primarily due to weakness in Australia from supply issues and a rapid consumer shift to NEVs.
Major restructuring charges: Incurred £64 million in adjusting items, including a £28 million write-down for exiting 13 dilutive distribution contracts and £22 million for headcount/site reductions, mainly in APAC.
Profitability and margin pressure at group level: Consolidated adjusted operating margin declined 40 basis points to 5.3%, adjusted PBT fell 10% in constant currency, and adjusted EPS was flat year-over-year.
rows.key_quote: In Australia... in January, EV penetration was just over 8%. In June, it was nearly 25%.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Group returned to comparable growth in Q2, up 2%, representing a 2-point sequential improvement driven by better trends across most activities. 2. Gucci showed significant turnaround signals with its revenue decline narrowing to 2% (a 6-point sequential improvement) and its leather goods category returning to growth. 3. Strong financial discipline resulted in a 5% drop in H1 OpEx, a €4.7B reduction in net debt, and puts the company on track for a €1B inventory reduction.
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Management guided for a 'flattish' Q3 for the group, citing a more difficult comparison base and timing of new product campaigns. 2. Mainland China, a key strategic market, remains a soft spot with performance still down despite gradual quarter-on-quarter improvement. 3. Balenciaga faced a challenging quarter in retail as the house works through a creative transition and rebalances its product offering.
rows.key_quote: Gucci retail improving by 7 points sequentially in Q2 and all regions showing better trends.

rows.positive_highlights: 1. Record IP Optical bookings with a book-to-bill of 1.6x, increasing backlog over 60% year-to-date. 2. Strategic partnership with Salesforce to provide voice capabilities for its AI-powered Agentforce contact center. 3. Strong sequential growth in optical solutions (up 70%) and defense-related revenue (up 60% Y/Y and sequentially).
rows.negative_highlights: 1. Lowered full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance due to slower project ramps. 2. Cloud & Edge revenue down 19% year-over-year, primarily due to lower sales to Verizon. 3. Consolidated gross margin fell 280 bps year-over-year to 49.3%, with full-year margin guidance also reduced.
rows.key_quote: Voice network modernization deployments with U.S. Tier 1 service providers have improved, but more slowly than we expected, moderating our second half growth rate.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Q3 Guidance: Revenue guided to $3.75B (+21% YoY adj.) and EPS to $4.11, with gross margins expanding to 58.5%.
2. Accelerating Growth Drivers: Company-specific growth areas (Automotive, Industrial, Data Center) grew mid-20% and now represent 1/3 of total revenue.
3. Physical AI Momentum: The design-win funnel for its AI processors grew over 50% in the quarter to $1.5B, indicating a major future growth vector.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Mobile Weakness: Mobile segment guided to be down mid-single-digits year-over-year in Q3.
2. External Supply Constraints: Management noted customers are facing memory constraints that require design workarounds.
3. Inflationary Cost Pressures: Acknowledged rising input costs are requiring selective price increases to be passed on to customers.
rows.key_quote: Our company-specific growth drivers grew in the mid-20% range year-over-year, and represented roughly 1/3 of second quarter revenue.

rows.positive_highlights:
1. Strong Rate Momentum: Truck revenue per load surged 17% YoY, with the 14.4% sequential increase being the largest in 15 years. 
2. Market Cycle Turn: Management confirmed market conditions have 'begun shifting rather rapidly in favor of the transportation provider' after a multi-year downturn. 
3. Heavy Haul Growth: Heavy haul revenue grew 18% YoY, driven by a 9% increase in volume and an 8% increase in rates, supported by data center and an industrial demand.
rows.negative_highlights:
1. Elevated Insurance & Claims Costs: The company recorded $10.5 million in net unfavorable adjustments to prior year claims estimates, a significant increase from $2.3 million the prior year. 
2. Heightened Litigation Risk: Extensive discussion centered on the post-Montgomery court ruling environment, which increases litigation costs and liability risk for brokers. 
3. Variable Margin Compression: Variable contribution margin compressed to 13.9% from 14.1% YoY, primarily due to higher rates paid to truck brokerage carriers in a tightening market.
rows.key_quote: Market conditions... have begun shifting rather rapidly in favor of the transportation provider.

rows.positive_highlights:
